blocks.text: Two independent concerns are at work: whether the container is still open (`open → closing → terminal`, driven by `close()` and `dispose()`), and releasing the resources themselves. `close()` is always synchronous and idempotent and never calls your code; `dispose()` is always asynchronous.

sections.heading: IReleaseDescriptor: how a resource is released

blocks.code:
type IReleaseDescriptor = {
  readonly syncSafe?: boolean
  readonly order?: number
  readonly graceful?: (context: IReleaseContext) => void | PromiseLike<void>
  readonly gracefulTimeoutMs?: number
  readonly force: (context: IReleaseContext) => void | PromiseLike<void>
  readonly gcFallback?: boolean
  readonly custom?: (context: IReleaseContext) => void | PromiseLike<void>
}

blocks.text: Fields:

items: `syncSafe?: boolean`: declares that `SyncLifecycleScope` may accept this descriptor. It does not change the static type of `LifecycleScope`; whether a scope is sync or async depends on which factory created it, never on descriptor content.
`order?: number`: release ordering key, `0` when omitted. It only applies in a `DisposeTransaction` running in `order` mode, where larger values are released first.

`graceful?`: a gentle release. When it times out, the scope stops waiting for it (without cancelling it) and moves on to `force`. If `graceful` throws (as opposed to timing out), `force` still runs. A `graceful` that returns synchronously counts as a completed release: even if it overran its budget, `force` does not run, and one `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` diagnostic goes to `context.report`.
`gracefulTimeoutMs?: number`: the graceful phase's own budget, further capped by the transaction's shared absolute `deadlineAt` (the smaller wins).
`force: (context) => void | PromiseLike<void>` (required): must complete unconditionally and must not depend on any precondition.

`gcFallback?: boolean`: an async scope may register a best-effort `FinalizationRegistry` fallback, which explicit release (`dispose()` or `release()`) unregisters. A live scope holds strong references to its resources, so this never collects one resource while its scope is reachable; it only helps when the whole owner is forgotten and never replaces explicit disposal. A sync scope accepts the field but registers no finalizer.
`custom?`: an escape hatch. When present it takes over the release completely and `graceful`/`force` are ignored.

blocks.text: `IReleaseContext` (the first argument of every callback): `signal: IAbortSignal` (aborts when the container starts closing), `deadlineAt: number | undefined`, `scheduler?: IScheduler` (the clock that produced `deadlineAt`; `systemScheduler` by default), `report(error: unknown): void` (a diagnostic channel; its own throws and rejections go to the shared host error queue from `@migaia/utils`), and `disposer?: IDisposerContext`. Only callbacks driven by a `LifecycleScope` receive `disposer.join()`. That explicit "wait for my own owner" operation throws `SCOPE_REENTRANT_DISPOSE` immediately, whether called synchronously or after any await, microtask, Promise chain, nested helper or timer, and never returns the outer disposal Promise. A generic `createDisposeTransaction()` without a scope owner does not fake this capability. Do not capture the scope and call `scope.dispose()` inside a disposer to get around it.

blocks.code:
function createLifecycleScope(options?: ILifecycleScopeOptions): ILifecycleScope

type ILifecycleScopeOptions = {
  readonly errorPolicy?: 'throw' | 'collect' | 'report' | 'firstError' // default 'throw'
  readonly report?: (error: unknown) => void
  readonly deadlineAt?: number
  readonly scheduler?: IScheduler // default systemScheduler
}

type ILifecycleScope = ILifecycleOwner & {
  readonly lifecycle: 'open' | 'closing' | 'terminal'
  own<T>(resource: T, descriptor: IReleaseDescriptor): T
  release(resource: unknown): boolean
  close(): void
  dispose(): Promise<readonly ICollectedError[]>
  [Symbol.asyncDispose](): Promise<void> // await using; discards the collected errors
}

blocks.text: The general-purpose async ownership container:
Edge cases:

items: `own(resource, descriptor)`: throws `SCOPE_CLOSED` / `SCOPE_TERMINAL` when the container is `closing` / `terminal`, and `SCOPE_REENTRANT_OWN` when called from inside one of its own disposers. An invalid descriptor shape (`order`, `custom`, `graceful`, `gracefulTimeoutMs`, `force`, checked by the same rules as at dispose time) throws `INVALID_OPTION` at registration; an accessor that throws is rethrown unchanged.

`release(resource)`: unregisters a resource without releasing it (the caller already released it) and returns whether an entry was found and removed. If the entry used `gcFallback`, its `FinalizationRegistry` entry is unregistered too.
`close()`: synchronous and idempotent; `open → closing`.

`dispose()`: releases every registered resource in reverse (LIFO) order. Concurrent calls share one Promise. To express "wait for my own owner" inside a disposer, use `context.disposer.join()`, which throws `SCOPE_REENTRANT_DISPOSE` without disturbing the shared Promise. Once the container is `terminal`, `dispose()` still returns the first dispose Promise with its original result or rejection. With `errorPolicy: 'collect'` the result is the collected `ICollectedError[]`; the other three policies throw or report internally and return an empty array.
`[Symbol.asyncDispose](): Promise<void>` makes the scope usable with `await using` (TypeScript needs the `ESNext.Disposable` lib).

blocks.text: A purely synchronous container:

blocks.code:
const scope = createSyncLifecycleScope()
scope.own(node, { syncSafe: true, force: () => node.detach() })
scope.close()
const failures = scope.dispose() // returns synchronously

blocks.text: Rules and edge cases:

items: Every descriptor must state `syncSafe: true`; otherwise `own()` throws `SCOPE_SYNC_VIOLATION` at registration, not at release.
Descriptor shape checks match the async version: an `order` that is not a finite number, a missing `force` and similar mistakes throw `INVALID_OPTION` from `own()`.
A `LifecycleScope` or `ProvisionalScope` instance cannot be owned (detected by an internal brand); trying throws `SCOPE_SYNC_VIOLATION`.

A callback (`custom`, `graceful` or `force`) that returns a thenable is detected synchronously at release and reported as `SCOPE_SYNC_VIOLATION`. A violating `graceful` still falls through to `force`; a violating `force` or `custom` counts as that item's failure under the current error policy.
The fallback chain matches the async version (`custom`, otherwise `graceful` then `force`) but without timeouts, since there is nothing to wait for.
`release()` and `close()` behave as in the async version. `dispose()` is idempotent and returns `[]` on later calls; calling it from inside a disposer throws `SCOPE_REENTRANT_DISPOSE`.
`[Symbol.dispose](): void` makes the scope usable with `using` (TypeScript needs the `ESNext.Disposable` lib).

blocks.text: Runs one descriptor's full fallback chain (`custom`, otherwise `graceful` with its timeout race, then `force`) without a full transaction. Useful in tests and custom orchestration:

Both arguments are required and `context` has no optional fields: build the complete object. Failures while admitting or running the descriptor end up in the returned array (empty on success). A context that cannot be admitted (a throwing getter, an invalid deadline) rejects the Promise. A `graceful` timeout sends a diagnostic to `context.report` (`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, or a note that it fell through to `force`). A failing `force` additionally reports an error labelled `RELEASE_FORCE_FAILED`, while the original error still goes into the returned array unchanged.
Coordinates the release of several resources, either by priority (`order`) or in an exact sequence (`plan`). One transaction uses one mode:
Edge cases:

items: `{ kind: 'order' }`: groups items by `descriptor.order` (default `0`) and releases larger values first; the sort is stable, so items with the same value keep the order you gave. `order` is read only in this mode.
`{ kind: 'plan' }`: runs `items` exactly in the given order and never reads `order`.

`signal?`: forwarded into every item's `context.signal`. When `run()` starts, the transaction mirrors the abort state of the signal you passed; without one, items receive a lazily created signal that never aborts.
`deadlineAt` / `scheduler`: shared by every item in one `run()`, not recomputed per item.
`pending?`: after every item is released, `pending.drain()` is awaited once so that work started by the releases can finish (typically a `createPendingTracker()`).

Descriptor checks (types and accessors of `order`, `custom`, `graceful`, `gracefulTimeoutMs`, `force`) are made per item. One item's invalid descriptor (coded `INVALID_OPTION`) does not stop the others; it counts as that item's failure under the error policy.

`errorPolicy` behaves like `createErrorCollector`. Under `throw`, a single failure keeps its native instance and an unclassified error gets `SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED` attached; a primitive is wrapped with the original on `cause`; an error that already has a valid source and code keeps it. Several failures become an `AggregateError` coded `SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED`.

blocks.text: `mergeCleanupResults(values)` accepts an array of cleanup results (or PromiseLikes of them), waits for each result's `physicalCompletion` chain and returns a frozen `{ cleanupErrors }`. Errors are merged in input order and, within each input, in the order they were observed now or later. A rejected source Promise is kept as its original error, and no other branch is dropped. It does not rely on realm-local `instanceof Promise`, so Promises from other realms and plain thenables both work.

`ICleanupResult<TError>` is the shared boundary between lifecycle, PluginHost and Tray: the current `cleanupErrors` and the later `physicalCompletion` never contain the same error twice. Domain flags such as logical terminal, ok or cleanupComplete stay with each caller. Do not put the full error list into the physical continuation, or errors are counted twice.

For containers whose `dispose()` must start every disposer synchronously but whose cleanup may finish asynchronously. The ledger is the single source of truth for what is pending, the raw errors and when everything has ended. The caller still decides the order, clears its own registry and turns raw errors into its own throw/report/aggregate contract.
State and identity:

items: It starts `open`; `start()` does not change the state.

The first `seal()` moves to `closing` synchronously, freezes every error observed so far and returns the single outcome. Later `seal()` calls return the same object, and `outcome.physicalCompletion` stays the same Promise.

Once sealed with `pending === 0` it becomes `terminal`; otherwise it becomes `terminal` after the last thenable settles. `whenTerminal()` only waits for that; it does not promise a stable Promise identity.
A valid thenable that never settles keeps the ledger `closing`. The ledger adds no timeout, abort, retry or forced terminal state of its own.

blocks.text: Callbacks and thenables:

items: `start()` first checks that `source` is a string and `callback` a function; invalid input throws `INVALID_OPTION` synchronously without calling the callback.

A callback that throws synchronously, or whose result's `.then` getter throws, is recorded in the error snapshot taken at `seal()`. `start()` does not rethrow item failures, so later items can still be started.
A thenable's `.then` is read once and called with the original thenable as receiver; the first settlement wins. Rejections enter the final ledger in the order they are observed.

Each error is a frozen `{ source, error }`; the original `error` object is never replaced. `physicalCompletion` does not reject because of an item failure, so the ledger never takes over the caller's error policy.

blocks.text: Re-entry and closing:

items: Calling `start()` or `seal()` while an item's callback or thenable probe is still running throws `SCOPE_REENTRANT_OWN` synchronously (with the `disposalLedgerReentrant` message); the outer `start()` records it as that item's synchronous failure.
`start()` after `seal()` throws `SCOPE_CLOSED` synchronously (with the `disposalLedgerClosed` message) without calling the new callback.
There is no rollback: once `closing`, the ledger can only wait for admitted thenables to settle.

blocks.text: Error policy: the ledger always collects raw errors. `firstError` is simply the final ledger's first observation; `throw`, `report`, the `AggregateError` message/source/code and containment of reporter failures all belong to the calling adapter and are not pushed into the ledger.

blocks.code:
import {
  createGenerationController,
  type IGenerationController,
  type IGenerationControllerOptions,
  type IGenerationRequest,
  type IGenerationToken
} from '@migaia/lifecycle'

function createGenerationController(options?: IGenerationControllerOptions): IGenerationController

type IGenerationControllerOptions = {
  readonly parentSignal?: IAbortSignal
  readonly onSuperseded?: (info: ILifecycleError) => void
  readonly scheduler?: IScheduler // default systemScheduler
  readonly report?: (error: unknown) => void
}

type IGenerationToken = object

type IGenerationRequest = {
  readonly generation: number
  readonly token: IGenerationToken
  readonly signal: IAbortSignal
}

type IGenerationController = {
  readonly generation: number
  readonly disposed: boolean
  begin(options?: { readonly timeoutMs?: number }): IGenerationRequest
  isCurrent(token: IGenerationToken): boolean
  complete(token: IGenerationToken): boolean
  supersede(reason?: unknown): void
  adopt<T>(
    token: IGenerationToken,
    value: T,
    release: (value: T) => void | PromiseLike<void>,
    onReleaseError?: (error: unknown) => void
  ): boolean
  dispose(reason?: unknown): void
}

blocks.text: A generation counter with one `AbortSignal` per generation; starting a new generation makes the previous one stale:
Edge cases:

items: `begin(options?)`: makes the active generation (if any) stale at once by aborting its `signal`, increments `generation` and returns a new `{ generation, token, signal }`. An invalid `options.timeoutMs` (not finite, or negative) throws `INVALID_OPTION`; after that many milliseconds the generation's `signal` aborts. Calling it after `dispose()` throws `GENERATION_DISPOSED`.
`isCurrent(token)`: whether `token` is still the current generation; always `false` after `dispose()`.
`supersede(reason?)`: makes the current generation stale (aborting its `signal`) while the controller stays usable, so a later `begin()` still works. A no-op after `dispose()`.

`complete(token)`: finishes only the matching current generation: returns `true` and makes the token no longer current. It clears the timer, then removes the parent listener, and leaves the signal un-aborted. A stale or disposed token returns `false` without affecting the current generation. A cleanup failure still surfaces as `GENERATION_CANCELLATION_FAILED` with the original `cause`, and the token is stale afterwards; a later `begin()` still works. Real cancellation keeps using `supersede`, the parent signal, a timeout or `dispose`, which keep the signal and its reason.

`adopt(token, value, release, onReleaseError?)`: when `token` is still current, returns `true` and leaves `value` with the caller. Otherwise calls `release(value)` and returns `false`. A throwing or rejecting `release` is only reported through `onReleaseError` and never affects which generation is current (it does not throw and is not fed into an error policy). If `onSuperseded` is set, the stale path first fires one diagnostic carrying the `GENERATION_SUPERSEDED` code; it is not a failure.
`dispose(reason?)`: final. Afterwards `begin()` always throws `GENERATION_DISPOSED` and `isCurrent()` always returns `false`.

When `parentSignal` aborts, the active generation aborts synchronously (its timer is cleared, the parent listener removed and its own controller aborted). Failures during that cleanup are combined into `GENERATION_CANCELLATION_FAILED`.

blocks.code:
import {
  createQuiescenceTracker,
  createStringLeaseRegistry,
  createObjectLeaseRegistry,
  createPendingTracker,
  type IQuiescenceTracker,
  type ILeaseRegistry,
  type IPendingTracker
} from '@migaia/lifecycle'

function createQuiescenceTracker<TKey extends object>(): IQuiescenceTracker<TKey>
function createStringLeaseRegistry(): IQuiescenceTracker<string>

type IQuiescenceTracker<TKey> = {
  retain(key: TKey): IDisposer // IDisposer = () => void
  count(key: TKey): number
  whenZero(key: TKey): Promise<void> // strict, exclusive wait
  whenZeroOnce(key: TKey): Promise<void> // non-exclusive wait
  seal(key: TKey): void
  isSealed(key: TKey): boolean
  forget(key: TKey): boolean
}

blocks.text: Counts leases per key: object keys use a `WeakMap` (collected with the key), string keys use a `Map` (an unsealed entry is removed when its count reaches zero):
Neither factory takes arguments. Edge cases:

items: `retain(key)`: throws `QUIESCENCE_SEALED` on a sealed key. The returned release function is idempotent (it decrements only on the first call).
`whenZero(key)`: you must `seal(key)` first, or it throws `QUIESCENCE_UNSEALED_WAIT` synchronously (not as a rejected Promise). Resolves immediately when the count is already zero.
`whenZeroOnce(key)`: needs no seal; waits for the next time the count reaches zero and does not block new `retain()` calls.
`seal(key)`: idempotent; the key rejects new leases from then on.
`forget(key)`: removes the key's state and returns `true` only when its count is zero and nobody is waiting; otherwise returns `false`.
An unsealed string key that reaches zero is removed from the underlying `Map` automatically, so it does not linger; a sealed key keeps the fact that it is sealed.

blocks.text: The same engine under lease-oriented names (they call `createQuiescenceTracker()` / `createStringLeaseRegistry()` internally), for call sites where "lease" reads better. No arguments.
A narrow interface exposing only `track`, `drain` and `size`, for tracking and draining Promises in flight (built on one string-keyed `createStringLeaseRegistry()`):

blocks.code:
const pending = createPendingTracker()
pending.track(doWork()) // returns the same promise
await pending.drain() // waits until size is 0; work tracked while draining is not missed
pending.size // number of Promises in flight

blocks.text: No arguments. Once a tracked promise settles (resolved or rejected), its lease is released automatically. `drain()` never throws. It loops on `whenZeroOnce()`, so Promises tracked during the drain are waited for as well.
Two-phase ownership during construction: resources wait here until you either `commitTo(parent)` them to their real owner or `rollback()` and release them. You choose one, once:
Edge cases:

items: `own(resource, descriptor)`: throws `PROVISIONAL_SETTLED` after commit or rollback, and `INVALID_OPTION` for an invalid descriptor shape (`order` is not read here; the parent's `own()` checks it at commit).

`commitTo(parent)`: calls `parent.own(resource, descriptor)` for each resource in registration order. If one fails, everything already handed over stays with the parent, and everything not yet handed over is released in reverse order and awaited before the original error is rethrown, so no resource is left owned by nobody. If the cause is that `parent` is already `closing`/`terminal` (code `SCOPE_CLOSED`/`SCOPE_TERMINAL`), the error is wrapped as `PROVISIONAL_PARENT_CLOSED` with the original on `cause` and the release failures of leftover resources on `errors`.

`rollback()`: releases every registered resource in reverse order. A single failure keeps its coded native instance; a primitive is wrapped with the original on `cause`; several failures become an `AggregateError` coded `SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED`. Concurrent and repeated calls share one Promise.

A repeated rollback returns the first Promise, including its rejection. Rolling back after a successful commit, committing twice, or committing after rollback is rejected with `PROVISIONAL_SETTLED` (rollback returns a rejected Promise).
When `parentSignal` aborts (already at construction, or later), `signal` aborts synchronously too, but that does not trigger rollback or commit; the caller must still choose one.

blocks.text: A strict first-in-first-out queue that runs one task at a time, with an optional watchdog for how long a task may wait to start:
Edge cases:

items: `queueAdmissionTimeoutMs`: a number removes a task that has waited longer than that and rejects it with `QUEUE_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT`; `undefined` (the default) only diagnoses and never rejects for waiting; `false` does not even start the diagnostic timer.
`admissionDiagnosticMs`: the diagnostic threshold, used only when `queueAdmissionTimeoutMs` is `undefined` and `onAdmissionDiagnostic` is provided; `false` turns the diagnostic timer off.

`owner`: detects self-dependency. If an owner whose task is running submits a new task to the same queue, that submission is rejected at once with `QUEUE_SELF_DEPENDENCY`, because a FIFO queue cannot run the new task before the current one finishes. This is partial protection: a running task that submits a task with a different or no `owner` and awaits it also deadlocks, but nothing reliably signals that case, so it is not intercepted. The safe pattern is to submit follow-up work without awaiting it inside the current task.
`size`: read-only; tasks waiting plus 0 or 1 running.

blocks.text: The scheduler contract `IScheduler`/`IScheduledTask` and the default `systemScheduler` (a monotonic `performance.now()` clock) are exported by `@migaia/utils/scheduler`; `createManualScheduler`/`IManualScheduler` come from `@migaia/utils/testing`. This module neither exports nor re-exports them. It keeps only the admission layer: when no scheduler is injected into `createMutationQueue`, `createGenerationController`, `boundedWait` or a dispose transaction, they use a snapshot of `resolveScheduler(systemScheduler)`, so an invalid delay is still rejected with lifecycle `INVALID_OPTION` (`detail.field: 'delayMs'`). Calling the utils `systemScheduler.schedule()` directly with the same input yields utils `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead.
The first three positional arguments of `abortableDelay(scheduler, ms, signal, reportCleanup?)` are required and the scheduler is used as given; resolve or snapshot it first if you need admission.

blocks.code: function snapshotScheduler(value: unknown): IScheduler | undefined

blocks.text: Turns any duck-typed value into a standard `IScheduler` snapshot (checked, with accessors read once so a hostile getter cannot be read twice):

blocks.code: const snap = snapshotScheduler(candidate) // undefined, not a throw, when it is not a valid scheduler

blocks.text: One argument `value: unknown`, no options. Returns `undefined` when neither `now` nor `schedule` is a function, and throws `TypeError` (`INVALID_OPTION`) when reading `now` or `schedule` throws. The snapshot's `schedule()` validates the delay, calls the injected `schedule`, then reads the returned task's `cancel` and `unref` once each, in that order. A missing or non-function `cancel` throws `INVALID_OPTION`. A function `unref` gives the snapshot task an `unref()` forwarded with the original task as receiver; without one the snapshot task has no `unref`. If reading `unref` throws (native `TypeError`, original value on `cause`) or it is not a function, `INVALID_OPTION` is thrown after calling the `cancel` already read, so the timer the injected scheduler started is rolled back. If that rollback fails, the primary error is unchanged and the rollback error is attached on its `errors`.

Boundary helpers for code that accepts a custom scheduler. `resolveScheduler(value)` throws an `INVALID_OPTION` error with the `schedulerInvalid` message for an invalid value (rather than returning `undefined` like `snapshotScheduler`). `resolveSchedulerOption(options, fallback?)` reads `options.scheduler` and returns `fallback` when it is absent (or `undefined` in the overload without a fallback); reading the property itself throwing raises `TypeError` (`INVALID_OPTION`).
Delegates to the host's native `AbortController` and returns a real host instance (structurally compatible with DOM and Node `AbortSignal`, so they can be passed to each other):

No arguments and no custom factory. The object is built by the current realm's own `globalThis.AbortController`; lifecycle returns no facade, Proxy or home-made EventTarget. When the host constructor is missing, its getter throws, it cannot be constructed, construction fails or the result lacks the minimal controller/signal shape, `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` is thrown with the original cause.
Behaviour to be aware of:

items: `abort()` and `abort(undefined)` use the host's default reason, usually a native `DOMException` named `AbortError`, not `undefined`.

An explicit reason other than `undefined` keeps its `===` identity. When an `undefined` reason from a structural parent signal is forwarded to a native child, it is normalised to the host `AbortError` as well.
Repeated `abort()` calls are idempotent and do not overwrite the first reason.

An external listener that throws goes through the host EventTarget's error channel; `try/catch` around `controller.abort()` cannot catch it, and lifecycle does not provide an `ABORT_LISTENER_FAILED` error.

Parent and cancellation callbacks that lifecycle registers itself go through a module-private observed subscription. It handles a signal that is already aborted, an abort during registration, a re-check after registration and idempotent removal, and sends its own callback/read/cleanup failures to the matching operation's collect or report boundary. It does not proxy, enumerate or catch other listeners on the same signal.

Waits until an absolute deadline and never cancels the task it waits for:

blocks.code: const won = await boundedWait(task, deadlineAt) // true: task finished first; false: deadline first (task still running)

blocks.text: `task` and `deadlineAt` are required; `deadlineAt` is an absolute time on the scheduler's clock and is validated. A `.catch()` is always attached to `task`, timeout or not, so a later rejection does not become an unhandled rejection. If `deadlineAt` has already passed it returns `false` immediately (after attaching that handler).

blocks.code:
function createTerminalController(): ITerminalController

type ITerminalController = {
  readonly lifecycle: 'open' | 'closing' | 'terminal'
  close(): void
  forceTerminal(): void
  whenTerminal(): Promise<void>
}

blocks.text: The reusable open/closing/terminal state machine that `createLifecycleScope` and `createSyncLifecycleScope` are built on:

blocks.code:
const terminal = createTerminalController()
terminal.close() // open → closing, idempotent
terminal.forceTerminal() // straight to terminal; resolves whenTerminal()
await terminal.whenTerminal()

blocks.text: No arguments. `close()` is synchronous and idempotent and only acts when `open` (a no-op when `closing` or `terminal`). `forceTerminal()` is synchronous and idempotent and goes straight to `terminal`, skipping `closing`. `whenTerminal()` returns the same Promise every time, resolving once when `terminal` is reached; called earlier, it does not resolve immediately.

`package.json` declares `sideEffects: false`: importing a module starts no timer, registers no listener and changes no global. Tree-shaking is done by bundlers; Node and Bun resolve the import graph when importing ESM directly but do not remove unused code for you. To check the effect, inspect the modules a Rollup/Vite build keeps or the chunk contents; comparing total gzip bytes alone is easily misled by compression noise.

A subpath still keeps its own dependencies. `/disposal`, for example, keeps the thenable/error helpers; importing by subpath only guarantees that unrelated Scope, Generation or scheduler code is not pulled in, not that one file has no dependencies.

Collects or reports errors under one of the four policies; `createDisposeTransaction` and `createSyncLifecycleScope` use it internally:

`policy` and `report` are both required; `throw` and `collect` may pass `undefined` explicitly, while `report` and `firstError` need a function or creation throws `INVALID_OPTION`. `add(source, error)` acts immediately according to the policy (`'report'` calls `report` right away; `'firstError'` remembers only the first error and sends the rest to `report`). `finalize(message)`: `'collect'` returns the collected array; `'report'` returns an empty array (already reported in `add`); `'throw'` keeps a single failure's native instance and attaches `SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED` to an unclassified error, wraps a primitive with the original on `cause`, leaves an error with a valid existing source and code unchanged, and combines several failures into an `AggregateError` coded `SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED`; `'firstError'` throws the first error if there was one and otherwise returns an empty array.

items: `own()` throws `SCOPE_CLOSED`/`SCOPE_TERMINAL`: the container is already `closing`/`terminal` and accepts nothing new. Create a new scope instead of reusing the closed one.

`own()`/`dispose()` throws `SCOPE_REENTRANT_OWN`/`SCOPE_REENTRANT_DISPOSE`: a disposer called `own()`/`dispose()` on the very scope that is releasing it. Move that logic out of the disposer or let an outer owner coordinate it.

`SyncLifecycleScope.own()` throws `SCOPE_SYNC_VIOLATION`: the descriptor lacks `syncSafe: true`, a callback returned a thenable, or you tried to own an async `LifecycleScope`/`ProvisionalScope`. A sync scope never awaits; move async resources to `createLifecycleScope()`.

`whenZero(key)` throws `QUIESCENCE_UNSEALED_WAIT` synchronously: `seal(key)` was not called first. The strict wait requires cutting off new leases first; `whenZeroOnce()` drops that requirement but is not exclusive.
`GenerationController.begin()` throws `GENERATION_DISPOSED`: the controller was disposed and cannot be reused; create a new one.

`commitTo()` throws `PROVISIONAL_PARENT_CLOSED`: the target parent is `closing`/`terminal`. What was handed over stays with the parent and the rest was already released; no manual `rollback()` is needed.
`enqueue()` throws `QUEUE_SELF_DEPENDENCY`: an owner submitted and awaited a new task while its own task was running, which would deadlock a FIFO queue; split it into two independent top-level calls.

`systemScheduler` throws `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` (`source: '@migaia/utils'`): the host lacks `performance.now`, `setTimeout` or `clearTimeout`. Inject your own `IScheduler`, or run in a runtime that has them.

You need an event bus, current-value subscriptions or a dependency graph: `@migaia/lifecycle` deliberately does not provide them; see `@migaia/event-subscriber`, `@migaia/reactive` and `@migaia/capability/graph`.

`abortableDelay(scheduler, ms, signal, reportCleanup?)` is imported from the root `@migaia/lifecycle` entry. `scheduler` does the timing; `ms` must be finite and non-negative; `signal` may be `undefined`. It returns `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the delay elapses, `false` when the abort event comes first. The caller decides whether cancellation should become a domain `AbortError`. The result of a synchronous callback is not committed until listener registration and scheduler admission have finished; an admission failure stays the primary error and the original error instance or cause chain stays traceable. The task handle is cancelled at most once, and the abort listener is managed by the module's single observed-subscription helper.

By default a cleanup failure rejects the wait; with `reportCleanup(error)`, cleanup failures go to that observer instead and do not replace a completed or cancelled result. Registration or scheduling failures still reject; `DELAY_FAILED` keeps the native Error's identity and stack, or keeps the original value on `cause` when identity cannot be attached. An invalid duration or cleanup reporter is rejected with `INVALID_OPTION` before admission.

`boundedWait(task, deadlineAt, { scheduler, reportCleanup? })` still races an absolute deadline against a task and does not cancel the task. Its default cleanup-failure behaviour is unchanged; the optional `reportCleanup` lets, for example, a logger flush report a timer cleanup failure as a diagnostic while keeping the task-or-deadline winner. Batch debounces, periodic health checks and budget grant timers are not one-shot relative delays and are not forced into this helper.

`@migaia/lifecycle/scope` is the narrow entry for the async `createLifecycleScope`; import the sync and provisional scopes (`createSyncLifecycleScope`, `createProvisionalScope`) from the root. The module has only one scope implementation. The generation and quiescence subpaths map directly to their single owning modules.

sections.heading: Helpers that are no longer public

blocks.text: `createLifecycleUnit` and its option/result types are no longer exported; applications use `createGenerationController` for stale work and keep loading state in their own code. `createStringQuiescenceTracker` was replaced by `createStringLeaseRegistry`, which has real consumers. `validateSchedulerTime`, `validateSchedulerDelay`, `tagLifecycleError` and `createLifecycleRangeError` are internal and exposed neither at the root nor from a leaf. `/scheduler` exposes the snapshot/resolve admission helpers. Error constructors and scheduler arithmetic helpers are internal with no compatibility aliases; application errors use their own module's identity.

The generation controller's `report?: (error: unknown) => void` receives failures nobody else can receive: a stale resource's release error when `adopt()` is called without `onReleaseError`, and timer or parent-listener cleanup errors from an asynchronous timeout. Throws and rejections from the reporter itself go to the shared host error queue from utils; without a reporter these diagnostics are not emitted.

`resolveScheduler`/`snapshotScheduler` preserve an admitted `IScheduler.defer` alongside `now`/`schedule`. Replacing the method later cannot redirect owners that already registered; raw getters are read during admission. Missing required methods still make `snapshotScheduler` return `undefined`, while getter failures preserve their cause and a supplied malformed `defer` throws a coded `TypeError`. This adds no second clock and does not change deadline cancellation. An older object may omit `defer` and rely on the utils deferred helper's zero-delay fallback.

输出路径中的 sink、hook、pipeline 失败通常通过 onFailure 观察，业务 log/dispatchRaw 不因这些失败直接抛出；这不保证所有输入读取、构造、配置、拓扑操作或 raw 都不会抛错。尤其同步 raw 的 write 失败可以直接抛出。onFailure 中的失败不递归回到自身，改由宿主 reporter 诊断；正常 failure 也继续交给 runtime console.error/write，订阅不是替换默认报告。

ILogEntry 包含 id、tag、time、message、args、meta、context、error、data。id 由核心生成；time 是当前 realm 的 Date，缺省时创建；args 默认空数组，context 默认 logger.ctx.path（构造 context 默认 []），data 默认空对象，meta/error 可省略。tag 是普通标签，级别语义属于 level 插件。

传入 Error 参数会生成 name/message/stack 投影，error.raw 保留原 Error 引用。HTTP 和 color JSON 输出使用 utils 的有界错误链投影，保留 source/code/name/message/stack/cause/errors，不发送 raw；未带语义身份的业务错误使用 unknown/UNKNOWN 诊断占位，不冒充 Logger 抛错码。本地 console 或 custom sink 可继续检查原 Error。

默认阶段顺序为 before → `before:<tag>` → pipeline → 各 sink → after → `after:<tag>` → 转发。hook 的 entry 是活引用。每个 sink 收到独立顶层容器，args、meta、context、data 各复制一层，time 复制成 Date；嵌套业务值仍共享引用，不保证深层隔离。after hook 的修改不影响已交给 sink 的副本，但会影响随后转发的条目。
pipeline 替换值必须保留当前 realm Date 类型的 time；字符串时间或外 realm Date 会报告 PIPELINE_ENTRY_INVALID，source 为 pipeline，并继续交付原 entry。默认不会因此从 dispatch 抛出。同一个 hook 函数多次登记时，off 只移除本次登记。

rows: usePipeline；next 先记录值，当前 stage 返回后才执行下游
useAsyncPipeline；await next(entry) 等待下游，可在之后执行收尾
useGeneratorPipeline；每个 stage 耗尽后取终值
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline；依次 await 耗尽各 stage，中间 yield 不提前交给下游

blocks.text: 同步 stage 可提升到全部 mode，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其他异步/生成器 stage 要求相应模式，不兼容时类型为 never，运行时也拒绝 PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH。执行中禁止新增 stage。重复 next 产生 PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE，延迟 next 产生 PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE 诊断；不调用 next 即截断条目。模式语义与适配由 middleware-pipeline / Plugin Host 拥有，本包不另造执行器。
应用 config.get 支持 'plugin'、'plugin.key'、'plugin.[index].key'；对象和数组配置递归冻结。config.update(name, recipe) 的 patch 是浅合并，不直接修改旧快照。插件 install(core) 中的 core.config 只有无参 get()，只读取当前插件自身配置，不能通过该门面轮询、更新或读取其他插件。

每次安装重新调用插件工厂，不将同一个有状态插件实例跨 Logger 复用。插件安装期可用 core.onDispose(resource) 登记资源，应用变量没有这一安装能力；卸载会撤销该插件登记的 stage、sink、hook、flush/shutdown 回调与扩展。公开调用方使用 ILoggerCore/ILoggerPluginCore，ILoggerDomainCore 仅用于内部装配；类型推导辅助由发布声明和编辑器提示承载。

flush() 等待已观察到的 defer、sink/hook thenable、onFlush、batch 和 extends 下游。它使用 scheduler 的绝对 3000 毫秒预算逐轮排空，不会无限等待一个不合作的 Promise；到期通过 onFailure 报 LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE，尚未完成的工作可由以后 flush 继续观察。跨 realm Promise 或普通 thenable 也会被跟踪，不要求 instanceof Promise。
shutdown 开始时同步进入关闭状态并先发布稳定 Promise。onShutdown 仍可 log/dispatchRaw 写最后条目，但 raw 从关闭开始即不再输出；然后 flush，最后卸载插件并终结。handler 与 flush 共享 3000 毫秒排空预算，后续 Host disposal 使用 execution 的预算，不能把整个 shutdown 说成最多 3 秒。

并发、同步重入、已完成或失败后的 shutdown/dispose 都复用同一完成 Promise，不再重新执行 cleanup。终态 log/dispatchRaw/raw 静默忽略，onFailure 不会专门报告这些被忽略的调用。关闭失败也不能恢复，需新建 Logger。结果 cleanupErrors/cleanupComplete 描述物理清理，不是日志送达回执；下游拒绝或超时仍需宿主补偿。读取时钟失败进入稳定 Promise 的 INVALID_OPTION/cause，仍尝试 Host cleanup，清理次错不覆盖主因。
level(config?) 默认 {}，提供 debug/info/warn/error/fatal、setLevel、addFilter、removeFilter。

rows: []；所有过滤器均返回 true 才放行
false；插件产生的日志是否经 defer

blocks.text: 未知 tag 不按五级阈值过滤，但仍运行 filters。改变级别用 setLevel，addFilter 返回幂等 off，removeFilter 按函数身份移除匹配项。内置 level 在安装时捕获 minLevel 与 filters；config.update 只提交配置快照并调用可选 plugin.update，不会自动更新没有 update hook 的 level 运行状态。
color(config?) 默认 {}，提供 console sink 和 Feature 能力 paint(tag, text)、dim(text)；color 插件的稳定名称是 ansis。

rows: true；pretty 中显示 ISO 时间
undefined；无覆盖时用内置 level 映射，按 tag 指定染色函数

blocks.text: data.silent === true 只让 color 跳过打印，其他 sink 仍接收。color: 'auto' 依次检查 NO_COLOR（有值则关闭）、FORCE_COLOR（有值且非 '0' 则开启）、TTY、CI，再默认关闭；format: 'auto' 先接受 LOG_FORMAT 的 json/pretty，再在 CI 或 TTY 下选 pretty，其余选 json。colorMessage: 'tail' 且没有 args 时会染 message。这些环境读取来自捕获的 Runtime，不改变核心 tag 语义。
batch(config?) 默认 {}，不添加实例方法，通过 Feature 提供 createBatcher(config, onBatch)，处理项不必是日志 entry。

blocks.text: batcher.push(item) 收集，flush() 发送剩余并等待在途 callback；自动登记到 Logger flush。满载报告 BATCH_OVERFLOW，并丢最老排队批次；容量全被在途占用时丢新批次，detail.dropped 是条目数。它有界而非绝不丢失。卸载先关闭接纳、尝试排空，未交付项会报告，不能把 cleanupComplete 当作送达。
http(config) 的 url 必填，用 POST { entries } 发送；其余字段如下：

rows: 2；有限非负整数，表示额外尝试次数
30000；有效 Retry-After 超出时截到此上限
undefined；可含 maxSize/maxWaitMs/maxConcurrentBatches/maxPendingBatches/asyncOutput，未覆盖字段取 batch provider 默认

blocks.text: 网络失败、429 和 5xx 可重试，其他 4xx 直接失败。429 优先接受有效 Retry-After，缺失或无效则指数退避。预算到期时尝试 abort 当前请求；取消器可由 runtimeManager.createAbortController 提供，否则尝试原生 AbortController，无可用控制器时不安排该请求计时，不保证忽略 signal 的 fetch 会终止或结算。没有 fetch 时，发送经 failure 路径报告 TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE。序列化失败为 SERIALIZE_FAILED，失败响应或重试耗尽为 DELIVERY_FAILED。

batch 与 http 同批安装会按 Feature 依赖排序，[http(...), batch()] 同样生效；provider 也可预先安装，跨 use 调用晚装不会追溯重绑。没有 provider 但显式提供 http.batch 时使用本地有界队列，强制 maxSize: 1、asyncOutput: false，其他并发和容量配置仍适用；没有 provider 且未配 batch 时直接逐条发送。关闭先尝试排空最终日志，在 HTTP 插件释放时取消剩余传输。

file(config) 只从独立子入口导入。path 必填，batch 可选并复用 IBatchPluginConfig 全部字段；rotate 可含 maxEntries/maxBytes，均无默认阈值。每批编码为逐行 JSON，达到当前批次条目数或文本字节阈值时调用可选 fs.rotate(path)，不是按磁盘文件累计尺寸旋转。Node 默认 fs 只有 append，不提供 rotate；没有 batch provider 时也使用私有 batcher。浏览器/default 缺 fs.append 时安装失败，FILE_SINK_UNAVAILABLE 可在 Host 安装错误 cause 中找到。写入失败经 onFailure。

process(config?) 默认 {}；captureCrashes 默认 true，shutdownTimeoutMs 默认 3000，interceptProcessExit 默认 false。缺 Runtime process 时 no-op；存在时适配信号、崩溃与退出，interceptProcessExit 会改变原本同步退出的语义。多个参与者共用一组 listener，必须同 process 身份、配置和 scheduler 时间域，否则 PLUGIN_CONFIG_CONFLICT；最后一个卸载后撤销 listener 并重置共享状态。迟到诊断使用首位安装者捕获的 manager，不保证进程崩溃时所有日志送达。

reasoning(config?) 提供 startThinking/thinking/endThinking/startResponse/response/endResponse；labels.thinking 默认 'Thinking...'，labels.response 默认 undefined，asyncOutput 默认 false。token 经 raw 输出，阶段结束再产生 data.silent = true 的完整 entry，供 HTTP/审计收集。可选 color Feature 负责 paint/dim，无提供方则纯文本；同批依赖按拓扑接入。
uuid(config?) 提供每条 entry 的 data.uuid、data.uuidDisplay，display 默认 false。UUID 使用 Logger 捕获的 Runtime；display 控制 color pretty/JSON 的显示，不是日志身份 ctx.id 的替代品。

sections.heading: 转发图与 Runtime 能力

blocks.text: extends(...others) 让条目完整经过目标的 pipeline 和 sink，目标自己的 level/filter 仍生效。每跳把 topic 加入展示链，把稳定 ctx.id 加入内部循环路径，二者分开；topic 可以为空或重名。注册静态拒绝 EXTENDS_SELF/EXTENDS_CYCLE，运行时跳过已走过的 id。sink 私有 data 快照可读展示 topicChain，循环检测 symbol 不外泄。
unextend 按目标 ctx.id 移除，不关闭目标；重复移除为 false。flush 沿图等待下游；转发不合并目标插件扩展的 TypeScript 类型。

blocks.text: new Logger 捕获 runtimeManager 对象本身，插件也使用同一个引用；之后切换模块默认不重定向旧实例，也不是对 manager 对象深拷贝。getLoggerRuntimeManager() 返回当前同一对象，勿就地修改。setLoggerRuntimeManager(manager) 仅为未来 Logger 选择默认并返回幂等 restore，支持嵌套层恢复；需要确定归属时直接通过构造选项注入。默认 UUID 优先 crypto.randomUUID，否则构造本地标识；defer 优先 setImmediate，再 setTimeout(0)，再 queueMicrotask；write 优先 process.stdout，否则 console.log。
LoggerLevel、LoggerColorMode、LoggerReasoningPhase、LoggerStatus 与 LOGGER_SOURCE 是稳定公开常量。颜色/级别类型从根入口导入 ILoggerColorMode/ILoggerLevel；plugins 不再导出旧 IColorMode/ILogLevel。
Logger 自有错误 source 为 @migaia/logger；来自 Plugin Host、middleware 或其它 owner 的完整身份保持原属。LoggerErrorCode 有 17 项：

替换 entry.time 不是当前 realm Date，报告并交付原 entry

process 身份、配置或时间域不兼容
非成功响应或可重试传输耗尽
retries 不是有限非负整数
flush / shutdown drain 到期仍有工作
安装主错之外还有 listener 回滚错误
插件最终清理失败；可能含未交付 dropped 细节
deadline task 或退出清理失败
failure hook 自身失败，仅走宿主诊断
有界队列满载并丢批，检查 detail.dropped
缺注入 fs 且无当前条件默认能力

blocks.text: failure.source 另一个维度为 defer/hook/sink/pipeline/flush/forward/shutdown，表示失败发生在哪一阶段，不是 semantic source。runtime reporter 自身 throw/rejection 经既有宿主异常队列保持可观察，不递归 Logger reporter，也不替换业务结果。

没有输出先看是否安装 sink，再看 level/filter 与 data.silent；批次逐条发送先确认 batch provider 在同批或已提前安装；关闭后不能复用 Logger；动态插件方法在 handle.extensions。需要确定完成时等待 flush/shutdown，但不要把它当作远端持久化回执。生产组合可选择 level、uuid、batch、http、color、process，配置真实 endpoint，并在宿主关闭边界保留 failure 观察直到 shutdown 完成，而不是为了演示发出网络请求。

pnpm --filter @migaia/logger run fmt

blocks.text: test 会先构建本包；typecheck:browser 与 test:e2e 是另外的现有入口。这里只列命令，不声称它们已经执行。
入口 @migaia/logger/plugins/durable 导出 binlog、wal、undoLog 工厂、ILogStore 契约、memoryLogStore、LogRecordState 和 LogStage。每个插件借用独立的调用方资源；保留原对象、类方法与 symbol，不把资源放入插件配置。同一 store 对象不能同时被另一个插件借用。插件不关闭注入资源。

binlog 提供有序追加、读取与订阅。wal.begin 返回前已提交 pending 意图；complete 与 abort 只允许 pending 前进至终态。undoLog 提供 undo.record/get/list/forget，只保存镜像，不执行业务回滚。活跃 txId 必须唯一；forget 先持久写 done 再删除索引，之后允许复用 txId。list 默认返回 100 项，按 time 降序、相同时间按 seq 降序；sinceTime 包含边界。所有读取返回独立快照。

打开原生事务前先等待 ready()；普通方法自动等待初始化。whenIdle() 在卸载后仍可等待已接纳工作及真实端口追加的完成；它不等待外部订阅回调，也不能证明业务事务已提交。logger 的 flush/shutdown 保留原有有限预算。即使 shutdown 拒绝，创建者也必须在 finally 中等待每个插件的 whenIdle，再关闭 store。旧嵌套对象与提取的方法在重装后仍被撤销。

binlog.append(kind,payload,options?) 返回一个序号；appendBatch(records,options?) 返回整批序号。read(fromSeq,{limit?}) 包含起点，limit 默认 100。truncate(beforeSeq) 只删除严格前缀，lastSeq() 永久保留已提交高水位。每个订阅只有一个游标与一个在途回调；慢 listener 不阻塞追加或其它订阅，取消幂等。回调失败停止该订阅，以 source=hook 报告原错。截断越过游标时停止并报告 LOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TRUNCATED。echo 默认 false；true 时普通日志 tag 为 binlog、message 为 kind，meta 只有 seq/time，不输出 payload。

原生事务拥有者可向 binlog 追加与 undo.record 传 ILogAppendOptions.transaction。该拥有者创建绑定精确 store 与活跃事务的 ILogAppendPort。logger 在当前调用栈发起已捕获的 append，返回暂定序号，不提交或回滚；同一个 FIFO 只登记该实际 Promise 的完成等待。真实提交后由 store 唯一发布 onAppend，旧插件卸载后的晚提交也由新安装接收。rollback 不通知、不占用 undo id。memory/file 不提供跨业务资源的事务端口；同名后端本身不证明原子性。

memoryLogStore(options?) 只保证进程内原子性。独立入口 @migaia/logger/plugins/durable/file 的 fileLogStore(path,options?) 使用内置 SQLite：Node/Deno 延迟加载 node:sqlite，Bun 延迟加载 bun:sqlite。支持矩阵为 macOS、Linux、Windows 本地文件系统；实际验证仍须分别给出运行时与操作系统证据。网络文件系统不承诺锁与持久保证。文件资源使用 synchronous=FULL、逐次原生事务和连接级排他锁；先逆序 finalize 语句，再关闭连接。不依赖任何存储包或第三方 native 驱动。COMMIT 失败的结果可能未知，因此本实例停止准入，重开读取真实已提交状态，不自动重放。

import { fileLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable/file'

await using store = await fileLogStore('./orders.sqlite')
await store.append([{ kind: 'order.created', payload: { id: 'o1' } }])
console.log(await store.lastSeq())

blocks.text: ILogStore.append 原子创建记录及 pending 状态，序号从 1 开始；空批不分配序号。read(fromSeq,limit) 按序读取保留快照，limit 为非负安全整数。setState(seq,state) 只允许 pending 到 done/aborted，或 pending 的幂等请求；已结束或不存在时报 WAL_RECORD_INVALID。states(LogRecordState.pending) 返回活跃序号。截断保留永久序号与非递减时间高水位，不复用已提交序号。onAppend 返回幂等取消函数，每个非空真实提交同步发送一次冻结的 lastSeq/count 统计；空批、状态变化、截断与 rollback 不通知，监听失败只报告。

载荷只接受普通 JSON 数据：拒绝 undefined、非有限数、bigint、函数、类实例、循环、数组空洞和访问器。调用进入 FIFO 前已完成快照，不调用 getter/toJSON；共享子对象按 JSON 值复制。store 和插件只通过固定 LogStage 发送身份统计，不包含记录、txId、原生句柄或认证配置；观察失败只报告。原始 I/O 错误始终可从 cause 到达，载荷、范围、关闭与锁错误保持各自语义码。
显式 dispose() 缓存主 Promise，清理失败时拒绝；异步释放 symbol 缓存另一 Promise，报告失败后成功。两个 Promise 共用一次实际清理。创建者在未借出时可使用 raw API，借出期间业务读写只经唯一插件，最后释放权不变。自定义 ILogStore 必须保持同样的原子提交、快照、序号、状态、通知与资源契约。下面的转发例保留一个已有拥有者，不建立第二提交机制：

blocks.code:
import { memoryLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'
import type { ILogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'

const delegate = memoryLogStore()
// A custom implementation must preserve this single owner's atomic commit and notices.
const custom: ILogStore = {
  append: (records) => delegate.append(records),
  read: (fromSeq, limit) => delegate.read(fromSeq, limit),
  lastSeq: () => delegate.lastSeq(),
  onAppend: (listener) => delegate.onAppend(listener),
  truncate: (beforeSeq) => delegate.truncate(beforeSeq),
  setState: (seq, state) => delegate.setState(seq, state),
  states: (filter) => delegate.states(filter),
  dispose: () => delegate.dispose(),
  [Symbol.asyncDispose]: () => delegate[Symbol.asyncDispose]()
}
await custom.append([{ kind: 'custom', payload: null }])
await custom.dispose()

blocks.text: `assertLogInteger(value, minimum = 1)` 复用原数字准入：安全整数且不低于 minimum；非法值保留原 `RangeError/INVALID_OPTION`，超出安全整数保留 `LOG_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED`。

原生日志适配器从同一 durable 入口复用 `snapshotLogRecords`、`prepareLogAppend`、`snapshotLogStoreState` 与 `createLogStoreIndex`。异步准入前捕获可移植 JSON，串行读取已提交 head 后准备序号和时间，再由适配器的原生事务持久写入。只有真实 commit 后才用 `index.applyAppend` 应用原准备批次，并发布一次原追加通知；rollback 不应用批次、不推进水位。状态与截断先检查、原生提交后再应用。恢复复用文件资源原有行、状态和载荷检查；可选载荷解码器只在行身份校验后运行。索引只包含已提交数据和原 pending 链表算法，不提供队列、资源、通知通道或关闭权。作者函数不改变 memory/file 原有同步提交及观察时序。

`level()` 还提供 `atLevel(level, entry)`：`entry` 沿原 `dispatchRaw` schema 保留自己的 tag、payload 和原 Error 引用，并通过同一 level 门槛和 filters。例如 `log.atLevel('debug', { tag: 'storage', message: 'get', meta: { operation: 'get' } })`；它复用原 asyncOutput 与输出资源，没有另一条管线。未调用此入口的未知 tag 保持原先仅过滤器检查，debug/error 等旧方法不变。
按要解决的交付问题选择完整示例；所有场景只使用公开入口和内存收集，不发出 HTTP 请求或写文件。

sections.id: 收集请求字段-不依赖控制台格式
sections.heading: 收集请求字段，不依赖控制台格式

blocks.text: 审计事件需要请求路径和订单标识，供后续收集器按字段读取；把对象打印在消息旁边，会让各收集器自行猜测含义。
传给 `log()` 的末尾对象仍是普通参数，不会自动成为元数据；手写控制台包装也容易把排版与交付混在一起，难以确定由谁负责完成输出。
构造 `Logger` 时明确执行预算，登记输出端，再用 `dispatchRaw` 传入命名字段；`context` 提供条目的默认路径，结束时等待 `shutdown` 完成清理。
execution 必填，mutationTimeoutMs 与 pipelineDrainTimeoutMs 都设为 false，显式取消对应 Host 期限；context 默认 []，本例覆盖为 checkout；dispatchRaw 的 tag/message 必填，meta.orderId 是应用自定义字段；shutdown 的 manual 是四种 reason 之一。

blocks.code: checkout 订单已保存 A-17

blocks.text: 输出 `checkout 订单已保存 A-17`，输出端直接读取默认路径、消息和显式元数据，不需要格式插件便可消费结构化条目。
核心默认不安装输出端，也没有级别方法；本例自行登记 `useSink`，`level()` 才添加 `info`、`warn`，`color()` 才添加控制台渲染。两项必填执行预算均设为 `false`，显式取消对应的 Host 时限。

sections.id: 避免一个输出端改写另一个输出端的条目字段
sections.heading: 避免一个输出端改写另一个输出端的条目字段

blocks.text: 控制台输出端为展示修改条目后，审计输出端意外读到了这些修改；与此同时，参数里的业务对象可能本就需要保留同一引用。
把同一个可变条目交给所有输出端，会让表层格式状态互相污染；把全部值深拷贝，又会改变业务对象身份并增加不同的处理成本。
`Logger` 为每个输出端提供浅快照和独立的 `data` 表；先修改一个输出端的 `data` 与嵌套参数，再观察另一个输出端，确认隔离具体到哪一层。
两项 execution 预算均为 false；data 默认 {}，args 默认 []，本例分别传 route 和 details；每个 useSink 回调处理同一条目的一份浅副本，嵌套 details 保持原引用。

blocks.code:
original 2
2

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `original 2`、`2`；第二个输出端的 `data.route` 保持原值，但两输出端与调用者都看到同一嵌套参数对象的计数变化。
隔离是浅层的：每个输出端分别获得参数数组、路径、`data`、元数据及日期容器的副本，嵌套业务值仍共享；若脱敏必须保护嵌套值，应在管线中替换后再交付。

sections.id: 继续执行前等待异步输出端完成
sections.heading: 继续执行前等待异步输出端完成

blocks.text: 请求写完日志便立即结束响应或退出进程，异步输出端虽然已经启动，却还没保存条目。
只发起、不暴露完成结果的输出端，无法让调用者知道何时写完；仅等待缓冲回调，也覆盖不了其他输出端直接返回的 Promise。
输出端返回真实的 Promise，再等待 `log.flush()`；`Logger` 将其与延后任务、钩子一并追踪，本例使用微任务展示顺序，不依赖猜测延迟。
两项 execution 预算均为 false；useSink 返回真实 Promise，flush 无参数并使用内部 3000 毫秒预算，随后 shutdown 以 manual 关闭。

blocks.code:
0
1 已保存

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `0`、`1 已保存`；日志调用在异步输出提交前返回，`flush` 在所追踪 Promise 保存条目后完成。
公开 `flush()` 不接收参数，使用日志调度器上的 `3000` 毫秒排空预算；截止诊断交给 `onFailure`，不会中止底层工作，也不证明远端已接收，输出端须返回 Promise 才会被追踪。

sections.id: 在共享关闭流程中写入最后一条日志
sections.heading: 在共享关闭流程中写入最后一条日志

blocks.text: 多个所有者同时关闭日志器，而关闭回调还要记录最终状态；重复启动关闭流程可能让最后一条日志写多次，或过早释放资源。
分散的清理函数可能让最终日志与输出端释放同时发生，若各自返回不同 Promise，调用者也难以共享同一次终结结果。
通过 `onShutdown` 登记最终日志，再保留 `shutdown` 的 Promise；`dispose()` 返回同一个完成结果，`Logger` 会先在等待预算内尝试排空最终条目，再释放所安装插件。
两项 execution 预算均为 false；onShutdown 回调接收 reason（本例未使用），manual 明确手动关闭；dispose 无参数，是 shutdown(manual) 的别名。

blocks.code:
true
最后一条

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `true`、`最后一条`；`shutdown` 与 `dispose` 共享同一 Promise，回调中的最终结构化日志到达输出端，关闭后的条目被忽略。
关闭后不能重新启用；关闭回调与排空共享 `3000` 毫秒等待预算，后续 Host 释放另用 `execution` 预算；释放结果报告清理状态及错误，不是日志送达回执。

sections.id: 按级别设门槛-并临时排除保密条目
sections.heading: 按级别设门槛，并临时排除保密条目

blocks.text: 服务平常只需要警告和错误，某次操作又要额外过滤保密条目；撤掉临时规则时，级别门槛仍须保留。
在各调用点散写条件，会重复级别比较；手动维护共享过滤列表，又容易误删别人的规则，或忘记恢复门槛。
安装 `level({ level: LoggerLevel.warn })`，用 `addFilter` 添加规则并保留移除句柄；`setLevel` 独立调整门槛，输出端展示同时通过两项检查的条目。
level 默认 debug、filters: []、asyncOutput: false，本例覆盖为 warn；标准级别完整取值是 debug/info/warn/error/fatal；addFilter 回调决定是否放行，返回句柄可幂等撤销，setLevel 独立改变运行中的门槛。

blocks.code:
import { Logger, LoggerLevel } from '@migaia/logger'
import { level } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [level({ level: LoggerLevel.warn })]
})
const entries: string[] = []
log.useSink((entry) => {
  entries.push(entry.tag + ':' + entry.message)
})
const off = log.addFilter((entry) => entry.message !== '保密')
log.info('低于阈值')
log.warn('保密')
log.error('可见')
off()
off()
log.warn('保密')
log.setLevel(LoggerLevel.info)
log.info('已放行')
console.log(entries.join(','))
await log.shutdown('manual')
error:可见,warn:保密,info:已放行

blocks.text: 输出 `error:可见,warn:保密,info:已放行`；首条信息被门槛挡住，首条保密警告被过滤，之后撤销过滤器与降低门槛分别影响后续调用。
默认 `level: debug`、`filters: []`、`asyncOutput: false`；标准级别为 `debug`、`info`、`warn`、`error`、`fatal`，其他标签不受级别门槛限制，但仍经过过滤；移除句柄按过滤函数身份删除匹配项。

sections.id: 通过指定宿主控制台把错误输出为-json
sections.heading: 通过指定宿主控制台把错误输出为 JSON

blocks.text: 收集器需要可解析 JSON，以及错误名称、消息与堆栈；直接把 `Error` 当普通对象序列化，会丢失不可枚举的内置字段。
直接 `JSON.stringify(new Error())` 通常只得到空对象，手写控制台包装还可能把 JSON 写到另一份宿主控制台，而非当前日志器所使用的那份。
安装 `color({ format: "json" })`，提供公开的 `runtimeManager.console` 接口；本例沿用其余默认能力，仅把控制台输出收集到内存，不写文件也不发送 HTTP。
color 默认 format: auto、color: auto、timestamp: true、colorMessage: none、colorMap: undefined，本例只覆盖 format: json；runtimeManager 沿用当前默认能力，仅将 console.log/warn/error 三个方法改为内存捕获；context 默认 []，本例为 checkout。

blocks.code:
error checkout Error 余额不足
true false

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `error checkout Error 余额不足`、`true false`；JSON 保留错误名称、消息与堆栈字符串，但不输出本地 `raw` 错误引用。
默认 `format: auto`、`color: auto`、`timestamp: true`、`colorMessage: none`，`colorMap` 无覆盖项；JSON 渲染使用有界错误链投影，嵌套参数与业务数据仍遵循普通 JSON 语义。
核心负责构造日志条目、执行处理管线、交给输出端以及等待收尾，不内置级别或控制台输出；这些能力由插件选择组合。本包依赖 event-subscriber、lifecycle、middleware-pipeline、plugin-host、utils 和 ansis；插件安装与资源归属复用 Plugin Host，Logger 不继承 PluginHost。

blocks.text: shutdown reason 四个取值是 'signal'、'uncaughtException'、'unhandledRejection'、'manual'。onShutdown 回调收到本轮 reason。构造静态插件的扩展出现在实例类型上；动态 use 后通过 handle.extensions 调用，原变量类型不扩张。缺失插件的 unUse 拒绝为 Plugin Host 的 PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED；必需 Feature 消费者可以阻止移除提供方。

输出路径中的 sink、hook、pipeline 失败通常通过 onFailure 观察，业务 log/dispatchRaw 不因这些失败直接抛出；这不保证所有输入读取、构造、配置、拓扑操作或 raw 都不会抛错。尤其同步 raw 的 write 失败可以直接抛出。onFailure 中的失败不递归回到自身，改由宿主 reporter 诊断；正常 failure 也继续交给 runtime console.error/write，订阅不是替换默认报告。

ILogEntry 包含 id、tag、time、message、args、meta、context、error、data。id 由核心生成；time 是当前 realm 的 Date，缺省时创建；args 默认空数组，context 默认 logger.ctx.path（构造 context 默认 []），data 默认空对象，meta/error 可省略。tag 是普通标签，级别语义属于 level 插件。

传入 Error 参数会生成 name/message/stack 投影，error.raw 保留原 Error 引用。HTTP 和 color JSON 输出使用 utils 的有界错误链投影，保留 source/code/name/message/stack/cause/errors，不发送 raw；未带语义身份的业务错误使用 unknown/UNKNOWN 诊断占位，不冒充 Logger 抛错码。本地 console 或 custom sink 可继续检查原 Error。

默认阶段顺序为 before → `before:<tag>` → pipeline → 各 sink → after → `after:<tag>` → 转发。hook 的 entry 是活引用。每个 sink 收到独立顶层容器，args、meta、context、data 各复制一层，time 复制成 Date；嵌套业务值仍共享引用，不保证深层隔离。after hook 的修改不影响已交给 sink 的副本，但会影响随后转发的条目。
pipeline 替换值必须保留当前 realm Date 类型的 time；字符串时间或外 realm Date 会报告 PIPELINE_ENTRY_INVALID，source 为 pipeline，并继续交付原 entry。默认不会因此从 dispatch 抛出。同一个 hook 函数多次登记时，off 只移除本次登记。

rows: usePipeline；next 先记录值，当前 stage 返回后才执行下游
useAsyncPipeline；await next(entry) 等待下游，可在之后执行收尾
useGeneratorPipeline；每个 stage 耗尽后取终值
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline；依次 await 耗尽各 stage，中间 yield 不提前交给下游

blocks.text: 同步 stage 可提升到全部 mode，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其他异步/生成器 stage 要求相应模式，不兼容时类型为 never，运行时也拒绝 PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH。执行中禁止新增 stage。重复 next 产生 PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE，延迟 next 产生 PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE 诊断；不调用 next 即截断条目。模式语义与适配由 middleware-pipeline / Plugin Host 拥有，本包不另造执行器。
应用 config.get 支持 'plugin'、'plugin.key'、'plugin.[index].key'；对象和数组配置递归冻结。config.update(name, recipe) 的 patch 是浅合并，不直接修改旧快照。插件 install(core) 中的 core.config 只有无参 get()，只读取当前插件自身配置，不能通过该门面轮询、更新或读取其他插件。

每次安装重新调用插件工厂，不将同一个有状态插件实例跨 Logger 复用。插件安装期可用 core.onDispose(resource) 登记资源，应用变量没有这一安装能力；卸载会撤销该插件登记的 stage、sink、hook、flush/shutdown 回调与扩展。公开调用方使用 ILoggerCore/ILoggerPluginCore，ILoggerDomainCore 仅用于内部装配；类型推导辅助由发布声明和编辑器提示承载。

flush() 等待已观察到的 defer、sink/hook thenable、onFlush、batch 和 extends 下游。它使用 scheduler 的绝对 3000 毫秒预算逐轮排空，不会无限等待一个不合作的 Promise；到期通过 onFailure 报 LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE，尚未完成的工作可由以后 flush 继续观察。跨 realm Promise 或普通 thenable 也会被跟踪，不要求 instanceof Promise。
shutdown 开始时同步进入关闭状态并先发布稳定 Promise。onShutdown 仍可 log/dispatchRaw 写最后条目，但 raw 从关闭开始即不再输出；然后 flush，最后卸载插件并终结。handler 与 flush 共享 3000 毫秒排空预算，后续 Host disposal 使用 execution 的预算，不能把整个 shutdown 说成最多 3 秒。

并发、同步重入、已完成或失败后的 shutdown/dispose 都复用同一完成 Promise，不再重新执行 cleanup。终态 log/dispatchRaw/raw 静默忽略，onFailure 不会专门报告这些被忽略的调用。关闭失败也不能恢复，需新建 Logger。结果 cleanupErrors/cleanupComplete 描述物理清理，不是日志送达回执；下游拒绝或超时仍需宿主补偿。读取时钟失败进入稳定 Promise 的 INVALID_OPTION/cause，仍尝试 Host cleanup，清理次错不覆盖主因。
level(config?) 默认 {}，提供 debug/info/warn/error/fatal、setLevel、addFilter、removeFilter。

process(config?) 默认 {}；captureCrashes 默认 true，shutdownTimeoutMs 默认 3000，interceptProcessExit 默认 false。缺 Runtime process 时 no-op；存在时适配信号、崩溃与退出，interceptProcessExit 会改变原本同步退出的语义。多个参与者共用一组 listener，必须同 process 身份、配置和 scheduler 时间域，否则 PLUGIN_CONFIG_CONFLICT；最后一个卸载后撤销 listener 并重置共享状态。迟到诊断使用首位安装者捕获的 manager，不保证进程崩溃时所有日志送达。

uuid(config?) 提供每条 entry 的 data.uuid、data.uuidDisplay，display 默认 false。UUID 使用 Logger 捕获的 Runtime；display 控制 color pretty/JSON 的显示，不是日志身份 ctx.id 的替代品。

blocks.text: test 会先构建本包；typecheck:browser 与 test:e2e 是另外的现有入口。这里只列命令，不声称它们已经执行。
入口 @migaia/logger/plugins/durable 导出 binlog、wal、undoLog 工厂、ILogStore 契约、memoryLogStore、LogRecordState 和 LogStage。每个插件借用独立的调用方资源；保留原对象、类方法与 symbol，不把资源放入插件配置。同一 store 对象不能同时被另一个插件借用。插件不关闭注入资源。

binlog 提供有序追加、读取与订阅。wal.begin 返回前已提交 pending 意图；complete 与 abort 只允许 pending 前进至终态。undoLog 提供 undo.record/get/list/forget，只保存镜像，不执行业务回滚。活跃 txId 必须唯一；forget 先持久写 done 再删除索引，之后允许复用 txId。list 默认返回 100 项，按 time 降序、相同时间按 seq 降序；sinceTime 包含边界。所有读取返回独立快照。

打开原生事务前先等待 ready()；普通方法自动等待初始化。whenIdle() 在卸载后仍可等待已接纳工作及真实端口追加的完成；它不等待外部订阅回调，也不能证明业务事务已提交。logger 的 flush/shutdown 保留原有有限预算。即使 shutdown 拒绝，创建者也必须在 finally 中等待每个插件的 whenIdle，再关闭 store。旧嵌套对象与提取的方法在重装后仍被撤销。

binlog.append(kind,payload,options?) 返回一个序号；appendBatch(records,options?) 返回整批序号。read(fromSeq,{limit?}) 包含起点，limit 默认 100。truncate(beforeSeq) 只删除严格前缀，lastSeq() 永久保留已提交高水位。每个订阅只有一个游标与一个在途回调；慢 listener 不阻塞追加或其它订阅，取消幂等。回调失败停止该订阅，以 source=hook 报告原错。截断越过游标时停止并报告 LOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TRUNCATED。echo 默认 false；true 时普通日志 tag 为 binlog、message 为 kind，meta 只有 seq/time，不输出 payload。

原生事务拥有者可向 binlog 追加与 undo.record 传 ILogAppendOptions.transaction。该拥有者创建绑定精确 store 与活跃事务的 ILogAppendPort。logger 在当前调用栈发起已捕获的 append，返回暂定序号，不提交或回滚；同一个 FIFO 只登记该实际 Promise 的完成等待。真实提交后由 store 唯一发布 onAppend，旧插件卸载后的晚提交也由新安装接收。rollback 不通知、不占用 undo id。memory/file 不提供跨业务资源的事务端口；同名后端本身不证明原子性。

memoryLogStore(options?) 只保证进程内原子性。独立入口 @migaia/logger/plugins/durable/file 的 fileLogStore(path,options?) 使用内置 SQLite：Node/Deno 延迟加载 node:sqlite，Bun 延迟加载 bun:sqlite。支持矩阵为 macOS、Linux、Windows 本地文件系统；实际验证仍须分别给出运行时与操作系统证据。网络文件系统不承诺锁与持久保证。文件资源使用 synchronous=FULL、逐次原生事务和连接级排他锁；先逆序 finalize 语句，再关闭连接。不依赖任何存储包或第三方 native 驱动。COMMIT 失败的结果可能未知，因此本实例停止准入，重开读取真实已提交状态，不自动重放。

import { fileLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable/file'

await using store = await fileLogStore('./orders.sqlite')
await store.append([{ kind: 'order.created', payload: { id: 'o1' } }])
console.log(await store.lastSeq())

blocks.text: ILogStore.append 原子创建记录及 pending 状态，序号从 1 开始；空批不分配序号。read(fromSeq,limit) 按序读取保留快照，limit 为非负安全整数。setState(seq,state) 只允许 pending 到 done/aborted，或 pending 的幂等请求；已结束或不存在时报 WAL_RECORD_INVALID。states(LogRecordState.pending) 返回活跃序号。截断保留永久序号与非递减时间高水位，不复用已提交序号。onAppend 返回幂等取消函数，每个非空真实提交同步发送一次冻结的 lastSeq/count 统计；空批、状态变化、截断与 rollback 不通知，监听失败只报告。

载荷只接受普通 JSON 数据：拒绝 undefined、非有限数、bigint、函数、类实例、循环、数组空洞和访问器。调用进入 FIFO 前已完成快照，不调用 getter/toJSON；共享子对象按 JSON 值复制。store 和插件只通过固定 LogStage 发送身份统计，不包含记录、txId、原生句柄或认证配置；观察失败只报告。原始 I/O 错误始终可从 cause 到达，载荷、范围、关闭与锁错误保持各自语义码。
显式 dispose() 缓存主 Promise，清理失败时拒绝；异步释放 symbol 缓存另一 Promise，报告失败后成功。两个 Promise 共用一次实际清理。创建者在未借出时可使用 raw API，借出期间业务读写只经唯一插件，最后释放权不变。自定义 ILogStore 必须保持同样的原子提交、快照、序号、状态、通知与资源契约。下面的转发例保留一个已有拥有者，不建立第二提交机制：

blocks.code:
import { memoryLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'
import type { ILogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'

const delegate = memoryLogStore()
// A custom implementation must preserve this single owner's atomic commit and notices.
const custom: ILogStore = {
  append: (records) => delegate.append(records),
  read: (fromSeq, limit) => delegate.read(fromSeq, limit),
  lastSeq: () => delegate.lastSeq(),
  onAppend: (listener) => delegate.onAppend(listener),
  truncate: (beforeSeq) => delegate.truncate(beforeSeq),
  setState: (seq, state) => delegate.setState(seq, state),
  states: (filter) => delegate.states(filter),
  dispose: () => delegate.dispose(),
  [Symbol.asyncDispose]: () => delegate[Symbol.asyncDispose]()
}
await custom.append([{ kind: 'custom', payload: null }])
await custom.dispose()

blocks.text: `assertLogInteger(value, minimum = 1)` 复用原数字准入：安全整数且不低于 minimum；非法值保留原 `RangeError/INVALID_OPTION`，超出安全整数保留 `LOG_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED`。

原生日志适配器从同一 durable 入口复用 `snapshotLogRecords`、`prepareLogAppend`、`snapshotLogStoreState` 与 `createLogStoreIndex`。异步准入前捕获可移植 JSON，串行读取已提交 head 后准备序号和时间，再由适配器的原生事务持久写入。只有真实 commit 后才用 `index.applyAppend` 应用原准备批次，并发布一次原追加通知；rollback 不应用批次、不推进水位。状态与截断先检查、原生提交后再应用。恢复复用文件资源原有行、状态和载荷检查；可选载荷解码器只在行身份校验后运行。索引只包含已提交数据和原 pending 链表算法，不提供队列、资源、通知通道或关闭权。作者函数不改变 memory/file 原有同步提交及观察时序。

`level()` 还提供 `atLevel(level, entry)`：`entry` 沿原 `dispatchRaw` schema 保留自己的 tag、payload 和原 Error 引用，并通过同一 level 门槛和 filters。例如 `log.atLevel('debug', { tag: 'storage', message: 'get', meta: { operation: 'get' } })`；它复用原 asyncOutput 与输出资源，没有另一条管线。未调用此入口的未知 tag 保持原先仅过滤器检查，debug/error 等旧方法不变。

Consume logs by named fields rather than reverse-engineering text. Core entries deliver message, context, and meta separately, as shown in Collect structured request details without a console formatter.

Keep one output’s top-level changes out of another. Each sink receives separate shallow containers with an explicit nested-reference boundary, as shown in Keep one sink from rewriting another sink’s entry fields.
Wait for admitted asynchronous output before continuing. Promises returned by sinks participate in flush tracking, as shown in Wait for asynchronous sink work before continuing.
Let several cleanup owners share one shutdown. Shutdown publishes a stable Promise before final entries and cleanup run, as shown in Write the final entry once during shared shutdown.

Control the level threshold separately from temporary filters. level provides setLevel and a removable addFilter instead of repeated call-site checks, as shown in Apply a threshold and temporarily remove private entries.

blocks.text: The core builds entries, runs a pipeline, dispatches to sinks, and waits for cleanup. Levels and console rendering are optional plugins. Dependencies are event-subscriber, lifecycle, middleware-pipeline, plugin-host, utils, and ansis; plugin installation and resource ownership belong to Plugin Host rather than another lifecycle implementation. blocks.text: The pipeline object contains only mode. Both execution budgets accept a finite non-negative number, including zero and fractions, or false for no deadline. They do not change the public flush() method's internal 3000 ms budget. Constructor installation rejects Promise/thenable install results and rolls back accepted resources rather than returning a partially installed Logger. Use await log.use(plugin) after construction for asynchronous installation.

ctx contains stable id, options, path, topic, createdAt, and env with isTTY/isCI. The context, path, top-level options, and env containers are frozen. Nested option values and the createdAt Date retain their identity and remain mutable; this is not a deep snapshot.

blocks.text: Shutdown reasons are 'signal', 'uncaughtException', 'unhandledRejection', and 'manual'; onShutdown receives that reason. Static constructor plugins contribute methods to the instance type. Dynamic use exposes methods on handle.extensions without expanding the existing variable's type. unUse rejects missing names with Plugin Host's PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED, and required Feature consumers can prevent provider removal.

Sink, hook, and pipeline failures normally reach onFailure without being thrown from the business log/dispatchRaw call. This is not a guarantee that arbitrary input reads, construction, configuration, topology changes, or raw can never throw. In particular, synchronous raw write failures may escape directly. A failure observer's own failure goes to the host reporter without recursively invoking itself; ordinary failures also continue to runtime console.error/write, so subscribing does not replace default reporting.

ILogEntry has id, tag, time, message, args, meta, context, error, and data. The core generates id. time is a current-realm Date, created when omitted. args defaults to an empty array, context to logger.ctx.path (the constructor context defaults to []), and data to an empty object; meta/error are optional. A tag has no built-in level meaning without a plugin.

An Error argument produces a name/message/stack projection while error.raw retains the original Error. HTTP and color JSON use the bounded utils error-chain projection, retaining source/code/name/message/stack/cause/errors without sending raw. Business errors without semantic identity use the diagnostic placeholders unknown/UNKNOWN rather than a fabricated Logger error code. Local console/custom sinks can still inspect the original Error.

The built-in phase order is before → `before:<tag>` → pipeline → sinks → after → `after:<tag>` → forwarding. Hooks receive a live entry. Each sink gets separate top-level containers: args, meta, context, and data are shallow-copied and time is copied as a Date. Nested business values remain shared references. An after hook cannot change snapshots already given to sinks, but its changes can reach the subsequent forwarding step.

Pipeline replacements must retain a current-realm Date time. Application config.get accepts 'plugin', 'plugin.key', and 'plugin.[index].key'. Objects and arrays in plugin config are recursively frozen. config.update(name, recipe) commits a shallow-merged patch without mutating the old snapshot. The install(core) facade exposes only core.config.get() for that plugin's own configuration; it cannot read/update other plugins or serve as an external-condition polling channel.

Create a fresh plugin object for each installation rather than share stateful instances across Loggers. During installation, core.onDispose(resource) owns resources; application variables do not expose this installation capability. Removal releases the plugin's stages, sinks, hooks, flush/shutdown callbacks, and extensions. Use ILoggerCore/ILoggerPluginCore publicly; ILoggerDomainCore is internal assembly detail, and inference-only helper types are carried by declarations/editor tooling.

flush() waits for observed deferred work, sink/hook thenables, onFlush handlers, batches, and forwarding targets. It drains rounds against an absolute 3000 ms scheduler budget rather than waiting forever for an uncooperative Promise. Expiry reports LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE through onFailure; later flush calls can continue observing remaining work. Foreign-realm Promises and ordinary thenables are tracked without an instanceof Promise requirement.

Shutdown marks its state synchronously and publishes one completion Promise before invoking callbacks. onShutdown may still log/dispatchRaw final entries, but raw stops output as soon as shutdown starts. It then flushes, unloads plugins, and becomes terminal. Handlers and flush share the 3000 ms drain budget; subsequent Host disposal uses execution budgets, so the whole shutdown is not bounded to three seconds.

Concurrent, reentrant, completed, and failed repeated shutdown/dispose calls reuse the same Promise rather than repeat cleanup. Terminal log/dispatchRaw/raw calls are silently ignored, without a dedicated onFailure notification. Failure does not revive the Logger; create a new instance. cleanupErrors/cleanupComplete describe physical cleanup, not delivery acknowledgement. Transport failures and deadlines still need host-level remediation. Clock failures reject that stable Promise with INVALID_OPTION/cause while still attempting Host cleanup; secondary cleanup errors do not replace the primary failure.

`@migaia/logger/plugins/durable` exports the `binlog`, `wal`, and `undoLog` plugin factories, the `ILogStore` contract, `memoryLogStore`, `LogRecordState`, and `LogStage`. Each plugin borrows one distinct caller-owned store. The original object remains intact, including class methods and symbols; it never enters plugin configuration. Another installed plugin cannot borrow the same object. Plugins never close injected resources.

`binlog` adds ordered append/read/subscribe operations. `wal.begin` commits pending intent before it returns; `complete` and `abort` only advance pending records to a terminal state. `undoLog` adds `undo.record/get/list/forget`; it stores images and does not apply business rollback. Active transaction ids are unique. Forget persists done before removing the active image, and then permits id reuse. `list` defaults to 100 items, newest time first with sequence descending for ties; `sinceTime` includes its boundary. Reads return independent snapshots.

Call `ready()` before opening a native transaction. Ordinary methods automatically await initialization. `whenIdle()` remains callable after uninstall and waits for already accepted work; it does not await external subscriber callbacks or prove that an owning business transaction committed. Logger flush/shutdown retain their existing finite budgets. Always wait for durable `whenIdle` in `finally`, including rejected shutdown, before the creator closes the stores. Old nested APIs and extracted methods stay revoked after reinstall.

`binlog.append(kind,payload,options?)` returns one sequence; `appendBatch(records,options?)` returns all sequences. `read(fromSeq,{limit?})` starts inclusively and defaults to 100; `lastSeq()` retains the committed high watermark after `truncate(beforeSeq)` removes the strict prefix. Subscribers process history and live data through one cursor, one callback at a time; slow listeners do not block writes or other subscribers. Cancellation is idempotent. Callback failure stops that subscriber and reports the original error through source `hook`. Truncation past its cursor stops it with `LOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TRUNCATED`. Optional `echo:true` emits tag `binlog`, message `kind`, and metadata `{seq,time}` without copying payload into output.

A native transaction owner may pass `ILogAppendOptions.transaction` to binlog append methods or `undo.record`. That owner creates an `ILogAppendPort` bound to the exact store and active transaction. Logger starts the captured append in the current stack, returns provisional sequences without committing, and registers its actual Promise in the same FIFO for `whenIdle`. Store-owned `onAppend` publishes once after real commit, including a late commit after plugin reinstall. Rollback publishes nothing and does not reserve undo ids. Memory/file stores do not provide cross-resource transaction ports; supplying the same backend name does not establish atomicity.

`memoryLogStore(options?)` provides process-local atomicity. `fileLogStore(path,options?)` from the separate `/plugins/durable/file` entry uses builtin SQLite: Node/Deno load `node:sqlite`, Bun loads `bun:sqlite`. macOS, Linux, and Windows local filesystems form the support matrix; only runtime/OS combinations actually exercised establish verification. Network filesystems do not receive a locking/durability guarantee. The file resource uses `synchronous=FULL`, one native transaction per mutation, and a retained exclusive connection lock. Prepared statements release before the connection closes. No storage module or third-party native driver is required. A failed COMMIT stops admission because its outcome may be unknown; reopen to recover committed state without automatic replay.

import { fileLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable/file'

await store.append([{ kind: 'order.created', payload: { id: 'o1' } }])
console.log(await store.lastSeq())

blocks.text: `ILogStore.append` atomically creates records and pending states, allocating sequences from one. Empty batches allocate nothing. `read(fromSeq,limit)` reads ascending retained records; limits are nonnegative safe integers. `setState(seq,state)` permits pending to done/aborted, or an unchanged pending state; terminal/missing records reject `WAL_RECORD_INVALID`. `states(LogRecordState.pending)` returns only active sequences. Truncation preserves the permanent sequence/time watermark, so new records never reuse committed numbers. `onAppend` returns an idempotent off function and delivers one frozen `{lastSeq,count}` notice after a nonempty commit; empty appends, state changes, rollback, and truncation do not publish. Listener failures only report.

Payloads accept plain JSON data: no undefined, nonfinite numbers, bigint, functions, classes, cycles, sparse arrays, or accessors. Input snapshots complete before FIFO admission without invoking getters/toJSON. Shared subobjects are copied as JSON values. Store and plugin observations use fixed `LogStage` names and identity statistics, never records, transaction ids, native handles, or authentication settings. Observer failure only reports. Original I/O failures stay reachable through `cause`; payload/range/closed/lock errors retain their semantic codes.

Explicit `dispose()` returns a stable main Promise that rejects on cleanup failure. The asynchronous disposal symbol returns a different stable Promise that reports failure and resolves. Both share one physical cleanup. The creator owns the resource and may use raw methods before borrowing; while borrowed, business reads/writes go through its one plugin. A custom store must implement the same atomicity, snapshots, sequence/state, notices, and resource rules. This forwarding example preserves one existing owner rather than creating a second commit mechanism:

blocks.code:
import { memoryLogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'
import type { ILogStore } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/durable'

const delegate = memoryLogStore()
// A custom implementation must preserve this single owner's atomic commit and notices.
const custom: ILogStore = {
  append: (records) => delegate.append(records),
  read: (fromSeq, limit) => delegate.read(fromSeq, limit),
  lastSeq: () => delegate.lastSeq(),
  onAppend: (listener) => delegate.onAppend(listener),
  truncate: (beforeSeq) => delegate.truncate(beforeSeq),
  setState: (seq, state) => delegate.setState(seq, state),
  states: (filter) => delegate.states(filter),
  dispose: () => delegate.dispose(),
  [Symbol.asyncDispose]: () => delegate[Symbol.asyncDispose]()
}
await custom.append([{ kind: 'custom', payload: null }])
await custom.dispose()

blocks.text: `assertLogInteger(value, minimum = 1)` reuses original numeric admission: a safe integer at or above minimum. Invalid values retain `RangeError/INVALID_OPTION`; exhausted integers retain `LOG_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED`.

Native log adapters reuse `snapshotLogRecords`, `prepareLogAppend`, `snapshotLogStoreState`, and `createLogStoreIndex` from the same durable entry. Capture portable JSON before asynchronous admission, prepare sequence/time from the serialized committed head, and persist with the adapter's original transaction. Only after its actual commit, apply the exact prepared batch with `index.applyAppend` and publish the original append notice once. Rollback does not apply the batch or advance watermarks. Check state/truncation before native writes and apply those changes after commit. Recovery reuses the file store's row/state/payload checks; an optional payload decoder runs after row identity validation. The index contains committed data and the original pending-list algorithm only; it provides no queue, resource, notification channel, or close authority. These author helpers do not change the synchronous commit or observation timing of memory/file stores.

`level()` also supplies `atLevel(level, entry)`. The entry keeps its category tag, normal `dispatchRaw` payload and original Error references while passing through the same level threshold and filters. For example, `log.atLevel('debug', { tag: 'storage', message: 'get', meta: { operation: 'get' } })` uses the original asyncOutput and output resources. Ordinary unknown tags retain their existing filter-only policy; debug/error and other existing methods keep their behavior.

Passing one mutable entry to every sink lets top-level formatting state leak between outputs. Deep-cloning everything has a different cost and changes application object identity.
Logger supplies each sink with a shallow snapshot and a separate data record. Mutate one sink’s data and a nested argument, then observe the second sink to see the exact isolation boundary.

sections.heading: Write the final entry once during shared shutdown

blocks.text: Several owners close a logger at the same time, and a shutdown callback still needs to record the final state. Repeating shutdown can duplicate the final entry or dispose resources too early.
Independent cleanup functions can race a final log call against sink disposal. Returning unrelated promises also makes it difficult for callers to share one terminal outcome.

Register the final entry through onShutdown, then retain shutdown’s Promise. dispose() returns that same completion; Logger attempts to drain final entries within its waiting budget before releasing the installed plugins.

sections.heading: Apply a threshold and temporarily remove private entries

blocks.text: A service wants warnings and errors normally, but one operation needs an extra privacy filter. Removing that temporary rule must leave the level threshold intact.
Scattered if statements duplicate level comparisons at every call site. A single shared mutable filter list makes it easy to remove another owner’s rule or forget to restore the threshold.
Install level({ level: LoggerLevel.warn }), then add a filter and retain its removal handle. setLevel changes the threshold independently; the sink shows which entries survive both checks.

level defaults to debug, filters to [], and asyncOutput to false; this example selects warn; the complete standard level set is debug/info/warn/error/fatal; addFilter supplies a removable predicate and setLevel changes the active threshold independently.

blocks.code:
import { Logger, LoggerLevel } from '@migaia/logger'
import { level } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [level({ level: LoggerLevel.warn })]
})
const entries: string[] = []
log.useSink((entry) => {
  entries.push(entry.tag + ':' + entry.message)
})
const off = log.addFilter((entry) => entry.message !== 'private')
log.info('below threshold')
log.warn('private')
log.error('shown')
off()
off()
log.warn('private')
log.setLevel(LoggerLevel.info)
log.info('visible')
console.log(entries.join(','))
await log.shutdown('manual')
error:shown,warn:private,info:visible

blocks.text: Prints `error:shown,warn:private,info:visible`. The first info entry fails the threshold and the first private warning fails the filter; removing that filter and lowering the threshold each affects later calls.
