blocks.text: Install the root module first. Each section is independently runnable and uses the code from its matching website case.

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/plugin-host

blocks.text: Shared parameters: defineHost requires host constructor options. Nested execution.mutationTimeoutMs and execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs are required without defaults, bounding active mutation and pipeline draining. Both are 5000 ms here; false waits without a deadline. Omitted pipeline.mode is sync. Omitted domainCore returns an empty object, and omitted custom dispose uses core structured cleanup.

sections.heading: Install a plugin and read its extension

blocks.text: An application needs to add a named capability and later release its resources. Consumers need a usable extension after installation, rather than a partially initialized plugin object.

Assigning plugin methods directly onto an object does not define when installation commits or who owns cleanup. Returning before an asynchronous installer finishes also exposes methods before their resources exist.

defineHost creates the lifecycle owner, and await host.use() returns the installed registration. Both execution budgets are required and set to 5000 ms here; they have no implicit defaults. Dispose the host after use.

definePlugin requires the nonempty name greeting and an install callback returning an ordinary extension object. greet is a plugin-defined no-argument method returning a string. host.use takes a plugin batch and returns handles in input order.
Output:

blocks.code: hello

blocks.text: Prints `hello`. The registration extension is called only after the installation promise has completed, and the final await waits for host cleanup.

The handle owns host operations; the plugin owns the extension it installs. mutationTimeoutMs bounds active mutations and pipelineDrainTimeoutMs bounds shutdown draining; false explicitly removes either deadline. These limits do not preempt user JavaScript.

sections.heading: Roll back a failed batch without removing existing plugins

blocks.text: A feature bundle installs several plugins, but one installer rejects its settings. Previously installed capabilities must stay live, and resources created earlier in the failed bundle must be released.
Registering each extension immediately leaves half a bundle visible after failure. A catch that clears the whole registry also removes plugins that were committed before this batch began.

defineHost keeps a use() batch private until it commits. Register draft cleanup through core.onDispose during installation, then await use(draft, broken) to observe completed rollback and the original failure cause.

Both arguments to use(draft, broken) belong to this batch; existing does not. core.onDispose(resource) requires a cleanup resource and accepts ownership during installation. original is a prebuilt local failure object; comparing error.cause === original verifies its identity.
Output:

blocks.code:
PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED true
draft
live

blocks.text: Prints `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED true`, `draft`, then `live`. The wrapper retains the exact TypeError on cause; the failed batch releases its draft resource while the existing registration still works.

Asynchronous use() releases registered failed-batch resources before rejecting; this example acquires one resource. Previously committed registrations stay live. Arbitrary external side effects are not undone, and rollback errors remain secondary detail.

sections.heading: Keep configuration separate from later source mutations

blocks.text: A plugin definition captures application settings, then the caller edits the original settings object before installation. The installed configuration should reflect the captured definition, not that later edit.
A shallow copy only separates the outer object. Nested settings remain shared references, so changing a nested limit can silently alter what a future installer reads.

definePlugin snapshots and recursively freezes admitted configuration data when the definition is created. Pass ordinary data records or arrays; the host later reads its own configuration through config.get(path).

config is optional and defaults to an empty configuration. Here its nested field is settings.limit: 3, captured when the definition is created. The required get path meter.settings.limit selects the plugin, settings record, and limit value. Unknown paths return undefined.
Output:

blocks.code:
3
true true

blocks.text: Prints `3` and `true true` on separate lines. Editing settings.limit to 99 does not change the installed value, and both captured configuration levels are frozen.

Omitted config defaults to an empty configuration. This is not JSON serialization: supported function leaves retain identity, while unsupported prototypes, accessors, symbols, thenables and cycles are rejected. Use host.config.update() for a committed configuration change.

sections.heading: Release plugin resources once in reverse acquisition order

blocks.text: A plugin opens resources in order and depends on later resources being released first. Several callers may also ask the same host to close, so cleanup must not run again for every caller.
Keeping separate teardown lists makes it easy to reverse one list incorrectly or invoke a disposer twice. Calling cleanup from every dispose request multiplies releases of the same resource.

During definePlugin installation, core.onDispose transfers resources to that registration. defineHost memoizes the disposal promise; await it to observe the plugin hook followed by the resource stack.

Each core.onDispose call receives a no-argument cleanup function. The optional definition dispose hook is plugin-level cleanup; an omitted hook adds no step. Host dispose() takes no arguments and memoizes default core cleanup, releasing resources in reverse registration order.
Output:

blocks.code:
true
plugin,second,first
3

blocks.text: Prints `true`, `plugin,second,first`, then `3`. Concurrent dispose calls share one promise, the plugin hook runs before its resources, and another completed dispose call adds no releases.

onDispose admits resources during installation; it is not a general late-registration API. The host collects cleanup failures, and disposeStepTimeoutMs defaults to 5000 ms per step; inspect cleanupComplete and physicalCompletion when cleanup exceeds its budget.

sections.heading: Start providers before consumers regardless of argument order

blocks.text: Two plugins are supplied in UI discovery order, so a consumer can appear before the provider it needs. The consumer still needs the exact provider output, not a separate reconstructed service.

Installing strictly in array order fails when discovery order changes. Rebuilding the dependency inside each consumer avoids the missing value but creates duplicate service state and separate lifetimes.

defineFeature declares synchronous factories and dependency aliases. provider.getFeature() creates a required cross-plugin reference; host.use() validates the graph and starts the provider before resolving the consumer.

defineFeature(factory, dependencies?) requires a synchronous factory. The optional dependency map defaults to empty. summary declares cache as an alias of provider.getFeature("cache"), required by default. features is the optional named Feature map; use(consumer, provider) intentionally reverses installation order.
Output:

blocks.code:
provider -> consumer
true
consumer provider

blocks.text: Prints `provider -> consumer`, `true`, then `consumer provider`. Factories follow dependency order and the consumer receives the exact output object; returned registration handles still follow the input order.

Factories must synchronously return objects, though their methods may be asynchronous. Outputs are frozen per registration; omitted dependencies mean an empty map, and required references must have available providers. This graph orders capabilities, not reactive data changes.

sections.heading: Reject a missing provider before installers run

blocks.text: A deployment enables a consumer plugin but omits its required provider. The host should report the missing prerequisite before the consumer opens any resources.
Looking up services inside the installer discovers the problem only after earlier setup has already performed work. Passing undefined onward shifts the failure into unrelated consumer code.

A reference returned by getFeature() is required by default. defineFeature retains that dependency, and host.use() checks it before installation; count installer calls to make that admission boundary visible.

getFeature("cache") requires a declared name. Without { optional: true }, the reference is required. use(consumer) omits the provider and fails preflight; installs increments only inside the consumer installer.
Output:

blocks.code:
PREREQUISITE_MISSING
0

blocks.text: Prints `PREREQUISITE_MISSING` and `0`. The missing provider is rejected directly by preflight, and the consumer installer is never entered.

Use getFeature(name, { optional: true }) only when the consumer deliberately handles an absent output as undefined. Required and optional references both contribute ordering when a provider exists; this example intentionally uses the required default.

This module owns plugin installation, Feature dependencies, configuration, stage ownership, and cleanup. Applications supply domain behavior. It depends on `@migaia/capability`, `@migaia/lifecycle`, `@migaia/middleware-pipeline`, and `@migaia/utils`. Pipeline execution and stage lifting use middleware-pipeline; lifecycle scopes, mutation queues, and cleanup use lifecycle.

The public entries are `@migaia/plugin-host` and `@migaia/plugin-host/composition`. Do not import internal files. Applications normally use the root Host, plugin, Feature, handle, and error APIs. Composition is a narrow protocol for one composition owner rather than an alternative application Host.

The class `PluginHost<TDomainCore, TValue, TInstalled>` requires its first type parameter, TDomainCore. Its runtime createPluginDomainCore implementation returns an empty object by default. The pipeline value type defaults to `never` and the declared installed tuple to `readonly []`; defineHost separately provides a default domain type. TInstalled informs installation constraints and configuration types. Runtime use() returns an exact input-order handle tuple; it does not change the static type of the Host variable. Published declarations cover the type-only extraction and merging helpers. `IPluginHostCoreFor<THost>` extracts a Host's domain and pipeline axes; type metadata adds no runtime capability.

Simple options or composed functions can suffice for a few static extension points. Use middleware-pipeline directly when only middleware execution is needed. This Host is useful when a library or application needs consistent plugin resources, dependencies, configuration, and reachability. Logger is an existing repository consumer.

sections.heading: Creating a Host and all options

blocks.text: The class entry can override `createPluginDomainCore()` to create a domain core for each installation. The default is an empty object. Domain cores must be ordinary objects with enumerable data properties. They cannot override config, onDispose, or the four use*Pipeline core members. Invalid surfaces retain native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION.

`defineHost(options)` returns one frozen canonical handle. It supports the class behavior and exposes the class-protected useSync and runPipeline methods to the owner holding that handle. Its required `host` field has the same shape as the class constructor options.

rows: Optional; omission returns an empty object. The Host supplies pluginName, zero-based batchIndex, and batch identity
Optional; omission preserves the original PluginHostError. Default structured disposal does not invoke this hook or translate individual cleanupErrors
Optional disposal middleware; it must call next itself to include core cleanup. Repeated core disposal shares the original promise
Optional; no domain public members by default, and the fourth type parameter defaults to an empty surface

blocks.text: Own surface descriptors are captured once before Runtime acquisition; accessors remain live. Domain members, Host identity, shared outlets, and fluent pipeline methods belong to the same frozen handle. Canonical Host keys, including identity, take precedence. Composing module should supply their methods here rather than copy a frozen handle. A surface option or descriptor-read failure retains the original through CALLBACK_FAILED. Existing calls with three type parameters remain valid.
The class constructor requires options; defineHost requires the same data under host.

rows: Optional readable name; the Host issues a unique id separately
Active mutation hook budget; false removes the deadline
Pipeline lease drain budget; false waits for actual draining
sync / async / generator / async-generator; fixed after construction
Diagnostics and exact contained failure objects
Terminal outlet for a diagnostic callback that throws or rejects
Shared now()/schedule() clock and timer owner
Report-only by default; a number rejects queued work at its limit; false disables related timers and reports
Report threshold only without an admission rejection limit; false disables its timer
Wait limit for one ordinary cleanup step; false waits without a deadline

blocks.text: Time values must be finite and non-negative. Invalid options, nonfunction callbacks, or a scheduler without now()/schedule() retain TypeError with INVALID_OPTION. Directly install utils if importing its scheduler entry.

`definePlugin(name, descriptorFactory, features?)` captures a definition without installing it. Each installation synchronously creates one descriptor, then uses its install(), expose(), and featureExpose() hooks. The two expose hooks return synchronous surfaces. Use `definePlugin(definition)` for configuration, setup, update, and disposal hooks. Both forms and valid raw descriptors share admission. Defining them does not execute an installer or Feature factory. Names are required, nonempty, unique within a Host, and cannot contain a dot. Object definitions capture own data fields and are frozen. The retired shared field has no compatibility fallback: migrate cross-plugin capabilities to Features; adapter-owned shared outlets still use their canonical owner protocol.

rows: Required; install returns a plain extension record or PromiseLike
Optional; omitted configuration becomes an empty record owned as a frozen snapshot
Optional Feature roots and explicitly exposed capabilities
Optional, object form only; prepares resources and retains its output identity
eager by default; lazy is the other value
Optional; successful completion commits config, its return value does not supply config
Optional post-commit notifications without cleanup ownership
Optional, at most once before releasing an installed generation
Optional plugin cleanup, with PromiseLike support
Cleanup fallback when dispose is absent

blocks.text: use(...plugins) accepts a plugin batch. Installation follows dependency order; returned handles follow input order. useSync cannot perform immediate asynchronous installation: a Promise/thenable result causes PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED with INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE on cause, while its eventual rejection stays observed. Immediate installation with setup throws top-level SETUP_REQUIRES_ASYNC_INSTALL before any hook. Constructor options have no plugins field. A class owner calls protected useSync(plugins); the functional handle takes useSync(...plugins). Lazy definitions can be registered synchronously and activated later.

A handle has name, readonly extensions, getFeature(name), and config.get()/update(recipe). Member reads resolve the current registration by name, so an old handle can read a replacement implementation. After removal it throws PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED. An extracted extension function remains bound to its original registration and throws REGISTRATION_REVOKED after revocation. `isPluginHandleCurrent(handle)` instead checks the generation present when that handle was created: disabled and suspended remain current, while replacement, removal, disposal, and unknown objects return false. This probe does not change name-addressed member reads.

Extension results must be ordinary objects. Only enumerable, configurable data properties are published. Accessors and nonconfigurable properties fail with INVALID_OPTION; non-enumerable keys are intentionally skipped with EXTENSION_NON_ENUMERABLE_IGNORED. Do not return a frozen extension object. Host keys, then, and disposal symbols are reserved; catch and finally are allowed. Occupied ordinary keys produce EXTENSION_DUPLICATE; canonical keys take EXTENSION_RESERVED precedence; Object.prototype conflicts produce EXTENSION_OBJECT_PROTOTYPE. Installation retains these failures under PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED. An own then key has its specific INSTALL_RESULT_THENABLE classification.

Install/update cores include the domain core plus config.get(), operation, lifecycle, features, featureExpose, onDispose(resource), and four use*Pipeline(stage) methods. Config reads the committed recursively readonly snapshot. Operation supplies its signal and absolute deadlineAt; lifecycle supplies the registration-generation signal. Stage methods return the same core, are install-window-only, and enforce mode compatibility.

core.onDispose takes ownership only during installation. Outside that window it throws RESOURCE_OUTSIDE_INSTALL without acquiring or releasing the supplied resource; the caller still owns it. Resources may be cleanup functions, synchronous disposables, or asynchronous disposables. Their PromiseLike results are assimilated by the lifecycle owner. Synchronous installation may register asynchronous disposers.

Object-form setup runs in this order: domain core → setup → featureExpose → synchronous Feature factories → install. A batch proceeds serially in dependency order. Setup receives only config.get(), operation.{signal,deadlineAt,now()}, lifecycle.signal, and onDispose(resource). It has no Feature outputs, pipeline registration, or Host mutation capability. Its output is passed by identity as the second argument to featureExpose and install. Without setup, those hooks retain their one-core-argument calls.

Setup and subsequent install share the registration's absolute mutation deadline. With no deadline, deadlineAt is undefined; now uses the injected scheduler clock. Success closes the setup registration window without aborting operation.signal. Timeout or Host closure aborts the attempt and rolls back resources. An unsettled setup cannot prevent Host closure. A late result cannot install; a late rejection is reported. Cooperative cancellation echoing the same abort reason is not reported again.

A late setup context.onDispose first attempts to release a valid resource, then throws RESOURCE_OUTSIDE_INSTALL. A resource without a disposer yields INVALID_OPTION. This differs from late core.onDispose ownership. Setup failures in async use, replacement candidates, and prepared composition admissions preserve the original on PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.cause. Lazy activate preserves its original failure identity. Restart diagnostics unwrap only one PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED layer, without stripping other original cause chains.

`defineFeature(factory, dependencies?)` or `defineFeature({ install, dependencies? })` creates an opaque synchronous definition. Dependencies default to an empty map. The factory's core.featureExpose contains explicitly provided capabilities; its second argument contains declared direct dependency aliases. A factory cannot return PromiseLike, though methods of its returned object may be asynchronous. Runtime authority comes from module-owned identity stores, not the type-only __feature field.

definition.getFeature(name) requires a declared name and creates a required reference by default. getFeature(name, { optional: true }) permits undefined when its provider is absent or not activated. A disabled provider still throws PREREQUISITE_DISABLED. handle.getFeature(name) reads the instantiated output. References retain provider name literals; IPluginFeatureName and IPluginFeatureOutput extract names and outputs.

The Host validates required providers and cycles before any installer, then uses dependency order regardless of use argument order. Consumers receive the provider's exact output object, frozen per registration. Cached ordinary output objects and pure functions do not automatically gain revocation guards. Liveness checks belong to handle reads, extension callables, and protected featureExpose entries. Local Feature dependency closures also contribute cross-plugin edges. Missing, disabled, removed, and cyclic prerequisites use top-level PREREQUISITE_MISSING, PREREQUISITE_DISABLED, PREREQUISITE_REMOVED, and DEPENDENCY_CYCLE rather than an installation wrapper.

readPluginDependencies(input) returns a readonly { provider, required } list. It traverses the local closure, preserves first-provider-reference order, and lets required references win over optional duplicates. Inputs may be definitions, valid raw descriptors, or composition admissions. An admission reuses its captured snapshot without rereading getters; other inputs use standard admission once. No setup, installer, or factory runs. Native admission errors keep their exact object, runtime type, and stack.

host.config is a stable facade. Its required get path can be a plugin name, plugin.key, or plugin.[index].key, with further nesting. Unknown plugins or paths return undefined. config.update(name, recipe) requires both arguments and a synchronous partial plain-record result. Missing plugins reject with PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED. handle.config offers the same operations scoped to one plugin.

Initial configuration is copied and recursively frozen. Ordinary records, arrays, and supported primitives are accepted; function leaves retain identity, so this is not a JSON serialization domain. Date, RegExp, Map, Set, class instances, accessors, nested non-enumerable properties, symbols, dangerous proto/constructor/prototype keys, callable then, and cycles are rejected. Repeated acyclic references are not cycles. Invalid values produce INVALID_CONFIG_VALUE; cycles produce CONFIG_CYCLE_REJECTED, with path/reason detail. Writes to frozen snapshots follow native JavaScript behavior without a promised PluginHost code.

Updates copy and freeze patched branches while sharing untouched frozen branches. update(next, core) sees the complete candidate, while core.config.get() still reads committed configuration. Success commits it. Recipe, patch admission, update-hook, and deadline failures preserve config identity, revision, and existing extensions. Unclassified callbacks receive CALLBACK_FAILED while retaining the original object or cause. Valid PromiseLike lifecycle results are assimilated once.

Both get and update require an active Host. Ordinary get entry failures throw synchronously; failures inside update's queue reject its promise. The setup/beforeRelease synchronous guards below still apply.

sections.heading: Disablement, dependency policies, replacement, and lazy activation

blocks.text: await host.plugin.disable(name) returns { token }. await token.enable() restores that exact registration; host.plugin.enable(name) enables by name; disabled() returns a readonly name snapshot. Disablement keeps resources and scopes without disposal. Extensions, Feature outputs, and stages become unreachable, while Host configuration remains readable and updatable. A successful installation first fires onEnable; each later real transition fires its corresponding notification. Notification failures are reported without rolling back state. A dependent cannot enable while its provider remains disabled. A token preflights the full restoration group before enabling any member.

disable and unUse accept { policy?: 'reject' | 'cascade' | 'suspend'; dryRun?: boolean }, defaulting to reject and false. Reject preserves state and exposes all transitive blockers in detail.blockedBy. Cascade includes required dependents. Suspend handles the target while retaining activated dependent instances and resources. Their handles and extracted functions throw PLUGIN_SUSPENDED, and their stages stop participating. Re-enabling the same provider can restore them directly; a new provider with that name follows capability resume planning to rebind, restart, or resume. Whole-Host release remains dependent-first, including suspended registrations.

dryRun: true returns a frozen { policy, order, steps, edges } plan without ok or mutation. Real unUse success and failure both include frozen affected containing only applied steps; failure additionally includes errors. Migration: replace strict equality against the old { ok: true } shape with an ok check and affected inspection. Literal dryRun true selects the plan overload; omission/false selects execution. Branch on a broad boolean first. Retired { cascade: true } is rejected with INVALID_OPTION.

replace(name, next) requires matching names. It installs the candidate first and leaves the old implementation serving if that fails. Publication switches new runs to the new stage generation; existing runs keep old leases. Captured old functions revoke immediately, while name handles resolve the new registration. Disabled state is retained. Activated required dependents can rebind through onDependencyReplaced. Missing or failed hooks cause their required closure to drain and dispose dependent-first, then reinstall topologically, retaining runtime config and prior activation/disablement state. Old generations dispose after draining. Restart failure does not undo the new provider: failed dependents stay removed, and DEPENDENT_RESTART_FAILED retains an AggregateError ordered as restart failure, rebinding errors, then cleanup errors; detail.dependents lists the affected plugins. Secondary cleanup failures stay reported.

Lazy use registers without activation; extensions throw PLUGIN_NOT_ACTIVATED. activate(name) activates required lazy providers before its own installer. Concurrent same-name calls share a promise. Eager installation activates required registered lazy providers; lazy entries used only by lazy members remain cold. Failed preflight activates nothing. Disabled activation yields PLUGIN_DISABLED. Failed activation withdraws attempted stages, extensions, and shared receipts, releases resources, and retains the cold registration/handle. Explicit retry uses a new scope and batch-bound core. Cleanup errors preserve the primary, and late physical work remains observed.

Mutations such as use, unUse, and config.update share lifecycle's FIFO queue. Defaults report waits beyond 1000 ms without a code or rejection. Only a numeric queueAdmissionTimeoutMs removes expired queued work with MUTATION_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. It does not interrupt started work or permanently disable the Host. False disables those timers and reports. Terminal dispose enters the queue without admission-timeout eviction.

Lifecycle hooks, including setup, install, Feature/expose, update, beforeRelease, disposal, enablement, and rebinding, cannot reenter Host mutation. LIFECYCLE_MUTATION is thrown by entry guards on use/unUse/replace/config.update, while asynchronous enablement entries reject their promises. Throughout an awaited setup or beforeRelease window, new mutations are rejected through the same entry-specific form. Work queued before the window remains FIFO and may reach a configured admission deadline.

Synchronous activate reentry is rejected before consulting a shared request. The runtime has no async-context tracking: after an await, same-name activate can share the active promise just like an external caller. Awaiting one's own activation self-deadlocks. A finite mutationTimeoutMs eventually rejects and rolls back with MUTATION_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT; false can leave it pending indefinitely. Start activation outside hooks.

Host stage registration returns this; plugin core registration returns the core. Unsupported lifts synchronously throw PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH with the upstream middleware-pipeline TypeError / INVALID_OPTION on cause.

Class owners invoke protected runPipeline(value, done) from a domain entry; functional handles expose it directly. Both value and done are required. Sync next records a value and starts downstream after the current stage returns. Async next starts downstream immediately; awaiting it supports after-downstream logic. Omitting next is normal short-circuiting: done is skipped while the run can complete successfully. Duplicate next produces PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE; late next is ignored and reported as PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE.

Generator modes drain the current stage before passing its ordinary return value onward. Implicit undefined or GENERATOR_HALT stops the chain. GENERATOR_CONTINUE selects the last yield, or the input if nothing yielded. GENERATOR_UNDEFINED forwards an actual undefined payload only when its type permits it. Async-generator awaits serially; it provides neither streaming fan-out nor onion execution. Import modes, stage types, and these unique symbols directly from middleware-pipeline, and install that dependency directly when importing it.

Registering stages while any nested run remains active throws PIPELINE_EXECUTING. A run captures its admitted stages. Host stages and plugin slots follow first-allocation order; disabling, restoring, and replacing retain positions. New runs do not acquire revoked generations; old runs retain their leases until completion or cooperative exit.

All stage modes receive context last; generators receive it second. context.signal is the Host lifecycle signal and aborts when disposal starts. A stage must use it to cancel its own I/O. At stage entry, return, or next dispatch, the runner can stop with HOST_DISPOSING or HOST_DISPOSED; it cannot preempt arbitrary promises. A signal reason and later admission error may have matching semantic identity without being the same object. Ordinary failure wins over simultaneous cancellation; one ordinary failure preserves its object. Async stage/downstream dual failures use AggregateError / PIPELINE_FAILED with [stageError, downstreamError]. Serial async-generator failures from factory, body, or done have no equivalent dual-frame aggregation.

Before an installed registration is released, beforeRelease(context) runs at most once. During ordinary removal its publication still serves existing calls. The context signal belongs to that registration; deadlineAt and remainingMs() use the Host clock and disposeStepTimeoutMs. Disablement, suspension, and cold lazy registration alone do not trigger it. Failure or timeout is collected without rolling removal back. Migration: a nonfunction beforeRelease formerly used as metadata now fails as TypeError / INVALID_OPTION.

Removal withdraws new registration/stage admission, drains the relevant leases, runs the plugin disposer, then releases registered resources in reverse order. Ordinary unUse/dispose uses per-step disposeStepTimeoutMs. Reaching it records DISPOSE_STEP_TIMEOUT and continues without cancelling an active promise. A disposer awaiting the host.dispose that invoked it creates self-waiting; a finite step budget allows logical closure to proceed, while false waits indefinitely.

unUse returns { ok: true, affected } or { ok: false, errors, affected }. Drain timeout records PIPELINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT and continues bounded cleanup. Default core dispose shares one promise across repeated calls and synchronous reentry. It returns logicalTerminal, cleanupErrors, cleanupComplete, and possibly physicalCompletion without reopening the Host on cleanup failure. Custom defineHost options.dispose middleware can throw or reject: that failure is classified and rejects the same memoized promise. Core structured cleanup does not guarantee that arbitrary middleware cannot reject.

cleanupComplete false does not mean resources have been released. cleanupErrors is a current snapshot; physicalCompletion carries later errors and may itself have a continuation. To obtain the complete final result, use lifecycle mergeCleanupResults([result]) and install lifecycle directly when importing it. Finite waits do not terminate running leases/disposers; late failures remain observed.

Cleanup functions run directly. Resource objects prefer asynchronous disposal, then synchronous disposal. A plugin's dispose hook takes precedence over symbol cleanup. asyncDisposeKey uses native Symbol.asyncDispose when available, otherwise the module fallback. Synchronous resources can use native Symbol.dispose or ordinary functions, without mandatory polyfills.

isManagedHost(value) recognizes Hosts created by this physical module instance. openComposition(host) accepts those identities, including class and functional Hosts; a lookalike or another installed module copy is not sufficient. The identity writer is private, and defineHost accepts no receiver alias.

A composition owner reads revision/getCurrentSnapshot(), captures definitions with createPluginAdmission, reserves opaque positions with createDataOrderSlot(name), then calls prepareAdmissions([{ admission, slot }]). Setup may execute, but candidate extensions, config, Features, and stages remain unpublished. commitPreparedAdmissions is synchronous without user code and rejects stale revisions. discardPreparedAdmissions rolls temporary resources back once. Returned registration tokens identify exact installations rather than whichever plugin currently has a name.

Calling createDataOrderSlot reserves its order immediately. Disablement, recovery, and replacement reuse it. Retire it only when a definition is permanently removed or the session ends. prepareUnUseBatch accepts exact tokens in the owner's cleanup order. commitPreparedUnUseBatch(prepared, { beforeCleanup? }) first commits logical revocation, then waits for the fence and generation-specific pipeline leases. beforeCleanup is optional without a default promise; when supplied it completes before cleanup.

Managed cleanup requires execution.pipelineDrainTimeoutMs. A number is shared across the batch's leases and cleanup steps; exhaustion continues later steps even if ordinary disposeStepTimeoutMs is false. Explicit pipelineDrainTimeoutMs false instead waits for actual completion step by step, bypassing ordinary limits. The budget does not revoke running work. Observe all physicalCompletion continuations for physical release, or let the outer realm owner terminate its actual execution environment.

createView(token) exposes only that exact registration's extensions, without Host, config, shared, or mutation capability. Repeated views keep function references and concrete Host receivers. Token views remain valid during disablement; complete Host views reject then and recover their original function references on enablement. Removal revokes both. Foreign or revoked tokens fail closed. Migration: the old root createRegistrationView and IPluginRegistrationReceipt were removed; use composition createView/IRegistrationToken.

inspectFeatures(roots) from composition reads trusted Feature topology without executing factories. Adapter-only getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core) accepts a canonical module core and connects declared shared outlets, Features, and registration lifetimes. It is not an admission bypass for ordinary plugins. Only canonical same-family contributions share a slot; ordinary extensions and other families cannot occupy it. A new shared getter publication on a nonextensible Host preserves native TypeError with PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED and leaves no failed family behind. Ordinary handle extensions retain their existing nonextensible-Host contract.

PluginHostError extends Error with readonly source, code, and optional detail. Its source is @migaia/plugin-host; cause/errors retain original failures. Mutable native callback errors receive identity in place; immutable or non-Error values remain on cause. Complete foreign identities retain their owner. INVALID_OPTION keeps TypeError; configuration-domain and cycle failures are PluginHostError. Do not classify all failures by one class or parse diagnostic text.

Rollback failures do not replace installation failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED.detail includes failedName and rollbackErrors in release order. Async use publishes a completed frozen detail; sync useSync publishes a frozen snapshot with detail.completion for final frozen identities. Await completion before translating errors that need all secondary failures. PLUGIN_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED is an additional diagnostic.

diagnostic's third argument retains the original contained failure. Reporter failures cannot alter Host control flow: onDiagnosticFailure receives them, then globalThis.reportError is used if available when that outlet is missing or also fails. Provide onDiagnosticFailure explicitly when Node observation is needed. PluginHostStatus is active/closing/disposed; PluginHostRegistrationLifecycle is idle/install/dispose. ERROR_TEXT is the named root export of stable English texts. MiddlewarePipelineMode and Violation belong to middleware-pipeline.

PluginHostDisposalNodeKind distinguishes Host errors, aggregates, and disposer wrappers. readPluginHostDisposalProvenance(error) reads only provenance registered by this physical module instance. Unknown errors and another module copy return undefined rather than structural guesses. This supports diagnostics, not a replacement for source/code/cause handling.

blocks.text: The emitted syntax target is ES2020. The host must supply Promise, Map, Symbol, AggregateError, and the native capabilities used. Node, Bun, Deno, Workers, mini-programs, and Electron processes can host it without a framework binding. Browser use, including Chrome/Edge 85+, Firefox 79+, Opera 71+, and Safari 14+, also requires the native APIs used. Disposal symbols remain optional as described above.
The existing scripts below are module gates. test checks dist freshness, builds the module when needed, then runs Vitest. No command is considered passed without actual execution.

pnpm --filter @migaia/plugin-host run fmt
pnpm --filter @migaia/plugin-host run lint

blocks.text: For a stalled installation, distinguish queue admission, hook execution, and self-awaiting activation. A failed config update preserves the committed snapshot; inspect code/cause. Use handles returned from use for typed extension access. For unfinished cleanup, inspect its result and continuations rather than assuming logical closure implies physical release.

On sync/async hosts, owners can call `runPipelineSync(value, terminal)` or `runPipelineAsync(value, terminal)` on the `defineHost` handle; subclasses use the same protected entries. Both consume the same registrations, order and lifecycle leases. Sync stages run in both. A visible async stage makes the sync entry throw `ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY` before any stage or terminal runs; removing or disabling it restores sync execution.

The sync entry returns `TResult | undefined`; the async entry accepts a terminal returning `Promise<TResult>` and returns `Promise<TResult | undefined>`. A stage that omits next halts with undefined. Empty lanes invoke the terminal directly, preserving its exact value or Promise identity. Nonempty async execution waits for the actual terminal operation before cleanup. Generator hosts retain `runPipeline`; explicit sync/async entries reject them with `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`.

`getPluginRuntimeIntegration(core).assertPreparedRegistration()` checks the original registration only. Current installation uses original operation admission; a completed candidate in the same unpublished batch requires its exact batch identity and a current installation; published registrations use the original handle admission. Rollback, removal, and host closing revoke access. It returns no registration object and grants no late resource or installation rights. Existing `assertCurrent()` and `core.config.get()` semantics remain unchanged.

libraries.description: Store-neutral reactive runtime, signals, computed values, and effects.

blocks.text: English

界面上的合计、筛选结果、徽标数字都是由其他数据推导出来的。手动在每个修改点同步它们，迟早会漏掉一处；每次写入都立刻通知，又会让页面闪过一半新一半旧的值。`@migaia/reactive` 用 Signal（可写的值）、Computed（自动推导的值）和 Effect（值变化后要做的事）记录谁依赖谁，值变了只更新真正受影响的部分。它与 UI 框架和宿主环境无关，浏览器、Node、Worker 里都能用；store 系列包（集合、持久化、React 绑定等）都建立在它之上。

items: 派生值漏更新：合计、筛选结果单独存在变量里，每个修改点都要记得重算，漏掉一处页面就显示旧值。根因是依赖关系靠人记，没有被程序记录下来。
页面闪过一半新一半旧的值：同时改名和姓，页头先显示 “Grace Lovelace”，再显示正确的名字。根因是每次写入都立刻通知监听者，监听者读到的是只改了一半的数据。
旧订阅没有取消：切换聊天房间后还在接收旧房间的消息，内存慢慢上涨。根因是订阅的清理散落在各处，靠人记得调用。
标签页卡死：两个副作用互相写对方读取的值，值始终对不上，就一直互相触发。根因是没有任何东西限制一次更新能连锁多少轮。
服务端渲染串数据：状态放在模块级的全局变量里，一个请求写入的值被另一个请求读到。根因是所有请求共用了同一份状态图。
派生值只声明一次，依赖自动登记。 手写时每个修改点都要记得重算；`computed` 在读取 `price.value` 时就记下了依赖，任何一个输入变化都会让它重算。示例
多次写入只更新一次，看不到一半新一半旧的值。 每次写入都立刻通知会渲染出混合值；Runtime 写入时只标记过期，副作用在下一次冲刷时按最终输入运行，从多条路径读取同一组值的派生值也一致。示例
没人读取的派生值不计算。 关着的面板也在重算是常见的浪费；`computed` 没人读取就不运行，最后一个读者离开后自动和输入断开，下次读取时才按需重算。示例
副作用死循环会被截断，而不是卡死页面。 互相触发的副作用可能无限运行；每次冲刷最多 `maxFlushPasses` 轮（默认 100），超过后停止并报告 `FLUSH_LOOP` 和相关的 `debugName`。示例
每个 Runtime 完全隔离，混用会立刻报错。 全局状态在服务端请求之间串用很难发现；不同 Runtime 的节点不能互相依赖，跨 Runtime 读取立刻抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`。示例

下面是常见的手写“值变了就通知”。它能跑，但有三个隐患（只用于说明，不必运行）：
用 Runtime 时，`computed` 只声明一次推导规则，依赖在读取时自动登记；写入只把下游标记为过期，副作用在下一次冲刷时统一运行；副作用返回的清理函数会在重跑前和 `dispose()` 时自动执行。
可以把一个 `Runtime` 想成一个独立的电子表格：`Signal` 是输入单元格，`Computed` 是带公式的单元格，`Effect` 是“某个单元格变了就打印或发请求”这类动作。

sections.id: 一张依赖图的完整生命周期
sections.heading: 一张依赖图的完整生命周期

blocks.text: 这段代码建立的是一张由当前 `runtime` 独占的依赖图。`runtime.effect()` 创建时会立即执行一次；执行过程中读取 `doubled.value`，使 `Effect → Computed → Signal` 三层依赖自动登记，所以 `seen` 首先得到 `2`。

`count.value = 3` 只会使 `doubled` 失效并把 `effect` 放入待执行队列，不会在 setter 内立刻重跑副作用。`runtime.flush()` 同步排空该 runtime 的队列：`doubled` 在被读取时按需重算为 `6`，随后 `effect` 把它写入 `seen`。生产代码通常让默认微任务自动冲刷；测试、服务端渲染或需要确定提交边界的代码才显式调用 `flush()`。

释放顺序按消费者到数据源执行：先停掉 `effect`，避免清理过程中再次观察数据；再释放派生节点 `doubled`；最后释放源节点 `count`。`dispose()` 断开依赖边并禁止继续读取已释放节点。`Runtime` 本身没有 `dispose()`；需要批量管理时，把这些节点交给 `@migaia/lifecycle` 的 `createLifecycleScope()` / `createSyncLifecycleScope()` 持有并统一释放。

1. 不要跨 `Runtime` 混用节点：一个 `Runtime` 创建的 `Signal` 被另一个 `Runtime` 的 `Computed` / `Effect` 读取会抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`。 2. 统一经 Runtime 工厂创建节点：`runtime.signal(value, options?)`、`runtime.computed(fn, config?)`、`runtime.effect(fn, options?)`，都有 `dispose()` / `disposed`。三个节点类是内部实现，不作为值导出。 3. `runtime.effect(...)` 创建时会同步立即执行一次，不是等到依赖变化才第一次运行。 4. 给 `Signal` 写入相同的值（`Object.is` 判定）不会触发任何通知，也不会推进版本号。 5. 没有读者的 `Computed` 会被自动挂起（断开依赖；下次读取先验证版本和拓扑，未变则复用缓存）。需要“暂时没人读也保持计算”时传 `{ keepAlive: true }`。 6. `dispose()` 之后的读取会立刻抛 `NODE_DISPOSED`，不会静默返回旧值，避免出现“看起来能用但永远不更新”的状态。 7. `defaultRuntime` 是进程级单例。服务端渲染的请求隔离、单测互不影响、Worker 独立运行，都应该显式调用 `createRuntime()`。 8. 调度可控：默认在微任务里合并冲刷；创建 Runtime 时可用 `schedulerStrategy` 改为 `requestAnimationFrame`、空闲回调或自定义策略。 9. 诊断不进入业务状态：trace 事件和错误上报走独立通道。
不适合的场景：只想要组件内部的局部状态（相当于 `useState`），不需要跨组件共享的依赖图；或者需要开箱即用的可观察集合、异步请求状态机。后两者由本仓的集合、resource 等包在本包之上提供，本包自身不包含。
通用的“一组资源集中释放”容器（原 `Scope` / `createScope()`）已移出本包，改用 `@migaia/lifecycle` 的 `createLifecycleScope()` / `createSyncLifecycleScope()`。
扩展入口的 `claimOwnership`、`ownerOf`、`assertOwnedBy` 对普通对象和函数对象使用同一归属契约：已登记的函数可以查到原 Runtime，跨 Runtime 校验抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`，另一模块副本的品牌抛 `COPY_CONFLICT`。
跨副本诊断使用 `@migaia/reactive.runtime-copies` 和 `@migaia/reactive.ownership-copy` 两个全局 Symbol key。升级时请让同一进程中的 reactive 副本保持同一版本：旧的 `@morning-watch/store` 命名空间与新版本互相不可见，混用时不会互相计数，也不会识别对方的归属标记。

`@migaia/reactive/extension` 提供 `getDefaultRuntime()`，给需要在导入时保持不创建任何东西的适配层使用。它在第一次调用时创建共享的默认 Runtime，返回的对象与根入口的 `defaultRuntime` 完全相同；导入根入口的 `defaultRuntime` 仍在导入时创建。`ReactiveErrorPhase` 也可以从扩展入口导入，与根入口导出的是同一个对象。
`@migaia/reactive/extension` 的 `deferRuntimeCleanup(runtime, task)` 通过该 Runtime 的 `scheduleIdle` 通道安排一次同步的适配层清理（默认使用微任务）。清理抛出的错误交给 Runtime 的 `reportError`。它不返回可修改的调度器或依赖图能力，也不负责异步资源。
English
包的定位、亮点和心智模型见 README。本指南先按场景给出可以直接运行的示例（Node 24），再列出两个公开入口的 API、边界行为与错误码。节点统一经 Runtime 工厂创建；`Signal`、`Computed`、`Effect` 类是内部实现。

blocks.text: 把购物车合计单独存在一个变量里，单价或数量一变，页面就该显示新的合计。
手写时每个修改单价或数量的地方都得记得重新计算合计，漏掉一处页面就显示旧值；依赖关系只存在于开发者的记忆里。
用 Runtime 时，`computed` 只需根据它读到的值把合计声明一次；读取它的 `effect` 会在任一依赖变化后重跑。不需要列出依赖：在函数里读了 `price.value`，就自动依赖它。
输出：

blocks.code:
购物车合计：60 元
购物车合计：90 元
购物车合计：75 元

blocks.text: 先输出 `购物车合计：60 元`，改数量后输出 `90 元`，改单价后输出 `75 元`。
副作用在创建时运行一次，之后每次变化运行一次；`runtime.flush()` 只是让时机更明确，不写它时默认的微任务冲刷也得到同样的输出。

sections.id: 切换订阅时先清理旧的
sections.heading: 切换订阅时先清理旧的

blocks.text: 聊天窗口每次切换房间都加入新房间，却从不离开旧房间，最后会收到所有去过的房间的消息。
手写订阅时，“离开”要写在切换房间的每个分支里，还要记得在关闭窗口时再写一次；漏掉任何一处，旧订阅就一直留着。
`effect` 可以返回一个清理函数，Runtime 会在副作用重跑之前、以及 `dispose()` 时调用它，所以“离开”总是先于下一次“进入”。
输出：

blocks.code:
进入 大厅
离开 大厅
进入 技术交流
离开 技术交流

blocks.text: 依次输出 `进入 大厅`、`离开 大厅`、`进入 技术交流`，`dispose()` 后输出 `离开 技术交流`。
每次清理拿到的都是它那一次运行的房间，因为闭包捕获的是那一次的 `name`。
同时改名和姓，页头先显示 “Grace Lovelace” 这种混合值，再显示正确的名字。
如果每次写入都立刻通知监听者，监听者会在两次写入之间运行，读到只改了一半的数据，页面也因此多渲染一次。
Runtime 写入时只把下游标记为过期，副作用在下一次冲刷（默认是微任务）时才运行，所以同一段同步代码里的写入会被一起看到。从多条路径读取同一组值的派生值（`initials` 和 `label` 都读了名字）也按最终输入重新计算。
输出：

blocks.code:
页头显示: Ada Lovelace（A.L.）
页头显示: Grace Hopper（G.H.）
副作用一共执行了 2 次

blocks.text: 创建时输出 `页头显示: Ada Lovelace（A.L.）`，两次写入后只输出一次 `Grace Hopper（G.H.）`；`副作用一共执行了 2 次`。
没有任何一行出现名和姓混搭的值：同一轮里的写入合并成一次副作用运行。

sections.id: 没人读取的派生值不计算
sections.heading: 没人读取的派生值不计算

blocks.text: 一个昂贵的统计放在可以收起的面板里，面板关着时，数据每变一次它仍然重算一次。
手写的派生值通常在写入时立刻重算，不管有没有人在看，关着的面板也在消耗时间。
`computed` 是惰性的：没人读取就不运行。最后一个读取者（这里是副作用）被释放后，它会和输入断开，之后的写入不再引发重算；下次读取时先检查输入是否变化，变了才重算一次。
输出：

blocks.code:
没人读取时计算次数: 0
报表面板: 305
报表面板: 315
面板打开期间计算次数: 2
面板关闭后计算次数: 2
再次读取: 415 计算次数: 3

blocks.text: `没人读取时计算次数: 0`；面板打开期间每次变化计算一次（共 2 次）；面板关闭后又写入两次，计数仍是 2；再次读取得到 415，计数变为 3。
计算只发生在有人读取的时候，关闭面板后的写入不会触发任何计算。

sections.id: 副作用互相触发时不会卡死
sections.heading: 副作用互相触发时不会卡死

blocks.text: 用两个副作用实现摄氏度和华氏度的双向同步，每个都写对方读取的值；两个值始终对不上时，标签页卡死。
手写的双向同步没有轮数限制，两个监听者会无限互相触发，卡在循环里的页面失去响应，也看不到是哪两段代码在打架。
每次冲刷最多运行 `maxFlushPasses` 轮（默认 100）。超过上限后，Runtime 停止本次冲刷，丢弃剩下排队的副作用，并报告 `FLUSH_LOOP`，附上它们的 `debugName`：自动冲刷交给 `onError`，手动调用 `flush()` 时直接抛出。
输出：

blocks.code:
async-flush FLUSH_LOOP
页面仍可响应，celsius = 12

blocks.text: 先由 `onError` 输出 `async-flush FLUSH_LOOP`，再输出 `页面仍可响应，celsius = 12`。
循环在 20 轮（示例里设的 `maxFlushPasses`）后被截断，而不是一直运行下去；报告里带的 `debugName` 指出了互相触发的副作用。

sections.heading: 服务端每个请求一个 Runtime

blocks.text: 服务端给很多用户渲染页面，一个用户的数据出现在另一个用户的页面上。
`defaultRuntime` 是整个进程共用的一个 Runtime；把请求状态放在这张共享的依赖图里，一个请求写入的值会被另一个请求读到，而且很难发现。
为每个请求用 `createRuntime()` 创建自己的 Runtime。不同 Runtime 的节点不能互相依赖：跨 Runtime 读取会立刻抛出 `CROSS_RUNTIME`，而不是悄悄把数据混在一起。
输出：

blocks.code:
你好，Ada | 你好，Grace
跨 Runtime 读取: CROSS_RUNTIME

blocks.text: 输出 `你好，Ada | 你好，Grace`：每个请求有自己的状态。
把节点带到别的 Runtime 里读取时输出 `跨 Runtime 读取: CROSS_RUNTIME`：串用会在出错的那一行暴露出来。

type IReactiveSignal<T> = IDisposable & {
  readonly runtime: IRuntime
  readonly debugName?: string
  readonly version: number
  readonly disposed: boolean
  readonly observed: boolean // !disposed && 有下游订阅
  value: T // 读建立依赖；写触发下游

blocks.text: 可写原子——响应式图里唯一的"真值来源"：

blocks.code:
const runtime = createRuntime()
const count = runtime.signal(1)
count.value // 1，在 Computed/Effect 内读取会建立依赖
count.value = 2 // Object.is 判定；写入相同值不触发任何通知，也不推进版本
count.peek() // 2，不建立依赖
count.dispose()
count.value // 抛 NODE_DISPOSED

blocks.text: 边界行为：

items: 经 `runtime.signal(value, options?)` 创建；返回窄节点视图，不暴露图边或内部方法。
`value = next`：`Object.is(next, 之前值)` 为真时短路，不推进版本、不触发下游；否则先向 `VersionClock` 领取新版本号再落值（领取失败——时钟耗尽——保持原子失败，绝不出现"值已变、版本未变"的陈旧状态）。
`dispose()` 幂等；释放时先标记 `disposed` 再断开全部下游订阅边（通知顺序：标记优先，确保被迫重跑的 Effect 读到明确的 `NODE_DISPOSED` 而不是重新订阅一个已释放节点）。

`addObservedHooks({ onObserved?, onUnobserved? })`：登记节点级生命周期钩子（多个调用方可各自登记互不覆盖），返回移除函数；多个钩子中若有失败，内部单个失败保留原实例，多个失败聚合为 `OBSERVER_FAILED` AggregateError；公开观察路径捕获并通过 `onError` 的 `lifecycle-hook` phase 报告，创建 Effect 不靠同步 throw 暴露 hook 失败。
跨 `Runtime` 读取/订阅一个 `Signal` 会抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`。

  keepAlive?: boolean
  debugName?: string
}
type IComputedConfig<T> = IComputedOptions<T> | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean)

type IReactiveComputed<T> = IDisposable & {
  readonly runtime: IRuntime
  readonly debugName?: string
  readonly version: number
  readonly disposed: boolean
  readonly observed: boolean

blocks.text: 惰性求值、带缓存的派生值——写只标脏（push），值只在被读时重算（pull）：
边界行为：

items: 经 `runtime.computed(fn, config?)` 创建；配置可以是对象，也可以直接传一个 `equals` 比较函数。
`equals`：默认 `Object.is`；比较函数本身抛错会阻止 dirty 落定（下次读取仍会重算，不会陷入"陈旧但标记为干净"的状态）。
`keepAlive`：默认 `false`——普通无人观察读取在 idle 时机挂起；最后观察者离开时同步挂起（断开依赖、保留版本/拓扑快照）。下次读取先重验证，未变化时复用缓存，否则重算；设为 `true` 时禁用自动挂起。
循环自依赖（求值过程中直接或间接又读了自己）抛 `CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY`，不会栈溢出。
已释放节点的 `value`/`peek` 一律抛 `NODE_DISPOSED`。

blocks.text: 副作用——唯一真正"被执行"的观察者（`Computed` 只标脏不重跑，只有 `Effect` 会被调度器实际 `tick`）：
边界行为：

items: 构造时立即同步执行一次，不是等到依赖变化才第一次运行。
`fn()` 可选返回一个清理函数（`IDisposer`），会在下次重跑前、以及 `dispose()` 时被调用（`runtime.untracked()` 包裹执行，不建立新依赖）；旧 cleanup 会先被摘掉（置空）再执行，避免新 `fn()` 抛错时下次重跑/dispose 重复执行旧 cleanup。

默认微任务策略下依赖变化不会立即重跑，而是被 `Scheduler.enqueue()` 标脏排队，由 `flush()`（自动或手动）驱动 `tick()`；`tick()` 内部会先确认依赖确实变化（`hasStaleDependencies`）才真正 `run()`。注入 `flush => flush()` 这类同步策略时，setter 可在完整 fan-out 后立即重跑 Effect。
依赖节点被 `dispose()`/`disconnectObservable` 断开时，会强制下次 `tick()` 无条件重跑（不看是否真的脏）。

blocks.code:
function createRuntime(options?: IRuntimeOptions): IRuntime
const defaultRuntime: IRuntime

type IRuntimeOptions = {
  adapter?: Partial<IReactiveRuntimeAdapter> // scheduleMicrotask/now/timestamp/reportError
  onError?: (error: unknown, context: IRuntimeErrorContext) => void
  onTrace?: (event: IRuntimeTraceEvent) => void
  maxFlushPasses?: number // 默认 100，须为正整数
  scheduleIdle?: (task: () => void) => void // 默认走 adapter.scheduleMicrotask
  schedulerStrategy?: ISchedulerStrategy // 创建期选择，默认微任务合并
}

blocks.text: 新建一个隔离运行时：
边界行为：

items: `maxFlushPasses` 非正整数（非安全整数或 `< 1`）抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`。

`adapter` 的每个方法（`scheduleMicrotask`/`now`/`timestamp`/`reportError`）独立解析：未提供或显式 `undefined` 回落到默认实现（`queueMicrotask`/`performance.now()`/`Date.now()`/no-op）；提供了但不是函数抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `TypeError`。
`onError`/`onTrace`/`scheduleIdle`/`schedulerStrategy` 若提供但不是函数，构造时抛携带顶层 `INVALID_OPTION` 的原生 `TypeError`。策略校验发生在创建 Scheduler 之前。
`defaultRuntime` 是进程级单例（模块加载时立即 `createRuntime()`），SSR 每请求隔离、单测互不污染、Worker 独立场景都应显式 `createRuntime()`，不要依赖它。
若检测到本库存在多份运行时副本（重复安装/CDN 副本共存/微前端各自打包），构造期会通过 `reportError` 上报一条 `COPY_CONFLICT` 诊断（不阻断构造）。

blocks.text: `IRuntime` 的公开方法（品牌字段省略）：

blocks.code:
type IRuntime = {
  signal<T>(value: T, options?: IReactiveNodeOptions): IReactiveSignal<T>
  computed<T>(fn: () => T, config?: IComputedConfig<T>): IReactiveComputed<T>
  effect(fn: () => void | IDisposer, options?: IReactiveNodeOptions): IReactiveEffect // 返回现有节点的生命周期句柄
  batch<T>(fn: () => T): T
  untracked<T>(fn: () => T): T
  flush(): 'completed' | 'deferred'
  runTracedAction<T>(name: string, fn: () => T): T
  reportError(
    error: unknown,
    context: { phase: IRuntimeErrorContext['phase']; observer?: object; observable?: object }
  ): void
  subscribeTrace(listener: (event: IRuntimeTraceEvent) => void): IDisposer
}

blocks.text: 逐个方法：

items: `batch(fn)`：显式合并多次写入为一次副作用刷新；进入时计深度，只有最外层退出才真正 `flush()`。若 `fn` 抛错且随后的收尾 `flush()` 也抛错，可写的普通 `Error` 保持原对象并在 `cause` 附上 flush 错误；非 `Error` 或不可写 `Error` 用携带 `ACTION_FLUSH_FAILED` 码的 `AggregateError` 保留原值。若业务错误的 `cause` getter 抛错，聚合错误的 `errors` 依次保留业务错误、flush 错误、getter 抛出值；`onError` 另收到 getter 抛出值及 `cause-read` phase。
`untracked(fn)`：`fn` 执行期间关闭依赖收集，读取任何 `Signal`/`Computed` 都不会建立依赖边。

`flush()`：同步冲刷当前队列。重入语义：observer `tick()` 内部再次调用 `flush()` 返回 `'deferred'`（外层 flush 仍在跑，本次调用不会真正冲刷）；最外层调用完成并排空队列后返回 `'completed'`。单次冲刷内的重算轮数超过 `maxFlushPasses` 抛 `FLUSH_LOOP`（见错误码表），并清空剩余队列，错误信息列出被丢弃的最多 8 个 `debugName`。
`schedulerStrategy` 创建期选项只改变何时 `flush`，不交出 Scheduler 队列。策略须同步返回；返回 thenable 会触发 `INVALID_OPTION` 诊断并回退到已验证的安全策略。Runtime 存活期间不公开替换入口。
`runTracedAction(name, fn)`：执行并追踪一段真实 action；`name` 必须是非空字符串，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。未启用 trace（无监听器）时只执行 fn 与同一 callback 错误边界，不创建 trace 事件。
`reportError(error, context)`：诊断通道；`context.observer`/`context.observable` 是原始节点对象，内部会先脱敏为 `IRuntimeNodeDescriptor` 再转发给 `onError`。reporter 自身 throw/rejection 交 utils 共享宿主异常队列，不反向破坏图操作。
`subscribeTrace(listener)`：只读诊断事件流（值变化、依赖连接/断开、副作用执行、显式 action），返回取消订阅函数。

blocks.text: 要求当前进程只有一份进入过正确性边界的模块副本，否则抛 `COPY_CONFLICT`。应用从根入口显式调用，库自身不主动调用它。重复安装、CDN 副本共存或微前端独立打包时，应去重依赖。
实现层通过本入口取得扩展能力。它允许图协议参与和所有权登记，能力多于公共 `IRuntime`；不会交出 tracker/scheduler/clock 对象或可变边集。

blocks.code:
import {
  createObserverBinding,
  type IObserverBinding,
  type IObserverCommitResult,
  type IObserverRetrackResult,
  type ICapture
} from '@migaia/reactive/extension'

function createObserverBinding(runtime: IRuntime): IObserverBinding

type IObserverBinding = {
  capture<R>(read: () => R): ICapture<R>
  observe(fn: () => void | IDisposer, options?: IReactiveNodeOptions): IDisposer
  commit(capture: ICapture<unknown>): IObserverCommitResult
  retrack(): IObserverRetrackResult
}

type IObserverCommitResult = 'committed' | 'stale' | 'no-observer'
type IObserverRetrackResult = 'changed' | 'unchanged' | 'no-observer'

blocks.text: 为一个订阅者建立三段式绑定：render 期只读地捕获依赖，commit 期才把依赖装到订阅者上，中间的渲染可能被并发渲染丢弃，捕获阶段绝不建边。绑定自持一个内部 `Effect`：适配层能完成 capture/observe/commit/retrack，却拿不到 `deps`、版本或强制调度入口：
四个成员逐一说明：

items: `capture<R>(read: () => R): ICapture<R>` —— 渲染期捕获：只记录本次读到了哪些依赖节点及其当时版本，不建立依赖边、不推进版本、不排 idle 工作。读取 dirty Computed 复用其 speculative preview，所需已求值图保留在同一个 token 内，commit 先验证完整依赖树，再接纳图/缓存，不重跑 derivation 或 comparer；被丢弃的渲染不会留下订阅残留。`ICapture<R>` 是带品牌的不透明 token，`result: R` 是 `read()` 的返回值；依赖集合存在 tracker 私有 `WeakMap` 里，拿到 token 既读不出依赖也改不了版本。
`observe(fn, options?): IDisposer` —— 安装绑定持有的内部 `Effect`（具体类保持私有，适配层拿不到它去改 `deps`/版本或调用 `run`/`markDirty`）。同一个 binding 重复调用（当前订阅者仍处于已观察状态时再次调用）抛 `BINDING_DUPLICATE`。返回的 disposer 幂等。

`commit(capture): IObserverCommitResult` —— 提交期安装依赖，把 `capture` 装到创建绑定时指定的那个 observer 上。`'committed'`：依赖边已安装；`'stale'`：捕获后依赖已变化，token 已消费，必须重新捕获——调用方只应在此时作废快照并重新取值，不应该在 commit 阶段去 pull 脏节点（那会把用户的求值错误抛在 commit 里，绕过 Error Boundary）；`'no-observer'`：提交目标尚不存在（还未 `observe()` 或已 dispose），token 未消费，可在 observer 就绪后重试。
`retrack(): IObserverRetrackResult` —— 强制当前已提交的 observer 重跑一次，并报告其依赖集合或记录版本是否发生变化（`'changed'`/`'unchanged'`），无 observer 时返回 `'no-observer'`。

blocks.text: 「某节点属于哪个 `Runtime`」的登记与断言，供在本包之上构建 Store/集合/资源类库的作者使用。

items: `claimOwnership(value: object, runtime: IRuntime): void` —— 登记普通对象或函数对象的归属；首次登记安装已有不可枚举、不可写的跨副本品牌，WeakMap 仍为本地权威。同一引用重复登记到不同 `Runtime` 抛 `OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`。
`ownerOf(value: unknown): IRuntime | undefined` —— 查普通对象或函数对象的归属，普通未登记值返回 `undefined`；foreign copy 品牌触发 `COPY_CONFLICT`，不作为普通未登记值放行。
`assertOwnedBy(value: unknown, runtime: IRuntime, what: string): void` —— 宽松断言：普通未登记值放行，foreign copy 品牌先拒绝（第三方可以把普通值注册进 Registry，不涉及图）；只有登记过且归属不符才抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`。
`assertReactiveOwnedBy(value: object, runtime: IRuntime, what: string): void` —— 内核图边界使用的严格断言：未登记直接抛 `NOT_RUNTIME_OWNED`；登记了但不属于当前 `runtime` 抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`。

blocks.code: import { createFieldSource, type IRuntimeFieldSource } from '@migaia/reactive/extension'

blocks.text: 为扩展层创建一条受控 Source（如 Wasm 字段、SharedArrayBuffer 支持的值）。调用方只拿到 `track`/`notify`/`commit`/`dispose` 四个能力，拿不到底层节点、`subs`、版本或 `Tracker`，因而不能制造单边依赖、伪造版本、通知另一张 `Runtime` 图：
边界行为：`track()`/`notify()`/`commit()` 在 `dispose()` 之后调用抛 `NODE_DISPOSED`；`commit(write)` 先领取版本号、执行 `write()`、再发布通知（与 `Signal.value = ` 的三段式一致）。

blocks.code:
import {
  internalRuntimeOf,
  isRuntimeTracking,
  isAnyRuntimeTracking,
  currentRuntimeVersion,
  type IObservable,
  type IObserver,
  type IInternalRuntime
} from '@migaia/reactive/extension'

items: `internalRuntimeOf(runtime: IRuntime): IInternalRuntime` —— 校验本库 Runtime 登记，未登记抛 `NOT_RUNTIME_OWNED`。`signal()` 返回 `IReactiveSignal<T> & IObservable`，`computed()` 返回 `IReactiveComputed<T> & IObservable & IObserver`。关系只读；observer 操作与所有权登记属于扩展能力，内部服务对象和可变边集不再公开。公开节点本身已经具有 `dispose()`。
`isRuntimeTracking(runtime: IRuntime): boolean` —— 只读查询：该 `Runtime` 当前是否正在收集依赖帧。
`isAnyRuntimeTracking(): boolean` —— 只读查询：进程内任意 `Runtime` 当前是否有依赖帧处于活跃状态。
`currentRuntimeVersion(runtime: IRuntime): number` —— 读取原有版本时钟，不暴露时钟对象；未登记对象抛顶层 `NOT_RUNTIME_OWNED`。

sections.heading: 自定义 source 与 observer

blocks.text: `createSourceBinding(node)` 为实现 `IObservable` 的新节点登记canonical版本与订阅者集合，返回只读 `version/subs` 和绑定原节点的 `source` 操作。构造时把只读元数据接入节点，再公开实例；保留SAB节点原身份。一般外部字段仍直接用 `createFieldSource(runtime)`。

`createTrackedObserver(observer)` 为实现 `IObserver` 的新节点创建只读 `deps/depVersions`，提供绑定自身的 `runTracked/clear/suspend/isSuspended/revalidate/hasStaleDependencies/deferIdle`。`clear` 只断图依赖，资源请求与取消仍由调用方管理；它不创建另一个Effect或tracker。框架render/commit适配继续用 `createObserverBinding(runtime)`。
这两个factory不能重绑已登记图节点（包括内置节点）：抛 `GRAPH_NODE_REGISTERED`，不会替换仍有活跃边的集合。`invalidateObservable(runtime, node)` 只摘节点下游、保留上游与缓存，供Atom routing切换；真正释放节点仍调用其dispose。
迁移：`@migaia/reactive/internals` 已删除。旧 `internalsOf/registerSubs/registerVersion/registerDeps` 等不能通过换名导入整个tracker；按上述角色迁移到 `/extension` 的绑定能力。`tracker/scheduler/clock` 和可写集合始终仅在kernel内部。

blocks.code: import { ReactiveErrorCode, type IReactiveErrorCode } from '@migaia/reactive'

blocks.text: 稳定错误码表，18 个码，唯一声明处 `src/error-code.ts`，`source` 恒为 `'@migaia/reactive'`。（迁移背景：原属于本包的 `SCOPE_CLOSED`/`SCOPE_REENTRANT_DISPOSE`/`SCOPE_SYNC_VIOLATION`/`GENERATION_DISPOSED`/`SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED` 五个码已随生命周期原语迁出，归属 `@migaia/lifecycle`，不在本表。）

rows: 未分类 action/batch/untracked/tracked derivation callback 失败；native 尽量原位附码，primitive（含 undefined）/不可变 native 原错保留 cause，已有 semantic identity 不变；非 Error 对象 throw 保留控制身份，供 Resource/Suspense owner 单次准入
在已 dispose 的 `Signal`/`Computed`/自定义 Source 上调用读取或写入方法
求值 `Computed` 时检测到它（直接或间接）读取了自己正在求值的结果
一个属于某 `Runtime` 的节点或已登记函数对象在另一个 `Runtime` 的追踪/所有权边界上被读取、订阅或校验
传入的对象不是由 `createRuntime()` 创建、或不携带内部所有权登记
同一个对象或函数引用被重复登记到不同的 `Runtime`
检测到本库存在多份运行时副本、查询到另一副本已登记的对象或函数，或 `assertSingleRuntimeCopy()` 校验到副本数大于一
跨副本诊断品牌被发现处于非预期形状
单调版本时钟达到配置上限（默认 `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`）后再次申请新版本号
一次冲刷内的重算轮数超过 `maxFlushPasses`（默认 100）
一次冲刷中多个 observer 的 `tick()` 失败、或多个 observable 生命周期钩子失败，作为 `AggregateError` 外壳
`runBatched()` 内业务动作与收尾 flush 同时失败；普通可写错误在 `cause` 附加聚合结果，不可读 `cause` 的三个原值直接置于 `AggregateError.errors`
预留：异步调度策略回调或 `reportError()` 捕获到未处理错误的诊断通道码（默认无内置抛出/上报点）
`capture()` 产生的 token 在 `commitCapture()` 时已失效、已被消费、属于另一个 tracker，或对应 observer 已 dispose
同一个 `IObserverBinding` 被重复调用 `observe()`（已处于 observed 状态）
source/observer binding尝试替换已有graph node的集合，须创建新节点
同一个 `Runtime` 对象被重复注册内部面（`registerInternals()`）
构造 `Runtime`/`Scheduler`/`VersionClock` 时传入的选项不满足取值要求

items: 读取节点抛 `NODE_DISPOSED`：节点已 `dispose()`，绝不会静默返回旧值；停止持有该引用，改用重新创建的实例。
抛 `CROSS_RUNTIME`/`NOT_RUNTIME_OWNED`：跨 `Runtime` 混用了节点，或传入的对象不是由 `createRuntime()` 创建；确认节点与消费它的 `Runtime` 是同一个。
`Computed` 抛 `CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY`：依赖图里存在自读环（`a` 直接或间接又读了 `a` 自己）；检查依赖图，拆掉循环引用。
`flush()` 抛 `FLUSH_LOOP`（自动冲刷时交给 `onError`，phase 为 `async-flush`）：副作用之间互相触发停不下来，典型是两个 `Effect` 各自写对方读取的值，而两个值始终对不上；错误信息列出了被丢弃的待办 `debugName`，据此定位并拆环。单个 `Effect` 在运行中写自己读取的值不会让自己重跑。
`createObserverBinding().observe()` 抛 `BINDING_DUPLICATE`：同一个 binding 在已处于 observed 状态时又被 `observe()` 了一次；再次调用前先确认当前是否已在观察中，或为新一轮渲染创建新的 binding。
`commit()` 返回 `'stale'`：这不是错误，是正常的竞态处理信号；作废当前快照，重新 `capture()`/`commit()`，不要在 commit 阶段直接 pull 脏节点。
`COPY_CONFLICT`/`BRAND_CORRUPTED`：进程内存在本库的多份模块副本；去重依赖（多数打包器问题），或在应用启动时调用 `assertSingleRuntimeCopy()` 主动 fail-fast。

中文

Totals, filtered lists and badge counts on a page are all derived from other data. Syncing them by hand at every place that changes the data eventually misses one; notifying on every single write makes the page flash half-updated values. `@migaia/reactive` uses Signals (writable values), Computeds (derived values) and Effects (work to do when values change) to record who depends on whom, and updates only what a change really affects. It does not depend on any UI framework or host, so it runs in browsers, Node and Workers; the store module (collections, persistence, React bindings and so on) are built on it.

items: Stale derived values: totals or filtered lists kept in their own variables must be recalculated at every place that changes the data, and one missed place shows an old value. The cause: people, not the program, keep track of the dependencies.

Half-updated values flashing on the page: changing first and last name shows "Grace Lovelace" in the header before the right name appears. The cause: every write notifies listeners immediately, so they read data that is only half updated.

Old subscriptions that never end: after switching chat rooms the window still receives the old room's messages, and memory slowly grows. The cause: subscription cleanup is scattered and depends on someone remembering to call it.
A frozen tab: two effects write the value the other reads, the values never agree, and they keep triggering each other. The cause: nothing limits how many rounds one update may chain.
Server rendering mixes data: state lives in module-level variables, and a value written by one request is read by another. The cause: every request shares one state graph.

A derived value is declared once, and its dependencies register themselves. Hand-written code must remember to recalculate at every change; a `computed` records a dependency the moment it reads `price.value`, and any input change makes it recompute. Example

Several writes produce one update, with no half-updated values. Notifying on every write renders mixed values; the Runtime only marks dependents as stale on write and runs effects in the next flush with the final inputs, so derived values read through several paths agree too. Example

A derived value nobody reads is not computed. Recomputing for a closed panel is a common waste; a `computed` does not run until something reads it, disconnects from its inputs when its last reader leaves, and recomputes on demand at the next read. Example

An endless effect loop is cut off instead of freezing the page. Effects that trigger each other may run forever; each flush is capped at `maxFlushPasses` passes (default 100), after which it stops and reports `FLUSH_LOOP` with the `debugName`s involved. Example

Every Runtime is isolated, and mixing them fails at once. Global state leaking between server requests is hard to notice; nodes of different Runtimes cannot depend on each other, and a cross-Runtime read throws `CROSS_RUNTIME` immediately. Example

The two changes that follow do not print once each; they merge into one update in the next microtask, which prints 360 directly ((300 + 100) × 0.9). `total` read `items.value` and `discount.value`, so those dependencies were registered with no extra subscription code.

With a Runtime, a `computed` declares its rule once and registers dependencies as it reads them; a write only marks dependents as stale and effects run together in the next flush; and the cleanup function an effect returns runs automatically before each rerun and on `dispose()`.

Think of a `Runtime` as an independent spreadsheet: a `Signal` is an input cell, a `Computed` is a cell with a formula, and an `Effect` is an action such as "print or send a request when a cell changes".

blocks.text: See the usage guide for every signature, edge behavior and error code. Below are the constraints that matter most in daily use.

sections.heading: The full lifecycle of one dependency graph

blocks.text: This code builds a dependency graph owned by the current `runtime` alone. `runtime.effect()` runs once immediately on creation; while it runs it reads `doubled.value`, which registers the three-level dependency `Effect → Computed → Signal` automatically, so `seen` first receives `2`.

`count.value = 3` only invalidates `doubled` and queues `effect`; it does not rerun the effect inside the setter. `runtime.flush()` drains that runtime's queue synchronously: `doubled` recomputes to `6` when read, and then `effect` writes it into `seen`. Production code usually lets the default microtask flush automatically; tests, server rendering or code that needs a definite commit point call `flush()` explicitly.

Release from consumers to sources: stop `effect` first so cleanup does not observe data again, then the derived node `doubled`, and finally the source node `count`. `dispose()` disconnects dependency edges and forbids further reads of the released node. A `Runtime` itself has no `dispose()`; to manage nodes in bulk, hand them to `createLifecycleScope()` / `createSyncLifecycleScope()` from `@migaia/lifecycle` and release them together.

1. Do not mix nodes across `Runtime`s: a `Signal` created by one `Runtime` and read by a `Computed` / `Effect` of another throws `CROSS_RUNTIME`. 2. Always create nodes through the Runtime factories: `runtime.signal(value, options?)`, `runtime.computed(fn, config?)` and `runtime.effect(fn, options?)`, each with `dispose()` / `disposed`. The three node classes are internal and not exported as values. 3. `runtime.effect(...)` runs once synchronously on creation; it does not wait for a dependency change before its first run. 4. Writing the same value to a `Signal` (by `Object.is`) triggers no notification and does not advance its version. 5. A `Computed` with no readers is suspended automatically (its dependencies are disconnected; the next read first checks versions and topology and reuses the cache when nothing changed). Pass `{ keepAlive: true }` when it must keep computing while nobody reads it. 6. Reading after `dispose()` throws `NODE_DISPOSED` immediately instead of silently returning an old value, so nothing can "look alive but never update". 7. `defaultRuntime` is a process-wide singleton. Request isolation in server rendering, independent unit tests and Workers should all call `createRuntime()` explicitly. 8. Scheduling is configurable: by default flushes merge in a microtask; when creating a Runtime, `schedulerStrategy` can switch to `requestAnimationFrame`, idle callbacks or a custom strategy. 9. Diagnostics never enter application state: trace events and error reports use separate channels.

Where it does not fit: you only need local component state (the equivalent of `useState`) and no dependency graph shared across components; or you need ready-made observable collections or a state machine for async requests. The collection and resource module in this repository build those on top of this module; it does not include them itself.

The general "release a group of resources together" container (formerly `Scope` / `createScope()`) has moved out of this module; use `createLifecycleScope()` / `createSyncLifecycleScope()` from `@migaia/lifecycle`.

sections.heading: Multiple copies and the extension entry

blocks.text: The extension entry's `claimOwnership`, `ownerOf` and `assertOwnedBy` apply one ownership contract to plain objects and function objects: a registered function reports its original Runtime, a cross-Runtime check throws `CROSS_RUNTIME`, and a brand from another module copy throws `COPY_CONFLICT`.

Cross-copy diagnostics use two global Symbol keys, `@migaia/reactive.runtime-copies` and `@migaia/reactive.ownership-copy`. When upgrading, keep every reactive copy in one process on the same version: the old `@morning-watch/store` namespace and the new version cannot see each other, so mixed copies neither count each other nor recognize each other's ownership marks.

`@migaia/reactive/extension` provides `getDefaultRuntime()` for adapters that must create nothing at import time. It creates the shared default Runtime on its first call and returns exactly the same object as the root entry's `defaultRuntime`; importing the root `defaultRuntime` still creates it at import time. `ReactiveErrorPhase` can also be imported from the extension entry and is the same object as the root export.

`deferRuntimeCleanup(runtime, task)` from `@migaia/reactive/extension` schedules one synchronous adapter cleanup on that Runtime's `scheduleIdle` channel (microtasks by default). Errors thrown by the cleanup go to the Runtime's `reportError`. It returns no modifiable scheduler or graph capability and does not own asynchronous resources.
中文

For what the module is for, its highlights and its mental model, see the README. This guide starts with runnable examples organized by scenario (Node 24), then lists the APIs, edge behavior and error codes of both public entries. Nodes are always created through the Runtime factory; the `Signal`, `Computed` and `Effect` classes are internal.

sections.heading: Keep derived values in sync automatically

blocks.text: A cart total is kept in its own variable, and whenever the price or quantity changes the page should show the new total.
Hand-written code has to recalculate the total in every place that changes price or quantity; miss one and the page shows a stale total, because the dependency exists only in the developer's head.

With a Runtime, `computed` declares the total once from the values it reads, and an `effect` that reads it reruns when any of them changes. Nobody has to list the dependencies: reading `price.value` inside the function is enough.
Output:

blocks.code:
cart total: 60
cart total: 90
cart total: 75

blocks.text: Prints `cart total: 60`, then `90` after the quantity changes and `75` after the price changes.
The effect ran on creation and once per change; `runtime.flush()` only makes the timing explicit, and without it the default microtask flush gives the same output.

sections.heading: Clean up the old subscription before switching

blocks.text: A chat window joins a new room whenever the room changes but never leaves the old one, and ends up receiving messages from every room it ever visited.
With hand-written subscriptions, "leave" has to be written in every branch that switches rooms and again when the window closes; missing any one of them keeps an old subscription alive.
An `effect` may return a cleanup function. The Runtime calls it before the effect runs again and when the effect is disposed, so "leave" always runs before the next "join".
Output:

blocks.code:
join lobby
leave lobby
join engineering
leave engineering

blocks.text: Prints `join lobby`, `leave lobby`, `join engineering`, and `leave engineering` after `dispose()`.
Each cleanup sees the room of its own run, because the closure captured that run's `name`.
Changing first and last name together makes the header show a mixed value such as "Grace Lovelace" before the correct name.
When every write notifies listeners at once, a listener runs between the two writes, reads half-updated data, and the page renders one extra time.

A Runtime write only marks downstream nodes stale, and effects run at the next flush (a microtask by default), so writes in the same synchronous code are seen together. Derived values that read the same inputs through several paths (`initials` and `label` both read the name) are recomputed from the final inputs too.
Output:

blocks.code:
header shows: Ada Lovelace (A.L.)
header shows: Grace Hopper (G.H.)
the effect ran 2 times

blocks.text: Prints `header shows: Ada Lovelace (A.L.)` on creation and, after the two writes, a single `Grace Hopper (G.H.)`; `effect ran 2 times`.
No line ever shows a mixed first and last name: writes in the same turn merged into one effect run.
An expensive aggregation sits in a panel that can be collapsed, and it recalculates on every change even while the panel is closed.
Hand-written derived values usually recompute right when data is written, whether or not anyone is looking, so a closed panel still costs time.

A `computed` is lazy: it does not run until something reads it. When its last reader (here the effect) is disposed, it disconnects from its inputs, so later writes trigger no recomputation; the next read checks whether its inputs changed and recomputes once if they did.
Output:

blocks.code:
computations while unread: 0
report panel: 305
report panel: 315
computations while the panel is open: 2
computations after closing: 2
read again: 415 computations: 3

blocks.text: `computations while unread: 0`; while the panel is open each change computes once (2 in total); after closing, two more writes leave the count at 2; reading again returns 415 and the count becomes 3.
Computation happens only when something reads the value; writes after the panel closed trigger none.

sections.heading: Effects feeding each other do not freeze the page

blocks.text: Two-way Celsius/Fahrenheit syncing is written with two effects that each write what the other reads; when the values never settle, the tab freezes.
Hand-written two-way syncing has no limit on rounds, so the two listeners trigger each other forever, the page stops responding, and nothing tells you which two pieces of code are fighting.

Each flush is capped at `maxFlushPasses` passes (default 100). Past the cap the Runtime stops, drops the remaining queued effects and reports `FLUSH_LOOP` with their `debugName`s: to `onError` for automatic flushes, or as a thrown error from a manual `flush()`.
Output:

blocks.code:
async-flush FLUSH_LOOP
the page stays responsive, celsius = 12

blocks.text: Prints `async-flush FLUSH_LOOP` from `onError`, then `the page stays responsive, celsius = 12`.
The loop was cut after 20 passes (the `maxFlushPasses` set in the example) instead of running forever, and the reported `debugName`s point at the effects feeding each other.
A server renders pages for many users, and one user's data appears on another user's page.
`defaultRuntime` is one shared Runtime for the whole process; request state kept in that shared graph can be written by one request and read by another, and the leak is hard to notice.
Create a Runtime per request with `createRuntime()`. Nodes of different Runtimes cannot depend on each other: a cross read throws `CROSS_RUNTIME` at once instead of quietly mixing data.
Output:

blocks.code:
Hello, Ada | Hello, Grace
cross-Runtime read: CROSS_RUNTIME

blocks.text: Prints `Hello, Ada | Hello, Grace`: each request has its own state.
The leaked read prints `cross-Runtime read: CROSS_RUNTIME`: mixing Runtimes shows up at the exact line that does it.

type IReactiveSignal<T> = IDisposable & {
  readonly runtime: IRuntime
  readonly debugName?: string
  readonly version: number
  readonly disposed: boolean
  readonly observed: boolean // !disposed && has downstream subscribers
  value: T // reading registers a dependency; writing notifies dependents
  peek(): T // reads without registering a dependency
  dispose(): void
  addObservedHooks(hooks: { onObserved?: () => void; onUnobserved?: () => void }): () => void
}

blocks.text: A writable atom, the only "source of truth" in the reactive graph:

blocks.code:
const runtime = createRuntime()
const count = runtime.signal(1)
count.value // 1; reading inside a Computed / Effect registers a dependency
count.value = 2 // compared with Object.is; writing the same value notifies nothing and keeps the version
count.peek() // 2, without registering a dependency
count.dispose()
count.value // throws NODE_DISPOSED

blocks.text: Edge behavior:

items: Created with `runtime.signal(value, options?)`; it returns a narrow node view that exposes no graph edges or internal methods.

`value = next`: when `Object.is(next, previous)` is true the write short-circuits, with no version bump and no notification. Otherwise it first takes a new version number from the `VersionClock` and then stores the value. If taking a version fails (the clock is exhausted), the write fails atomically, so "value changed but version did not" can never happen.

`dispose()` is idempotent. Releasing first marks the node `disposed` and then removes every downstream edge, in that order, so an Effect forced to rerun reads a clear `NODE_DISPOSED` instead of subscribing to a released node again.

`addObservedHooks({ onObserved?, onUnobserved? })` registers node-level lifecycle hooks (several callers can register without overwriting each other) and returns a removal function. When hooks fail, a single failure keeps its original instance and several failures are aggregated as an `OBSERVER_FAILED` `AggregateError`; the public observation path catches them and reports them to `onError` with phase `lifecycle-hook`, so creating an Effect never surfaces hook failures as a synchronous throw.
Reading or subscribing to a `Signal` from another `Runtime` throws `CROSS_RUNTIME`.

blocks.code:
type IComputedOptions<T> = {
  equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean
  keepAlive?: boolean
  debugName?: string
}
type IComputedConfig<T> = IComputedOptions<T> | ((a: T, b: T) => boolean)

type IReactiveComputed<T> = IDisposable & {
  readonly runtime: IRuntime
  readonly debugName?: string
  readonly version: number
  readonly disposed: boolean
  readonly observed: boolean
  readonly value: T // reading registers a dependency and recomputes lazily
  peek(): T // reads and recomputes without registering a dependency
  dispose(): void
}

blocks.text: A lazy, cached derived value: writes only mark it dirty (push), and the value is recomputed only when read (pull):
Edge behavior:

items: Created with `runtime.computed(fn, config?)`; the config can be an object or an `equals` comparison function.
`equals`: `Object.is` by default. If the comparison function itself throws, the dirty state is not settled, so the next read recomputes instead of being stuck "stale but marked clean".

`keepAlive`: `false` by default. An ordinary read with nobody observing suspends the node at idle time; when the last observer leaves it suspends synchronously (disconnecting dependencies but keeping its version and topology snapshot). The next read revalidates first, reusing the cache when nothing changed and recomputing otherwise. `true` disables automatic suspension.
A circular self-dependency (the evaluation reads itself directly or indirectly) throws `CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY` instead of overflowing the stack.
`value` / `peek` on a released node always throw `NODE_DISPOSED`.

blocks.text: A side effect, the only observer that is really "executed" (a `Computed` only marks itself dirty and does not rerun; only an `Effect` is actually `tick`ed by the scheduler):
Edge behavior:

items: Runs once synchronously on creation; it does not wait for a dependency change before its first run.

`fn()` may return a cleanup function (`IDisposer`), called before the next rerun and on `dispose()`, wrapped in `runtime.untracked()` so it registers no new dependencies. The old cleanup is detached (set to empty) before it runs, so if the new `fn()` throws, the next rerun or dispose does not run the old cleanup twice.

With the default microtask strategy, a dependency change does not rerun the effect immediately; `Scheduler.enqueue()` marks it dirty and queues it, and `flush()` (automatic or manual) drives `tick()`. Inside `tick()` it first confirms that a dependency really changed (`hasStaleDependencies`) before calling `run()`. With a synchronous strategy such as `flush => flush()`, the setter can rerun the Effect right after the full fan-out.
When a dependency node is disconnected through `dispose()` / `disconnectObservable`, the next `tick()` reruns unconditionally, without checking whether it is really dirty.
