items: Every tier must already exist in an earlier installation batch and support KV. Tiers with `ttlMs` also need TTL. The slowest tier must use `through`. Cache offers no cross-tier atomic commit or transactions.

Tier read failures are reported and treated as misses; tier write failures are reported and skipped. Loader and encoding failures use `CACHE_LOAD_FAILED`; embedding failures use `CACHE_EMBED_FAILED`. The original error remains in `cause`. Cache errors use `source: 'storage.backend.cache'`; argument and capability errors may come from storage-contract.
Ordinary `get/set` handle strings; `get` reads only entries written by ordinary `set`. Use `getOrLoad`, `getOrLoadEntry` and `peek` for encoded objects and negative entries.

Invalidation propagation is enabled by default and subscribes during `detect()`. Every tier above a change source needs hard TTL. Notifications do not make writes atomic across tiers. Dedicated cache backends avoid unrelated business clear notifications removing cache copies.

`write: 'back'` is not a durable queue. Failures are not retried. `flush()` processes current pending writes, and shutdown flushes once too. With propagation enabled, a back tier must be below every change source and have TTL; otherwise configuration is rejected.

Multi-tier `removeByPrefix` cannot return a reliable deduplicated count, so it rejects with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before I/O. Use uncounted `invalidate({ prefix })` instead. `removeMany` counts each known distinct logical key once.

`host.org(uuid).backend('cache')` routes every tier to the same organization. Cache shutdown drains work already started and cancels subscriptions without closing borrowed tiers separately. Host shutdown releases the backends it installed.

blocks.text: 中文 · Overview and installation

rows: Share duplicate loads and remember misses briefly

sections.heading: Load missing values and cache misses

blocks.text: Install base tiers first, then add the cache through `host.use(cachePlugin(...))`. A loader's `undefined` result is cached only when `negativeTtlMs` is configured.

`getOrLoadEntry` also returns `tier`, `stale`, `negative`, `ageMs`, `meta` and `tags`. `peek()` never loads and returns `undefined` for a missing entry. `getOrLoadMany(keys, loader)` deduplicates keys, reads each tier in batches, and passes only missing keys without an existing shared load to the loader. Return a `ReadonlyMap<string, value | undefined>`.

`stampedeLock: { backend, timeoutMs? }` can select a tier with real transactions and key locks. It rechecks under the lock and writes the value and TTL in that transaction. The timeout defaults to `30000` milliseconds. Transaction replay may invoke the loader again; this does not guarantee exactly-once loading.

Ordinary `get/set` read and write plain string entries, not the encoded objects above. Keys must be strings. For a stable key derived from parameters, import `cacheKey` from the root and use `await cacheKey('profile', { id: 'ada', version: 1 })`. Unsupported input retains the serializer's original error.

Order `tiers` from fastest to slowest. Each tier defaults to `write: 'through'`. This complete example uses two independent memory instances; install SQLite, Redis or PostgreSQL under the same IDs when replacing them in an application.

Through writes settle from the slowest tier upwards. Hits in slower tiers promote values to faster ones. Back mode coalesces pending writes by key and processes them every `1000` milliseconds by default. Failed items are reported and dropped without retry. The slowest tier cannot use back. This example disables propagation to demonstrate back separately. With the default `propagate: true`, every tier above a change source needs TTL, and back tiers must be below all change sources and have TTL.

Subscriptions start during `detect()`. If a reliable source loses its cursor or the cursor expires, the cache clears the relevant upper prefix before continuing. Ordinary notifications also cannot update every copy simultaneously. Hard TTL bounds stale copies when a notification is missed. Dedicated backends or instances are recommended for cache data.

`prefix` defaults to `cache:<pluginID>:`. Choose distinct prefixes for independent caches sharing a data backend. `clock` defaults to `Date.now`, and `random` to `Math.random`; override them only when a controlled clock or jitter source is needed. `$cache.cursor` is reserved for propagation cursors, not business entries.

Cache has no cross-tier transactions. Tier failures are reported and degrade to misses or skipped writes. A successful call does not mean every copy is durable. For multi-tier prefix deletion, use `invalidate({ prefix: 'profile:' })` rather than the counted KV `removeByPrefix`.
This example demonstrates refresh and bypass without waiting for expiry. Refresh stores the new value; bypass returns its value only to that call.

rows: Hard expiry for that tier; needs backend TTL
Serve stale data while refreshing; must be below effective hard limits
Randomly shorten expiry to spread refreshes

blocks.text: Per-call `ttlMs/maxAgeMs/staleAfterMs/negativeTtlMs` may shorten configured bounds, never extend them. A positive per-call TTL requires TTL support in every target tier. The shared KV `setMany` TTL domain separately accepts zero to remove immediately.

A loader receives the cache-closing signal. `options.ctx.signal` cancels only that caller's wait with contract `ABORTED`, leaving other callers' shared load running. Respond to the loader signal so shutdown can drain promptly. A false `cacheIf(value)` skips all tier writes. Loader and encoding failures use `CACHE_LOAD_FAILED` and preserve the original cause; do not silently turn them into misses.

Tag indexes need records and TTL; offload storage needs blob, and its reference tier must have TTL. This complete example uses built-in memory capabilities. An application can replace the object tier with the object-storage plugin.

Encoded content at or above `minBytes` is stored under a content hash; the tier keeps a reference. Smaller values stay in the tier. `maxEntryBytes` can skip oversized entries for a tier. Tags are written before values; a failed tag-index write is reported and skips the value so it does not leave an untracked tagged entry.

Invalidation removes references rather than immediately deleting objects that another key may use. `sweepOffload()` collects objects after their retention period. A newly invalidated object may remain until the longest referring tier's TTL; invalidation does not promise immediate disk reclamation.

Import `semanticCacheFeature` from its separate entry and select it in the cache plugin's second argument. The two-dimensional embedding below demonstrates an exact repeated prompt. Use a real model in an application, with dimensions, metric and model version matching the collection.

The vector backend must be installed earlier and needs TTL support when semantic TTL is configured. Metric defaults to `cosine`; `dot` and `euclid` are also supported. Native engines determine scores and candidate order. Do not reuse a score threshold across metrics. `candidates` accepts `1` through `10`, defaulting to `1`. Optional `accept` runs in order; false continues, while a failed acceptance callback is reported and skips that candidate.

Payload fields support strings, finite numbers and booleans. `$cache.*` fields are reserved. Identical prompts with different payloads are stored separately. `getOrLoad` shares loads by organization, prompt and canonical payload; per-call TTL can only shorten the limit, `cacheIf` may prevent storage, and cancelling one caller does not affect others. Embedding failures use `CACHE_EMBED_FAILED`.

`invalidate(where, { count })` returns the vector backend's deletion count. The default is `precount`; `scroll` is also supported. Counts include matching expired points still physically stored and retain the backend's concurrency limits, rather than representing a global snapshot. Semantic APIs exist only when selected, under `api.semantic`; they add no cache transaction or vector-backend shutdown.

Use `host.org(uuid).backend('cache')` to route borrowed tiers and Feature APIs to that organization. Shutdown cancels shared loads, waits for work already started, flushes back writes once, and cancels subscriptions. It does not independently close borrowed tiers; the host closes installed backends. `stats()` returns counters only; tier failures reach the host report callback and cache hooks.

blocks.text: `root` 是非空目录路径，目录由插件专用。下面先写入并读取，再只在 etag 仍匹配时覆盖。
`ifNoneMatch: true` 只在不存在时创建；`ifMatch: etag` 只在当前标识相同才写，两者互斥。失败报 contract `WRITE_CONFLICT`，不覆盖现有内容。etag 应原样传回；文件 etag 由内容哈希生成，同字节内容的再次写入可能不改变它，因此不能检测仅 metadata 的每次变动。
本地驱动支持 Node、Bun、Deno，安装时选择对应文件适配。一个真实目录只允许本进程一个写实例，不能由多个进程共同写。插件可能清理自己的未完成文件，因此目录要可信且专用。内容与 metadata 通过一次指针替换同时可见，已打开读对象不受后续覆盖或删除影响；此保证不包含掉电耐久或跨进程锁。

`end` 省略时读到末尾，超出末尾会截短；`start` 超出大小或对象本身为空时返回空流。`info.size` 仍表示完整对象。需要持续消费时，使用 `object.stream().pipeTo(destination)`；不要再调用 `bytes()`。两种方式共享一次消费机会，第二次消费会拒绝。`bytes()` 会聚合所选内容，适合大小可控的读取。
EOF、流错误与 cancel 会释放底层读取。尚未消费、提前停止或异常退出时，仍用 `finally` 释放对象，或 `await using`。对象不能交给多个独立消费者。取消与超时通过 `options.ctx` 提供；上传的流也需要配合取消，不要无限阻塞生产者。

未知长度的流及达到阈值的字节数组使用 multipart。默认同时缓冲的上界为五段加输入当前块。上传失败会尝试清理未完成 multipart；清理失败经宿主 report 报告。修改请求局部禁用 SDK 重试与区域重定向，不改调用方 client 的全局配置，避免自动重放结果不明的提交。

items: This backend provides blob, not ordinary KV or transactions. Logical keys are strings, including the empty string. Metadata values are strings; S3 additionally requires lowercase HTTP-token names and ASCII header values without line breaks.

A real directory supports one writer instance in the current process. Sharing it across processes is unsupported. Keep it trusted and dedicated, without unrelated application files. Filesystem updates provide atomic visibility, not fsync-level power-loss durability. File etags are SHA-256 content hashes: the same bytes may retain an etag, so it is not an incrementing update version.

Missing `get/head` returns `undefined`. `remove` reports whether it observed an object before deleting. `stream/bytes` share one consumption right. EOF or cancellation releases the read; explicitly dispose unread or abandoned objects.
Range `start/end` are nonnegative safe integers; end is inclusive and optional. `info.size` remains the full size. A start beyond the content returns empty bytes, not an absent object.

`ifMatch` and `ifNoneMatch: true` are mutually exclusive. Failed conditions use `WRITE_CONFLICT`. S3 conditions require detection support and reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` when unavailable, without falling back to unconditional writes.

Object errors use `source: 'storage.backend.object'`. `OBJECT_DATA_INVALID` means corrupt data or incomplete responses; `OBJECT_COMMIT_UNKNOWN` means commit confirmation is unknown. `OBJECT_FAILED` may include `committed: true` when writing succeeded but follow-up metadata reading failed. Inspect state before retrying.

`host.org(uuid).backend('object').use(blob)` separates organizations. Host shutdown releases read resources and S3 clients created from config. A caller-supplied `S3Client` is always borrowed and must be closed by its caller.

blocks.text: `root` is a nonempty path to a dedicated directory. This example writes and reads content, then overwrites only while its etag still matches.

`ifNoneMatch: true` creates only if absent; `ifMatch: etag` writes only when the current identifier matches. They are mutually exclusive. A failed condition uses contract `WRITE_CONFLICT` without overwriting existing content. Pass the etag back unchanged. Filesystem etags are content hashes, so writing the same bytes may leave the etag unchanged; it cannot detect every metadata-only update.

The filesystem driver supports Node, Bun and Deno, selecting an adapter during installation. A real directory allows one writer in this process and cannot be shared by writing processes. Keep it trusted and dedicated because the plugin may reclaim its unfinished files. A single pointer replacement publishes bytes and metadata together; open read objects retain their content after overwrite or deletion. This does not provide power-loss durability or cross-process locking.
Uploads accept `Uint8Array` or an unlocked `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`; chunks must be byte arrays. Upload four bytes from a stream, then read inclusive range `[1, 2]`:

Omit `end` to read through EOF; ends beyond EOF are clipped. A start beyond the size or an empty object returns an empty stream. `info.size` still describes the full object. For continuous consumption use `object.stream().pipeTo(destination)`, then do not call `bytes()`. Both share one consumption right; consuming again rejects. `bytes()` collects the selected content and suits reads with bounded size.

EOF, stream errors and cancellation release the native read. Use `finally` or `await using` for unread objects, early exits and failures. Do not give one object to multiple independent consumers. Provide cancellation and timeout through `options.ctx`; stream producers must cooperate with cancellation rather than block indefinitely.

Create a bucket and configure credentials the SDK can resolve. This example assumes an `application-objects` bucket in `us-east-1` and uses the SDK's default credential chain rather than hard-coded secrets.

For compatible services, set `endpoint` and `forcePathStyle` in `config`. Choose exactly one of `client` and `config`. A supplied client is borrowed and never destroyed by the host; config creates a client during installation and destroys it during shutdown. `prefix` defaults to `''`. Logical keys are also encoded for organizations, so do not assume they equal raw bucket object names.

rows: `8388608` (8 MiB), safe integer at least `5242880` (5 MiB)

blocks.text: Unknown-length streams and byte arrays at or above the threshold use multipart. Default buffering is bounded by five parts plus the current input chunk. Failed uploads attempt to clean up incomplete multipart state; cleanup failures reach the host report callback. Mutation requests locally disable SDK retries and region redirects without changing the supplied client's global settings, avoiding automatic replay of uncertain commits.

Default environment detection starts with `HeadBucket`; failure prevents host creation. It then writes and deletes random probe objects under a reserved prefix to check conditions. Missing probe permissions or unsupported conditions are reported and leave conditional writes unavailable, rather than treating unconditional writes as conditional success. Actual unconditional operations still require service permissions. Conditional multipart also requires conditions on the final Complete request; unsupported services reject without fallback.

S3 metadata names must be lowercase HTTP tokens, and values must be ASCII without line breaks. Content type must also be a valid header value. Etags are opaque; updatedAt comes from native LastModified. Range reads verify Content-Range and length; incomplete responses are failures, not missing objects.
Signing is S3-only and requires explicit `objectPresignFeature()` selection. Generate an upload request constrained by content type; signing itself does not upload data.

Give the actual HTTP client the returned `url`, `method` and every header. Omitting content, metadata, condition or range headers changes the signed request. `expiresInSeconds` accepts integer seconds from `1` to `604800`, defaulting to `900`. Actual validity cannot exceed credential expiry. Uploads support the same conditions as `put`; downloads support inclusive ranges. Keep temporary signed URLs out of public logs.
Write two objects inside a new organization, then page with the returned cursor. Do not construct cursors or reuse them across organizations.

`list` defaults to prefix `''` and limit `100`. Limit must be a positive safe integer. Keys use UTF-16 lexical order; cursors bind to one installation, organization and prefix. Paging is not a snapshot across pages: concurrent writes can change later results. `removeByPrefix('')` clears only this organization and counts observed removals; it is not a cross-object transaction.

libraries.description: PostgreSQL storage backend with native transactions and optional pgvector

blocks.text: English
把 PostgreSQL 接到统一存储接口，避免文本、记录、过期时间和应用 SQL 分别提交时出现一半更新成功的情况。将已有客户端或连接池交给对应驱动，再把插件安装到 host，就能在同一数据库事务中组合这些操作；通知、逻辑复制和向量等能力按需选择，客户端仍由应用负责关闭。

不同租户用了相同的键：原生表缺少一致的租户过滤。
服务已停，连接池仍在等待：订阅和存储操作还没结束就关闭了客户端。
存储方法与 SQL 一起提交。 事务中的 KV、记录和 SQL 使用同一条数据库连接，见事务与组织隔离。
按需选择数据库功能。 COPY、通知、向量与可重放变更流分别导入，不选就不增加对应 API，见导入数据并发送通知。
能分清通知丢失和历史丢失。 普通通知不保证重放；逻辑复制提供检查点，并拒绝无法证明连续的历史，见持续读取变更。
批量接口保留输入含义。 批量读取保留顺序和重复位置，批量写入拒绝等价重复键；使用绑定数组，避免按键发起查询。这里不作速度比较。

逻辑复制的 `truncate` 默认 `reset`。根流遇到 TRUNCATE 后，每个提交只发一条无 `orgId` 的 `reset`，消费者必须让所有组织缓存失效；`block` 会停止且不确认该提交。检测报告延迟与 WAL 保留量；无限 WAL 保留会警告。没有持续流需求时，不要保留复制 slot，可使用 TTL 或定时同步；关闭 host 不会删除 slot。
English
先设置 `DATABASE_URL`。账号需要在所选 schema 创建存储表的权限。以下示例都是完整程序，会实际写库；涉及应用表或扩展时会先说明。总是先结束 host，再关闭自己创建的客户端。

流式导入并在提交后通知
从检查点继续处理失效信息

blocks.text: 这里写入一个固定组织。预期输出为 `ready`、`true`。
组织 ID 是 UUID 字符串。同名逻辑键、期限、锁和修订分别隔离；默认组织与其它组织共用物理表。`host.dropOrg(id)` 删除该组织的托管行，不删除其它组织或应用表。显式组织视图不允许任意 SQL、COPY 或自有向量表检索。
`getMany` 保留顺序、重复位置，缺失位置为 `undefined`。等价重复写键在 I/O 前拒绝。空批不做原生操作，也不调用 pipeline/hooks。省略 `ttlMs` 时保留活值的期限，新值没有期限；零立即过期。期限和锁使用数据库时钟。`counter.increment` 只接受规范十进制文本与安全整数，在写入前拒绝溢出。
默认根视图可使用 `store.sql`、`tx.sql` 访问应用表。插值是绑定参数；标识符使用 `@migaia/storage-host/authoring/sql` 的 `sqlFragment.id`。同一事务可以混用应用 SQL 与标准存储方法。应用表的租户过滤由调用方提供。记录字段查询在客户端求值，原生规范键范围限制扫描。
事务请求 READ COMMITTED，检测会报告实际隔离级别。40001/40P01 经确认回滚后可能重试：观察到的修订没变时内部重放，变了才进入所选冲突策略。回调可能再次执行，外部副作用没有恰好一次保证。COMMIT 发出后连接中断不会盲目重放；提交标记可证明已提交，查不到或读失败都不能证明零写入。
先配置 `vector` 扩展。这里还选择 `halfvec` 量化召回，必要时会准备表达式索引；数据库与扩展版本必须支持它。输出取决于实际 ANN 候选，不承诺命中数量。

新建集合需要 `dimensions` 和 `metric`。metric 为 `cosine`、`dot`、`euclid`，分数分别为 `1-distance`、`-distance`、`-distance`。原向量存为 FLOAT32。`near(query, { exact: true })` 只对当前读取禁用 ANN；显式接 `rescore` 则选择量化召回。没有 `rescore` 时使用数据库现有计划和索引，单选 pgvector 不创建 ANN 索引。
量化模式在安装时选 `halfvec` 或 `binary_quantize`。`topK(k)` 限定候选数，`rescore({ topN })` 按原向量精确重排这些候选。topN 默认 k，必须是正安全整数且不超过 k。结果可以选字段、分组、通用 rerank，但不能删除、监听或再次 rescore，也不会隐式补读向量。
组织、期限及可下推 payload 条件进入原生召回过滤。ANN 过滤不保证最终足 k 条。JS 谓词仅过滤实际命中，不补搜；`requirePushdown()` 在 I/O 前拒绝需要客户端求值的条件。量化可能损失精度或发生原生转换错误。halfvec 索引最多4000维，binary 索引最多64000维，但原 vector 列最多16000维；这是上限，不是推荐配置。
同 schema/prefix/name 的集合配置跨组织、host 共享。dropOrg 保留配置和表结构。托管 `deleteWhere` 返回实际删除行数，包括物理尚在的过期匹配点。独立的 `api.pgvector.search` 接受结构化自有表目标和原生计划选项，不会把应用表变成托管集合。
示例创建应用表，导入两行 CSV，并把存储状态与通知放在同一次提交中。连接正常收到通知时预期输出 `done`；LISTEN 断线期间可能丢通知。

COPY 使用结构化表名、列名和返回异步字节流的 source factory。每次真实尝试重新调用 factory，不要传已消费的流。CSV 默认逗号、`header: false`；text 默认 TAB，支持省略 header 或显式 header:false；header:true 会拒绝。服务器文件和 PROGRAM 不支持。失败时先排空原生 COPY，再回滚。事务有 notify 和 COPY，没有 listen。
通知 channel 为非空 UTF-8 名，最多63字节；payload 少于8000字节，两者均拒绝 NUL。listen 返回订阅资源，需要释放。通知只是变化提示，不能证明断线消费者收到了所有提交。
部署方先配置 `wal_level=logical`、REPLICATION 角色、持久 pgoutput slot 与 FOR ALL TABLES publication。把已有名称放入 `PG_REPLICATION_SLOT`、`PG_PUBLICATION`。该功能仅支持 PostgreSQL preset 的 `/pg` 驱动，检测不创建这些部署资源。
使用已有 slot 时，PostgreSQL 可能需要先读取保留的旧 WAL，tailChanges 才能完成启动，示例随后的写入也会等待。启动耗时取决于积压，请先检查 confirmedFlushLagBytes 和 retainedWalBytes；不要为运行示例重置或共用生产 slot。
示例从当前进度开始，清理应用缓存并把已处理失效信息追加到文件。文件追加失败会使回调拒绝。没有 orgId 的 reset 必须处理为全组织失效。
`truncate` 默认 `reset`。根流每个 TRUNCATE 提交只发一条无 orgId 的 `kind: 'reset'`，需要清除全部组织缓存；组织流得到该组织自己的 reset。其它无 orgId 的非 reset 事件不能自动当全局事件。选择 `truncate: 'block'` 时停止、报告且不确认该提交。

`onChange` 成功才允许确认；回调拒绝就停止，不确认该提交。轮询 `readChanges({ after, limit })` 返回 `{ changes, cursor }`。先完成派生写入，再保存 cursor，下次把已保存 cursor 传回 after，才确认完整进度。游标可能包含部分提交进度，不要解析、修改或自行加减位置。slot 丢失或历史不再可证明连续时抛 `CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED`，一个 slot 只允许一个活跃消费者。

`onCapabilityProbe` 带出十进制字符串 `confirmedFlushLagBytes`（当前 WAL 位置减已确认位置）、`retainedWalBytes`（当前位置减 slot restart 位置）及 `maxSlotWalKeepSize`。无限保留值 `-1` 经 reporter 发出警告，不使检测失败，也不修改服务端设置。延迟和保留量都要关注，断开的 slot 可能持续占用磁盘。
释放 tail 或 host 只结束复制连接，不关闭 pool、不删除 slot/publication。没有持续流需求时不要保留 slot，可用 TTL 或定时同步。删 slot 是单独的管理操作；`api.logicalReplication.dropSlot()` 存在，但不是默认清理步骤。
宿主默认自动检测。设置 autoDetect:false 后，使用所选功能前应先 await host.detect()；托管向量首次实际使用仍会检查扩展。

items: 默认 `server: 'postgres'`、schema `public`、prefix `migaia`；driver 必填。`maxLockMs` 默认60000ms并限定租约，`concurrency` 选择冲突策略。cockroach、yugabyte 需要实际服务检测；协议连接成功不等于 PostgreSQL 专属功能可用。
`/pg` 借用 Pool，`/postgres-js` 借用 postgres.Sql，`/bun` 借用 Bun 1.4.4+ 且 prepare:false 的 SQL。先结束 host，再关闭相应客户端。根入口不加载驱动；复制额外需要 Node 22+ 及声明的复制 peer。能力检查不表示每个服务和运行时组合都已实际验收。
文本、记录使用支持 Map/Set 的便携集合编码，字节复制。记录键用规范保序字节，其它通道用同一身份的 hex。文本/字节缺失为 null，记录/metadata 缺失为 undefined。私有表不能当应用 SQL 接口；JSONB payload 只是过滤投影。
SQL 的 int8 返回 bigint，numeric/date/JSON/array 保留原生文本，bytea 返回独立 Uint8Array。不安装全局 parser。postgres.js 字符串参数使用 TEXT，需要其它类型时由应用 SQL 显式转换。
本包错误 source 为 storage.backend.postgres，码为 SQL_FAILED、DECODE_FAILED、TRANSACTION_FAILED、DUPLICATE_KEY。校验、取消、期限和并发错误保留各自 source；原错误可沿 cause 或 aggregate errors 找到。观察回调错误只报告；要改变操作，请用 pipeline。
宿主 journal 显式启用日志。text/bytes/record/托管 vector 的完整镜像及绝对期限在数据事务内捕获；外置 binlog 在提交后追加并等待完成，失败只报告，不能撤回数据。完整镜像模式在执行前拒绝原生 SQL、COPY、自有向量表终点。
原生日志在每个数据库事务内串行更新 head/record，不跨操作缓存索引。外置 WAL 先写 intent，再随数据写独立 marker，重开时区分已提交和未完成修改。undo 仅在宿主支持的日志组合中出现，先锁定全部目标并核对完整修订和镜像，再恢复；组织重建不让旧镜像重新有效，缺少 birth 的旧镜像以 UNDO_CONFLICT 拒绝，不能跨组织恢复。
日志按执行顺序保留重复写和中间值。undo 核对最终修订、恢复原绝对期限，不刷新已过期期限。telemetry 独立启用，每个根操作或完整事务跨重试只发一条完成事件，不接管 logger；先释放 host，再释放 logger 及其载体。

blocks.text: 中文

Use PostgreSQL through one storage API when text, records, expiry and application SQL must commit together rather than leave half an update saved. Pass an existing client or pool to its driver and install the plugin in a host, then combine these operations in the same database transaction. Select notifications, logical replication or vectors separately when needed; your application still closes the client.

items: The order row exists but its status does not: the two writes committed separately.
A rebuilt cache still serves stale data: a notification channel was treated as replayable history.
Two tenants overwrite the same key: tenant filtering varies between queries.
Shutdown hangs: the client pool closes before subscriptions and storage work have finished.
Commit storage operations and SQL together. KV, records and SQL in a transaction use the same connection. See Transactions and organizations.
Add only the database features you need. COPY, notifications, vectors and replayable changes have separate imports and explicit selection. See Import and notify.
Know when history is no longer safe to resume. Notifications may be lost; logical replication supplies checkpoints and rejects unprovable gaps. See Follow committed changes.
Keep batch semantics clear. Reads retain input order and duplicates, while writes reject equivalent duplicate keys. Array parameters avoid issuing one query per key; no speed comparison is claimed.

Put changes that belong together inside `store.transaction`. Callback failure rolls them back. Keep email, payments and other external effects outside callbacks that may retry.

blocks.text: Defaults are `server: 'postgres'`, `schema: 'public'` and `prefix: 'migaia'`. `cockroach` and `yugabyte` require actual server detection. Only PostgreSQL provides the ordinary change notifications; Cockroach does not support this module's pgvector Feature. Wire compatibility does not verify every deployment combination.

Organizations share tables while isolating equal keys, expiry, locks and standard vector points. Raw SQL, caller-table vector search and COPY access application tables; explicit organization views reject those endpoints. See Behavior and limits for data types, concurrency, failures and journal restrictions.

Logical replication defaults to `truncate: 'reset'`. Root streams emit one reset without `orgId` per TRUNCATE commit: consumers must invalidate every organization. `block` stops without confirming that commit. Detection reports replication lag and retained WAL and warns about unlimited retention. Keep no replication slot when a live stream is unnecessary; TTL or periodic synchronization may suffice. Host disposal never removes a slot.
中文

Use a database account that can create the module's storage tables. Each example is a complete program; it writes to the database. Set `DATABASE_URL` first. Examples that create application tables or indexes state those requirements below. Dispose the host before closing the caller-created client.

Import bytes and notify after commit

blocks.text: This writes into one fixed organization. Expected output is `ready` followed by `true`.

Organizations use UUID strings. Equal logical keys, TTL, locks and revisions remain separate; the default organization shares the physical tables. `host.dropOrg(id)` removes that organization's managed rows, not other organizations or application tables. Organization views reject raw SQL, COPY and caller-table vector search.

`getMany` keeps order, duplicates and `undefined` for missing positions. Equivalent duplicate write keys reject before I/O. Empty batches perform no native operation or pipeline/hook work. Omitted `ttlMs` preserves a live deadline; a new value has no deadline. Zero expires immediately. TTL and locks use the database clock. `counter.increment` works on canonical decimal text and rejects unsafe integers before writing.

Use `store.sql` or `tx.sql` on the default root for application tables. Interpolated values are parameters, not SQL source; use `sqlFragment.id` from `@migaia/storage-host/authoring/sql` for identifiers. A root transaction may mix application SQL and standard storage methods. Supply your own tenant filters for application tables. Record query fields are evaluated by the shared client-side query code; native key ranges bound the scan.

Transactions request READ COMMITTED, and detection reports the actual isolation level. SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 can trigger replay after a confirmed rollback: unchanged observed revisions permit internal retry; changed revisions enter the selected concurrency policy. Callbacks may run again. Do not rely on exactly-once external effects. After COMMIT was sent, a connection failure never triggers blind replay. A transaction marker can prove commit; missing or unreadable evidence cannot prove no write occurred.

Provision the `vector` extension before selecting this Feature. The example also selects `halfvec` quantized recall and creates its expression index when needed; the database version and extension must support it. Its output depends on actual ANN candidates, rather than a promised result count.

`dimensions` and `metric` are required when creating a collection. Metrics are `cosine`, `dot` and `euclid`; scores are respectively `1-distance`, `-distance` and `-distance`. Points store FLOAT32 vectors. `near(query, { exact: true })` disables ANN for that read unless an explicit `rescore` stage selects quantized recall. Without `rescore`, existing database indexes and plans are used; plain pgvector selection does not create ANN indexes.

Quantization selects `halfvec` or `binary_quantize` once during installation. `topK(k)` bounds recall; `rescore({ topN })` reorders those candidates using original vectors. `topN` defaults to k and must be a positive safe integer no larger than k. Rescored queries can select fields, group and use generic rerank; they cannot delete, watch or rescore twice. No extra vector fetch is implied.

Organization, expiry and supported payload conditions appear in the native recall filter. ANN filtering does not guarantee k surviving hits. JavaScript predicates filter returned hits without refill. `requirePushdown()` rejects conditions that need client evaluation before I/O. Quantization may lose precision or reject native casts. Halfvec indexes allow up to 4000 dimensions; binary indexes up to 64000, while the original vector column allows up to 16000. These are limits, not recommended dimensions.

Collection configuration is shared across organizations and hosts using the same schema/prefix/name. `dropOrg` retains that configuration and table structure. Managed `deleteWhere` returns actual deleted rows, including expired matches that still physically exist. The separate `api.pgvector.search` accepts a structured caller-table target and native planner options; it does not turn application tables into managed collections.

The program creates an application table, imports two CSV rows and commits a storage status with the notification. Expected output is `done` when the connected listener receives the committed notification. LISTEN is a live channel and can be lost on disconnect.

COPY accepts structured table/column names and a source factory returning an async byte iterable. Each actual attempt calls the factory again; never pass a consumed stream. CSV defaults to comma and `header: false`. Text defaults to TAB. Omitted header and explicit header:false are supported; header:true rejects. Server files and PROGRAM are unsupported. On failure, native COPY drains before rollback. Transactions expose notify and COPY, but no listen method.

Notification channels are nonempty UTF-8 names of at most 63 bytes; payloads are below 8000 bytes. Neither accepts NUL. `listen` returns a subscription that must be disposed. Notifications are hints, not durable delivery or proof that a disconnected consumer saw every commit.

Prepare `wal_level=logical`, a REPLICATION role, a persistent pgoutput slot and a FOR ALL TABLES publication before installation. Set `PG_REPLICATION_SLOT` and `PG_PUBLICATION` to their existing names. Only the PostgreSQL preset with `/pg` supports this Feature. Detection checks those facts without creating deployment resources.

With an existing slot, PostgreSQL may need to read retained older WAL before tailChanges finishes starting, so the next write in this example also waits. Startup time depends on that backlog: inspect confirmedFlushLagBytes and retainedWalBytes first, and do not reset or share a production slot to run this example.

This example starts at the current position, invalidates application caches and appends each processed invalidation to a file. A failed append rejects the callback. It also shows the required handling of a reset that has no organization.

`truncate` defaults to `reset`. A root TRUNCATE produces exactly one `kind: 'reset'` without `orgId` for its commit; invalidate every organization's cached data. A routed organization feed gets its organization's reset. Do not treat every untagged non-reset event as a global event. With `truncate: 'block'`, the consumer stops, reports the condition and does not confirm the commit.

A successful `onChange` permits acknowledgement; rejection stops the stream without confirming that commit. For polling, `readChanges({ after, limit })` returns `{ changes, cursor }`. Commit derived effects and save `cursor` only after processing succeeds; pass that saved cursor as the next `after` to confirm completed progress. Cursors include complete or partial commit progress, so never parse, edit or advance them manually. Lost slots or expired/unprovable history raise `CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED`. One slot supports one active consumer.

`onCapabilityProbe` includes decimal-string `confirmedFlushLagBytes` (current WAL position minus confirmed progress) and `retainedWalBytes` (current WAL position minus the slot's restart position), plus `maxSlotWalKeepSize`. Unlimited retention (`-1`) sends a warning through the reporter; it does not fail detection or change server settings. Monitor both lag and retained WAL, because a disconnected slot can retain disk indefinitely.

Disposing the tail or host releases replication connections and leaves the pool, slot and publication intact. Keep no slot when a live stream is unnecessary; TTL or periodic synchronization can avoid that retained-WAL obligation. Slot removal is a separate intentional administrative action; `api.logicalReplication.dropSlot()` exists but is not a cleanup default.

Host detection runs automatically by default. If you set autoDetect:false, call await host.detect() before relying on the selected features. Managed vector endpoints still check the extension at first real use.

items: Defaults: `server: 'postgres'`, schema `public`, prefix `migaia`; `driver` is required. `maxLockMs` defaults to 60000 ms and bounds their lease, and `concurrency` selects conflict handling. `cockroach` and `yugabyte` require their actual detected server behavior; PostgreSQL-only features do not become available merely because the wire protocol connects.

Drivers: `/pg` borrows `Pool`; `/postgres-js` borrows `postgres.Sql`; `/bun` borrows Bun 1.4.4+ `SQL` configured with `prepare: false`. Close each SDK only after host release. The root imports none of them. Logical replication additionally uses Node 22+ and its declared `pg-logical-replication` peer. Server compatibility and adapter capability checks are not a promise that every runtime/server combination has been exercised.

Data: text/records use portable collection-aware codecs, including Map/Set. Bytes are copied. Record keys use canonical ordered bytes; other channels encode the same key identity as hex. Missing text/bytes return `null`; records/metadata return `undefined`. Private storage tables are not an application SQL API. JSONB payload columns support filters, not a different truth value.

SQL results: int8 is bigint; numeric/date/JSON/array retain native text; bytea becomes independent Uint8Array. No global parser is installed. postgres.js string parameters use TEXT; cast values explicitly in application SQL when another database type is required.

Errors: module failures use source `storage.backend.postgres` and `SQL_FAILED`, `DECODE_FAILED`, `TRANSACTION_FAILED` or `DUPLICATE_KEY`. Shared validation, cancellation, timeout and concurrency codes keep their own source. Original errors remain reachable through `cause` or aggregate `errors`. Observer failures are reported; use pipelines to change an operation.

Journals are opt-in through the host's `journal` option. Full text/bytes/record/managed-vector images and absolute expiry are captured in the data transaction. External binlog append happens after commit and is awaited; append failure reports but cannot roll back committed data. Full-image logging rejects raw SQL, COPY and caller-table vector endpoints before executing them.

Native log storage serializes head/record updates in each database transaction and does not cache an index between operations. External WAL writes intent first and a separate marker with the data; recovery distinguishes committed data from unfinished intent. Undo is available only for the supported host journal combination, locks every target and verifies complete revisions/images before restoring. Recreating an organization cannot make old undo images valid; old images without revision birth reject with `UNDO_CONFLICT`. Cross-organization restoration is not allowed.

Selected logs preserve repeated writes and intermediate values in execution order. Undo compares the final revision and restores original absolute deadlines; an expired deadline is not extended. Telemetry is separately opt-in, reports one completed root operation/transaction across retries and never takes ownership of the logger. Release the logger and its storage only after the host.

rows: Build standard queries from stored samples.
Delete by condition and return a numeric count.

blocks.text: The backend supplies `vector` and vector-target `ttl`. It has no KV, records, RDF, transactions, secondary indexes, change feed or native live query. Explicit locks and unsupported concurrency policies reject before mutation.

`url` is required. `id` defaults to `qdrant`, and `collectionPrefix` to `migaia_`. `apiKey` and a supplied `http` port are optional. Supplied HTTP/SDK clients remain with the caller and are never closed by the host. Hosts detect by default; if disabled, call `await host.detect()` first.

Error source is `storage.backend.qdrant`. Native 4xx, network/5xx failures and invalid responses use `QDRANT_REQUEST_FAILED`, `QDRANT_UNAVAILABLE` and `QDRANT_RESPONSE_INVALID`. Original errors remain on cause chains. Cancellation cannot undo a dispatched mutation; it is never replayed automatically, and disposal waits for its actual result. See the usage guide.

Start a real Qdrant service first. Examples default to `http://127.0.0.1:6333`; set `QDRANT_URL` for another service address. Each uses a fresh collection name and writes data. Host disposal does not delete collections.

rows: Set expiry or delete by condition

blocks.text: A category condition should run before ranking when possible. Client conditions can only remove hits already returned by the engine.
Expected output:

`dimensions` sets vector size. `metric` is cosine, dot or euclid. Omitting the whole options object reads an existing schema; a mismatch rejects. Constructing a collection performs no I/O. `exact` defaults to false; true requests native exact search. `topK(k)` requires a positive safe integer. Low-level `search(query, {k: 0})` returns no hits without sending a search.

`near` uses the supplied vector, `similarTo(id)` reads an original sample, and standard `recommend` uses the positive-sample mean minus the negative-sample mean. Cosine keeps search and original-sample slots so `withVector()` retains input magnitude within native float32 precision. Euclid distance is negated to produce score. Standard `groupBy` handles only the selected top-k hits.

Exactly expressible scalar equality, membership, existence and numeric ranges run in the engine. String ranges, substring/prefix conditions and function predicates run after ranking, without refill; fewer than k hits can remain. `explain()` identifies client work. `requirePushdown()` rejects it with QUERY_NOT_PUSHABLE before search I/O. Payloads cannot overwrite reserved root paths `$org` and `$expiresAt`. Portable payloads and arbitrary UTF-16 string IDs round-trip through the shared codec. Upsert validates the whole batch before I/O and keeps the last validated point for a repeated ID. Deletion and standard recommendation deduplicate IDs by first occurrence.
Persist a temporary point, then delete it through an explicit scan without relying on a timer firing at a particular instant.
Expected output:

blocks.code:
true
undefined
1

blocks.text: `ttlMs` is nonnegative milliseconds; 0 makes a point immediately invisible. Omission retains an active point's expiry; new or already-expired points become persistent. `expire` and `persist` return false for missing/expired points. `remaining` returns undefined for missing/persistent points. Only `lockKey.vector(collection, id)` targets are supported. Expiry uses the client wall clock, so skew matters. There is no background physical-deletion task.

Deletion includes expired points that physically remain. Default precount issues an exact count and a wait:true deletion with the same filter. Concurrent changes may make the count differ from the final deletion. scroll collects matching IDs before deleting them in batches and returns successfully committed IDs. Scanning is not a snapshot: new points may be seen or left behind, and collected IDs are deleted even if they later stop matching.

If a condition cannot be represented exactly, precount and management deleteByFilter reject with source `@migaia/storage-contract`, code UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY. Explicit `count: 'scroll'` supports common predicates by scanning this organization's candidates.
Recall candidates with standard vectors, then select final hits with an extra multivector slot.
Expected output:

blocks.code: b

blocks.text: At installation, collections maps logical names to extra slots. dimensions is required; metric defaults to cosine. `multivector: 'max_sim'` selects a nonempty matrix; omission selects dense vectors. Only declared collections are accepted. Updates and queries support two-row all-integer matrices. Both fetch and SDK adapters encode multivector numbers as float JSON literals such as `1.0`, preserving values, payloads and sparse indices.

updateVectors changes only the extra slot of existing points in the current organization, with wait:true. It returns a native operation result without changing standard vectors, payload or expiry. Duplicate IDs, empty/ragged matrices and invalid numbers reject before the request. Put rescore after topK(k). topN defaults to k and must be a safe integer from 1 through k. Each terminal uses one Query API request: prefetch uses the original search slot, organization, expiry, pushable conditions and minScore to recall k, then the outer query selects topN. Score is the final engine score. Function predicates filter outer hits without refill. withVector() still returns standard vectors; common rerank adds rerankScore separately.

Qdrant 1.15.5 requires the extra slot when a collection is first created. Missing/mismatched slots in older collections reject the new feature with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY. No collection is recreated and no data migrated; standard reads/writes remain available. Standard upsert replaces the whole point and may clear its extra slot, so update extra vectors afterwards.
The same logical ID can hold different vectors in two organizations. Organization filtering happens before ranking.

blocks.code:
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { vector } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { qdrantBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-qdrant'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [qdrantBackendPlugin({ url: process.env.QDRANT_URL ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:6333' })]
})
const name = 'guide_' + crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '')
const documents = host
  .backend('qdrant')
  .use(vector)
  .collection<{ category: string }>(name, { dimensions: 2, metric: 'dot' })
const tenant = host
  .org('11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111')
  .backend('qdrant')
  .use(vector)
  .collection(name, { dimensions: 2, metric: 'dot' })
await documents.upsert([{ id: 'a', vector: [1, 0] }])
await tenant.upsert([{ id: 'a', vector: [2, 0] }])
console.log((await documents.near([1, 0]).topK(1).all())[0]?.score)
console.log((await tenant.near([1, 0]).topK(1).all())[0]?.score)

blocks.text: Expected output:

Organization views share physical collections without creating collections/indexes per organization. dropOrg(id) discovers managed collections within collectionPrefix and removes only that organization's points, including expired ones. Shared collections and other organizations remain.
Pass Features as the factory's second argument to add methods under store.api. None has a transaction projection.

rows: qdrantHybrid.query requires exactly two named dense/sparse prefetch branches with rrf fusion. updateSparseVectors changes configured sparse slots only; indices are unique nonnegative integers with equally sized finite values.
qdrantRecommend.recommend preserves best_score, lookup and native sample strategies.
qdrantGroupBy.search preserves multivalue groups; SDK 1.11's unforwarded with_lookup option is absent.
Collections, aliases, snapshots and explicit deletion.

blocks.text: Self-managed native methods use physical collection names and are available only in the default organization. Management deleteByFilter(logicalCollection, where, options?, ctx?) and purgeExpired(logicalCollection, options?, ctx?) also work in organization views. The former does not add an active-point condition; the latter samples the wall clock once. Neither counts nor scrolls. Both return `{operationId, status}`; wait defaults to true. Filter deletion accepts weak, medium or strong ordering. An operationId is not a deletion count. Other methods retain native boolean/nullable snapshot results.

The root uses fetch by default. `/http` exports fetchHttp(url, apiKey?); `/client` exports qdrantClientHttp(client) for a real SDK client. Configuration and lifetime remain with the caller. SDK 1.11 has no per-call signal, so a dispatched request must settle. Fetch receives the operation signal. Closing rejects new calls and waits for actual requests and iterators. Detection checks methods needed for standard vector, TTL and organization cleanup. Optional native Feature methods are checked when called; a missing method rejects with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY before mutation.

Mutations are sent once without automatic retry or redirect following. Explicit 4xx errors use QDRANT_REQUEST_FAILED, network/5xx errors use QDRANT_UNAVAILABLE, and invalid responses use QDRANT_RESPONSE_INVALID, all with source storage.backend.qdrant. HTTP retains available status/body evidence. For a nonwaiting snapshot with HTTP 202, SDK 1.11 may discard status and truncate the message. response-invalid then does not establish rejection; fetch returns native null. Inspect native state before deciding to retry.

Hooks observe only; their throws/rejections are reported without cancelling the operation. Use the host pipeline to change behavior. Telemetry contains neither authentication headers nor request bodies. Only reserved organization/expiry paths are guaranteed indexes. Dynamic payload paths may be unindexed; cost depends on the engine plan, candidate count and transferred bytes.

blocks.text: English
把 Redis 或 Valkey 接到统一存储接口，集中处理组织键、过期时间、记录查询和显式键锁，减少业务代码逐次拼接物理键和补写期限的负担。选择已连接客户端对应的驱动并安装插件后，可按需增加 Streams、限流或向量检索；可用能力取决于服务模块与驱动，Redis 的事务部分失败限制仍然适用。

blocks.text: 预期输出 `active`、`1`。锁显式保护同一逻辑键，组织使用 UUID。
普通覆盖保留活值 TTL，expire(0) 立即删除，期限与锁使用 Redis TIME/PTTL。小数毫秒向上取整；超出安全整数的绝对期限在 EXEC 前拒绝。getMany 保留输入顺序、重复与缺失位置；批量写拒绝规范等价重复键，空批零命令。标准 KV、记录、TTL、counter 都可在 tx 中使用；字节和文本、记录分别保存。

组织共用带 hash tag 的物理命名空间，相关键同槽；同名逻辑键、期限、修订和锁隔离。prefix 默认 migaia，maxLockMs 默认30000；concurrency 选择冲突策略。dropOrg 删除该组织标准数据及既有 Streams、sorted-set、限流和向量点，即使重启后没再选择对应 Feature；保留其它组织、调用方非托管键和共享检索 schema。clearAll 仍只清标准通道。
事务读取不会自动加逻辑锁；显式 lock 才创建 SET NX PX 锁。普通写沿所选并发策略处理。WATCH 在依赖读取前建立，数据、索引、修订和通知进入同一 EXEC。回调在 EXEC 前失败时不写入；EXEC 返回 null 才是已确认的 WATCH 放弃，可按冲突策略重试。
EXEC 逐项失败可能部分提交，发送后断连可能结果未知。这两者都不自动重放，并封闭这次安装的新写入；读取和释放仍可用。不能把 transactions:true 理解成原生错误后完整回滚。不要把外部副作用放进可能重试的回调。
下面显式安装四个 Feature，实际写入 Stream、榜单与限流键，并发送一条消息。新命名空间首次运行通常输出 true、Ada、true、3；重复运行时已有队列内容或未到期配额可改变前几项结果。

rows: add/range/createGroup/readGroup/ack/autoClaim；range默认-/+、count100，group默认0-0与createStream:true，读取count100，省略block不等待
publish/subscribe/keyspace；二进制消息用规范base64文本传输，keyspace仅expired/del/set，回调收到实际物理键的UTF-8字节
add/rank/top；有限score，top默认10条升序，同分按逻辑UTF-16键序，空add零命令
limit/windowMs正安全整数，consume默认cost1；拒绝不增加计数，resetAfterMs来自PTTL

blocks.text: 这些原生 API 出现在 store.api，不在 tx.api。Streams 与 PubSub 各有自己的消息语义，不会自动成为标准提交日志。订阅需要专用真实连接；先释放订阅，再释放 host 和 SDK。Keyspace 过滤命名空间与组织，但不会替你开启服务器通知配置。
Streams group 阻塞读取使用专用连接，每次原生 BLOCK 最多1000ms；只有空结果才继续等待，原生错误直接拒绝。取消或关闭要等当前阻塞片结束。PubSub 回调拒绝只报告，不能撤回已提交的发布。
显式选择 change-stream，让标准写入与历史 XADD 进入同一 EXEC。示例从当前高水位开始，等待一次标准提交，打印服务给出的 cursor；其值由服务决定。
maxLen 必须是正安全整数，使用原生近似 MAXLEN 裁剪。readChanges({after,limit}) 默认limit100，从排他游标读起。处理效果和检查点应在回调成功前完成；tail 只在 onChange 成功后推进，失败报告并关闭，不越过失败项。游标是原生 Stream ID，按原样保存，不转成不精确的 JS number。
非初始游标落后于保留首项时报 CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED。0-0 也不是“忽略丢失历史”：只有 XINFO 证明从未移除记录时可继续，裁剪后同样拒绝。跨裁剪边界保守拒绝。这份历史只覆盖标准库提交，不承诺外部原生命令或纯自然过期事件；普通 best-effort 变更提示也不能代替它。

sections.heading: 使用 Search 向量检索

blocks.text: 需要真实 Search 模块和二进制 connection/EXEC 端口。部分 Redis 8部署包含 Search，缺模块的 Valkey 会拒绝该 Feature。Bun 内置驱动缺少二进制端口，不能使用此例；基础 KV 不受影响。预期输出 guide。
新集合给 dimensions/metric，随后连接通过 FT.INFO 读取实际配置。默认近邻索引用HNSW，exact:true用FLAT；相同FLOAT32字节进入两组字段。cosine/dot分数为1-distance，euclid为-sqrt(distance)。FLOAT32溢出、转换后为零的cosine方向在修改前拒绝。
组织TAG、期限NUMERIC在KNN排名中过滤；可忠实表达的scalar条件下推，其它条件或函数仅过滤引擎命中，不补搜。requirePushdown在I/O前拒绝客户端条件，minScore是有界客户端阈值。payload保留完整便携编码，scalar索引字段按需通过FT.ALTER增加。相似/推荐查询读取指定样本后生成方向，不保证其它候选被补搜。

Search 的TAG token上限4096字节。超过上限的规范等值/成员条件不承诺下推；普通where仍可过滤topK命中，requirePushdown报QUERY_NOT_PUSHABLE；deleteWhere与原生search.filter在I/O前报UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY。完整payload、ID与物理键不截断。样本排除使用SHA-256短TAG，不承诺数学上零碰撞。

vector TTL使用同一WATCH/EXEC：TIME生成绝对期限，HASH字段与PEXPIREAT一起写，普通upsert保期限，persist同时清期限字段和原生expiry。根与真实事务TTL都接受vector target，但向量集合不因此获得通用事务能力。deleteWhere默认precount，两种count模式都分页找点后实际删除，只返回存在并提交删除的数量；原生已过期HASH不计数。
宿主默认自动检测。设置 autoDetect:false 时，使用所选后端能力前先 await host.detect()。版本满足不等于安装了 Search 模块。

nodeRedisDriver接受node-redis 6的pool；ioredisDriver接受ioredis 6 client；bunRedisDriver接受Bun RedisClient，分别从/node-redis、/ioredis、/bun导入。它们借用已连接客户端，不关闭原对象。ioredis内部连接禁用未确认命令重发；node-redis保留同一pool租约和EXEC逐项错误；Bun在MULTI前拒绝二进制输入。根入口不加载SDK，每个订阅消耗独立连接。
标准记录字段查询在客户端执行，不提供标准secondaryIndexes、SQL或RDF。文本/字节缺失为null，记录为undefined。物理索引可能残留已过期条目，读取会核对真实键；前缀删除使用有序索引，inspectLocks和部分清理需SCAN，成本包含实际扫描候选。

本包错误source为storage.backend.redis，REDIS_FAILED表示原生命令/连接/EXEC故障，TRANSACTION_FAILED表示未分类的业务回调/草稿失败，DECODE_FAILED表示协议或持久化数据不能解码。共享契约、host和本包已有错误保留身份，原始错误沿cause可达。dispose重复返回同一主Promise，符号释放用另一个报告型Promise，只清理自有订阅和租约。
host journal可以选择提交后外置binlog和遥测。只有EXEC全部成功才追加成功提交日志；原生部分错误或未知结果不追加、不重放。binlog失败经report报告，不能撤回已提交数据，外置日志与业务数据并非强原子提交。标准值、字节、记录与向量的镜像保留实际wire和绝对期限；历史向量完整before镜像需要二进制端口，缺少时此日志组合在修改前拒绝。

此后端明确nativeAtomic:false。要求同EXEC强原子binlog、WAL intent/marker或undo的组合当前拒绝，不得当作已支持能力。storageLogStore单独从`@migaia/storage-host/journal`导入，每次在原生命名空间读当前索引；多个实例可共用namespace和连续序号，不跨操作缓存索引。原生Feature API不冒充标准业务通道的日志来源。遥测显式启用，根操作和完整事务跨重试各记一次；logger及载体仍由调用方在host之后释放。
中文

Use Redis or Valkey through one storage API that handles organization keys, expiry, record queries and explicit key locks, reducing repeated key-prefix and expiry code. Choose a driver for your connected client or pool, install the plugin, and add Streams, rate limiting or vector search when needed. Available capabilities depend on the server modules and driver; Redis transaction partial-failure limits still apply.

items: Tenant caches overwrite each other: raw keys lack consistent organization prefixes.
Updating a live value removes its expiry: value and TTL were written separately.
MULTI reports an error but data changed: an EXEC item error is not a rollback.
Reconnected consumers miss changes: Pub/Sub was treated as retained history.
Keep logical keys and organizations consistent. Text, bytes and records use separate physical keys while equal keys in different organizations remain isolated. See Organization data with expiry.

Submit standard mutations in one EXEC. Values, indexes, revisions and notifications share the commit, with identifiable input failures checked first. Redis's partial-failure limits still apply. See Transactions and concurrency.
Choose live hints or retained history deliberately. Pub/Sub serves online listeners; the change Stream can resume from a cursor. See Resume change history.

Use capabilities the server actually has. Vector selection checks the Search module and binary driver ports instead of silently replacing native search with local computation. No performance comparison is claimed.

blocks.text: A capability token selects standard methods; a Feature adds optional methods. WATCH detects changes after a read. EXEC executes queued commands, but one command's failure does not undo successful commands.

blocks.text: The module is currently `private: true` for this repository's workspace. Public registry availability is not implied. Link workspace dependencies from a consuming workspace module, then install the SDKs you use:

pnpm add redis ioredis

blocks.text: The root entry loads no SDK. ioredis and node-redis provide binary commands/EXEC. The Bun adapter has no binary port: basic KV remains available, but Search vectors cannot be selected. Each subscription needs its own connection; leave pool capacity for both subscriptions and business operations. Exact peer ranges are in module.json.

Prefix defaults to migaia and maxLockMs to 30000. Ordinary overwrites retain TTL; deadlines and locks use Redis time. Standard record queries evaluate on the client. Standard secondary indexes, SQL and RDF are absent. Organization views use the same namespace mapping; dropOrg also removes that organization's supported persistent Feature data.

Ordinary change hints are best effort, without external-command coverage, reconnect replay or instant expiry notification. Search requires the real module; connecting to Valkey does not imply vector support. EXEC item failures and disconnects after send can leave partial or unknown writes. New writes are then sealed rather than silently retried. See Transactions and concurrency.
中文

These complete programs need Redis 7.2+ or Valkey 7.2.5+ and REDIS_URL. Set REDIS_SEARCH_URL for the vector example to a service that actually provides Search. Programs write data. Release the host before closing its caller-created pool.

rows: Sessions, expiry, counters and tenant isolation
Application queues, messages, rankings or quotas

blocks.text: Expected output: active, then 1. The explicit lock protects a logical key; organization IDs are UUIDs.

Overwriting a live value retains TTL; expire(0) deletes immediately. Expiry and locks use Redis TIME/PTTL. Fractional milliseconds round up; unsafe absolute deadlines reject before EXEC. getMany retains order, duplicates and missing positions. Batch writes reject equivalent duplicate keys; empty batches issue no commands. Standard KV, records, TTL and counters also work on tx. Text, bytes and records use separate channels.

Organizations share a hash-tagged physical namespace so related keys stay in one cluster slot. Keys, expiry, revisions and locks remain organization-specific. Prefix defaults to migaia, maxLockMs to 30000; concurrency selects a conflict policy. dropOrg removes the organization's standard data plus existing Streams, sorted-set, quota and vector points, even if a later installation no longer selects those Features. It retains other organizations, unmanaged application keys and shared Search schemas. clearAll keeps its standard-channel scope.

Transaction reads do not automatically lock keys. Explicit lock uses SET NX PX; ordinary writes use the selected concurrency policy. WATCH starts before dependent reads. Values, indexes, revisions and notifications enter one EXEC. A callback failure before EXEC writes nothing. Only a native null EXEC proves a WATCH abort and can enter ordinary conflict retry handling.

An EXEC item error may leave partial writes. A disconnect after sending EXEC may leave an unknown result. Neither is automatically replayed; new writes for that installation are sealed while reads and disposal remain available. transactions:true is not a promise of complete rollback after native execution errors. Keep external effects outside callbacks that may retry.

The program selects four Features and writes a Stream entry, ranking, quota and message. In a fresh namespace, typical output is true, Ada, true,3. Existing entries and an unexpired quota can affect later runs.

rows: add/range/createGroup/readGroup/ack/autoClaim; range-/+ and count 100; group 0-0 with createStream:true; read count 100, nonblocking when block is omitted
publish/subscribe/keyspace; binary messages use canonical base64 text; keyspace supports expired/del/set and returns actual physical-key UTF-8 bytes
add/rank/top; finite scores, ascending top 10, UTF-16 logical-member order for ties, no command for empty add
positive safe limit/windowMs, consume cost 1 by default; rejection does not increase the count, resetAfterMs comes from PTTL

blocks.text: These APIs appear on store.api, not tx.api. Application Streams and Pub/Sub retain their own delivery semantics and do not automatically become standard commit logs. Subscriptions need dedicated real connections. Release the subscription, then the host, then the SDK. Keyspace notifications filter the namespace/organization without changing server notification configuration.

Blocking group reads hold a dedicated connection. Each native BLOCK is at most 1000 ms; only empty replies continue waiting. Native failures reject immediately. Cancellation and disposal drain the current blocking slice. Pub/Sub callback rejection only reports and cannot undo a committed publication.
Select change-stream so standard writes and history XADD share one EXEC. This starts at the actual high-water position, waits for a standard commit and prints its server-assigned cursor.

maxLen is a positive safe integer and uses native approximate MAXLEN trimming. readChanges({after,limit}) defaults to 100 and reads after the exclusive cursor. Finish derived effects and checkpoint persistence before a tail callback succeeds. Tail advances only after onChange succeeds; rejection reports and closes without skipping the failed item. Cursors are native Stream IDs; preserve strings rather than converting them into imprecise numbers.

A noninitial cursor behind retained history raises CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED. 0-0 does not bypass lost history: it resumes only when XINFO proves nothing has been removed, and rejects after trimming. Crossing a trim boundary also rejects conservatively. This history covers standard library commits, not external native commands or immediate natural-expiry events. Ordinary best-effort change hints cannot replace it.

The service needs the actual Search module and the driver needs binary connection/EXEC ports. Some Redis 8 deployments include Search; a Valkey deployment without the module rejects this Feature. Bun's adapter lacks those binary ports, so it cannot run this example, while its basic KV remains available. Expected output: guide.

New collections specify dimensions and metric; later connections read the real schema through FT.INFO. Approximate search uses HNSW; exact:true uses FLAT. Both fields receive identical FLOAT32 bytes. Cosine/dot score is 1-distance; Euclidean score is -sqrt(distance). FLOAT32 overflow and cosine directions that become zero after conversion reject before modification.

Organization TAG and expiry NUMERIC filters apply inside native KNN ranking. Faithful scalar conditions push down; other conditions and functions filter engine hits without refill. requirePushdown rejects client conditions before I/O; minScore is a bounded client threshold. Full payloads retain portable encoding while scalar index fields are added with FT.ALTER. Similar/recommend reads the specified samples, constructs a direction and uses the same native query without promising extra candidates.

Search TAG tokens are limited to 4096 bytes. Longer canonical equality/member conditions are not declared pushable. Ordinary where can still filter topK hits; requirePushdown raises QUERY_NOT_PUSHABLE, and deleteWhere/native search.filter raise UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY before I/O. Full payloads, IDs and physical keys are not truncated. Sample exclusion uses SHA-256 short TAGs without promising mathematically collision-free identity.

Vector TTL uses the same WATCH/EXEC path: Redis TIME supplies an absolute deadline, HASH metadata and PEXPIREAT change together, ordinary upsert retains expiry, and persist clears both deadline fields and native expiry. Root and real transaction TTL accept vector targets; collections do not gain general transaction support. deleteWhere defaults to precount. Both count modes page through actual points before deletion and return only existing committed deletions. Already expired native HASHes do not count.
Host detection runs automatically by default. With autoDetect:false, await host.detect() before using the selected backend capabilities. A version check does not imply a Search module is installed.

nodeRedisDriver accepts a node-redis 6 pool; ioredisDriver accepts an ioredis 6 client; bunRedisDriver accepts Bun RedisClient. Import them from /node-redis, /ioredis and /bun. Inject connected clients; the adapters never close the supplied root object. Owned ioredis connections disable replay of unacknowledged commands. node-redis retains one pool lease and per-item EXEC errors. Bun rejects binary input before MULTI. The root entry loads no SDK; reserve one connection per subscription.

Standard record field queries run on the client. Standard secondary indexes, SQL and RDF are absent. Missing text/bytes return null; missing records return undefined. Native indexes can retain expired entries and reads check actual keys. Prefix deletion uses an ordered index; lock inspection and some clearing use SCAN, whose cost includes real candidates visited.

module failures use source storage.backend.redis: REDIS_FAILED for commands/connections/EXEC, TRANSACTION_FAILED for uncategorized business callback/draft failures, DECODE_FAILED for malformed replies or stored data. Existing shared, host and Redis errors retain identity and the original error remains reachable through cause. Repeated dispose returns one main Promise; symbolic release has a separate report-only Promise. Cleanup releases only subscriptions and leases the adapter created.

Host journal configuration supports post-commit external binlog and telemetry. A success log is appended only after every EXEC item succeeds; partial or unknown outcomes do not append success or replay. Binlog failure reports but cannot roll back committed data: external append is not atomic with business writes. Standard values, bytes, records and vector images retain actual wire values and absolute expiry. Complete before images for historical vector deletion require binary ports; without them that logging combination rejects before modification.

The backend declares nativeAtomic:false. Combinations requiring strongly atomic binlog in the same EXEC, WAL intent/marker or undo currently reject and must not be treated as supported. Import storageLogStore separately from `@migaia/storage-host/journal`; it reads the current private index for every operation. Multiple instances may share a namespace and sequence without a cross-operation index cache. Native Feature APIs are not standard business-channel journal sources. Telemetry is opt-in and records each root operation or whole transaction once across retries. The application releases its logger and log storage after the host.

libraries.description: Native RDF and SPARQL protocol storage backend

blocks.text: 把 RDF 数据写入远程 SPARQL 端点或本地 Oxigraph，并用查询链读取、筛选和修改四元组，也就是包含主语、谓词、对象和图的数据。选择 HTTP 或 Oxigraph 适配后安装插件，应用可用 RDF 值构造查询，并通过 `expect` 声明提交时必须仍存在的四元组；网络写入结果未知时不会自动重试。

items: 拼接查询遇到引号就坏掉，把数据当作 SPARQL 语法插入。
两个请求都读到旧值后分别改名，误以为同一谓词天然只有一个值。
HTTP 写入超时后重试，第一次其实已经提交。
导入多个 RDF 文档后 blank node 混在一起，忽略了其文档内身份。
`term` 与模板绑定区分 RDF 数据和查询语法，见HTTP 读写。
`expect` 显式声明读到的四元组，让条件提交检测真实竞争，见检测并发修改。
图文档使用真实 RDF parser/writer，跨文档 blank node 分别命名，见图文档与本体。
结果未知的写入不会自动重放；原生拒绝、读取失败与提交未知分别报告，见失败与释放。

blocks.text: 下面使用真实 Oxigraph Store，写一条姓名四元组，再按主语读回数量。

blocks.code:
import { Store } from 'oxigraph'
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { rdf } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { term } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/rdf'
import { sparqlBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql'
import { oxigraphEndpoint } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql/oxigraph'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [sparqlBackendPlugin({ endpoint: oxigraphEndpoint(new Store()) })]
})
const store = host.backend('sparql')
const quad = {
  subject: term.iri('urn:example:alice'),
  predicate: term.iri('urn:example:name'),
  object: term.literal('Alice'),
  graph: term.defaultGraph
}
await store.use(rdf).add([quad])
console.log(await store.use(rdf).match({ subject: quad.subject }).count())

直接拼文本和发送 HTTP 还要自己处理数据转义和提交确认。这里只展示，不执行。

处理应用可直接比较的四元组。
带 term 绑定的原生 SELECT、ASK、CONSTRUCT、UPDATE。

blocks.text: raw SPARQL 是直接表达原生查询语句的模板。四元组包含主语、谓语、宾语和图。ground quad 指不含 blank node 或变量的可稳定命名四元组。组织视图把逻辑图映射到各自的真实命名图。

blocks.text: 当前包为 `private: true`，用于本仓库 workspace，不能假定 registry 已发布。从同一 workspace 的应用目录安装相邻包及真实 peers：

blocks.text: 需要 Node.js 24 或更新版本。根入口不加载 Oxigraph 原生运行代码；`/oxigraph` 显式选择真实 Store，`/http` 使用运行时 fetch。RDF 解析使用 n3，声明来自真实 RDF/JS 依赖。

rows: 安装一个端点，id 默认 sparql。

blocks.text: 提供 RDF、SPARQL 和原生乐观事务，不提供 KV、records、vector、SQL 或键锁。标准 RDF 仅接受命名主语/谓语、命名或字面量宾语、缺省或命名图。raw SELECT/CONSTRUCT 和文档另支持 blank node；RDF-star、文档变量与标准 blank quad 拒绝。推理由数据库承担。
endpoint 与 Store 由调用方管理，host 不关闭它们。Oxigraph 0.4.11 的公开 Store 类型没有 close/dispose 方法，无需编造一个；远程连接池的释放遵循调用方客户端 API。host 关闭拒绝新调用、取消活动读取并等待已发提交。
没有 `expect` 时只保证规范四元组的集合成员修改；不同宾语可同时存在，不提供谓词单值覆盖。HTTP 部署须保证单条条件 Modify 原子执行和同 dataset 的写后读可见性，协议本身不能证明这一点。原生错误域、提交未知和图文档边界见使用指南。

rows: 使用远程 SPARQL 服务

blocks.text: 此例写入两条姓名，再只删除 Alice。

blocks.code:
import { Store } from 'oxigraph'
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { rdf } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { term } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/rdf'
import { sparqlBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql'
import { oxigraphEndpoint } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql/oxigraph'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [sparqlBackendPlugin({ endpoint: oxigraphEndpoint(new Store()) })]
})
const store = host.backend('sparql')
const quad = {
  subject: term.iri('urn:example:alice'),
  predicate: term.iri('urn:example:name'),
  object: term.literal('Alice'),
  graph: term.defaultGraph
}
await store
  .use(rdf)
  .add([quad, { ...quad, subject: term.iri('urn:example:bob'), object: term.literal('Bob') }])
const selected = store
  .use(rdf)
  .match({ predicate: quad.predicate })
  .where((value) => value.object.value === 'Alice')
console.log(await selected.count())
console.log(await selected.delete())
console.log(await store.use(rdf).match({}).count())

blocks.text: 预期输出：
quad 的 subject/predicate 用命名节点，object 用命名节点或字面量，graph 用缺省图或命名节点。`term.literal` 支持 language 或 datatype；term 绑定负责转义。标准 API 不接受 blank node 或变量。
`match(pattern)` 的 pattern 是 quad 字段子集。查询链支持 where、follow/inverse、orderBy、distinct、skip、limit、分页、聚合和 stream。`explain()` 区分原生步骤与客户端步骤；`requirePushdown()` 对不支持的客户端步骤在请求前拒绝。
`delete` 对实际选中、接受修改的规范 quad 去重计数；`replace(old, new)` 仅替换选中的 old，未选中返回 0。根调用等提交确认后才返回；事务内数量描述当前修改草稿。
先声明 Alice 仍存在，再把它改为 Ada。若另一个事务移除了 Alice，这次提交会冲突。

blocks.code:
import { Store } from 'oxigraph'
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { rdf } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { ConcurrencyPolicy } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/concurrency'
import { term } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/rdf'
import { sparqlBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql'
import { oxigraphEndpoint } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql/oxigraph'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [sparqlBackendPlugin({ endpoint: oxigraphEndpoint(new Store()) })]
})
const store = host.backend('sparql')
const quad = {
  subject: term.iri('urn:example:alice'),
  predicate: term.iri('urn:example:name'),
  object: term.literal('Alice'),
  graph: term.defaultGraph
}
await store.use(rdf).add([quad])
await store
  .tx()
  .concurrency(ConcurrencyPolicy.optimistic({ retries: 1 }))
  .run(async (scope) => {
    scope.use(rdf).expect([quad])
    await scope.use(rdf).delete([quad])
    await scope.use(rdf).add([{ ...quad, object: term.literal('Ada') }])
  })
console.log((await store.use(rdf).match({}).all()).map((value) => value.object.value).join(','))

blocks.text: 预期输出：

blocks.code: Ada

blocks.text: `expect` 条件按合取检查；`expectAbsent` 要求各 quad 不存在。草稿按规范 quad 身份去重，同一 quad 最后成员操作生效。未声明前提的读取不会自动成为读集；两个事务分别插入不同宾语时可同时保留，不提供谓词单值覆盖。
`ConcurrencyPolicy.optimistic({retries: 1})` 最多重试一次真实冲突；callback 可能重新执行，外部副作用应放在事务成功之后。backoffMs 默认 20；省略策略时不自动启用乐观重试。只支持乐观并发，不支持键锁、wait/fail 策略或交互式远程事务。
一次条件 DELETE/INSERT WHERE 同时写用户数据和提交 marker，随后 ASK 确认，再清理 marker。只有 Update 成功且 ASK 明确 marker 不存在才是可重试的冲突。已发送 Update 结果未知、ASK 失败或取消为 SPARQL_COMMIT_UNKNOWN；停止该后端后续写入，不重放。清理 marker 失败只 report，用户数据已提交。
有 atomicUpdate 的端点才可在事务内执行一个 raw update body，不能混 RDF 操作/前提或第二个 raw body。Oxigraph 提供一次原生 Store.update；httpEndpoint 不提供此能力，在写入前拒绝。raw 事务模板只提供 update，不提供 select/ask/construct。

先运行支持 SPARQL Query 与 Update 的真实服务。示例默认连接本机 3030 端口的 `storage` dataset；地址不同时，设置 `SPARQL_QUERY_URL`、`SPARQL_UPDATE_URL` 和 `SPARQL_GRAPH_STORE_URL`，三者应指向同一 dataset。Graph Store URL 供图文档操作使用。此例先插入再 ASK，写入的数据会留在服务中。
预期输出：

blocks.code: true

blocks.text: queryUrl/updateUrl 必填，graphStoreUrl 仅图文档功能需要。URL 为不含内嵌凭据的绝对 HTTP(S)。可选 auth 精确选择 `{basic: {user, password}}` 或 `{bearer}`。修改请求一次发送，不跟随重定向；读取沿 fetch 行为。Graph Store HEAD404 返回 false，GET404 拒绝。认证头不进入诊断数据。
根 raw tag 支持 select、ask、construct、update。普通字符串是数据，不应作为语法插入；用 term 绑定 RDF 参数。raw SELECT/CONSTRUCT 支持结果内 blank node，标识仅限同一响应。
部署须保证单条条件 Modify 原子执行、同 dataset 写后读可见。已覆盖 Fuseki 6.2.0、Oxigraph 0.4.11 的原生路径，其他部署需确认等价保证；HTTP 协议不等于数据库事务。
写入一个图，导出后按 replace 再导入；所有操作都来自本例安装的 Feature。
预期输出：

blocks.code:
true
true
1
false

blocks.text: target 精确选择 `{default: true}` 或 `{graph: namedNode}`。document 的 format 是 text/turtle 或 application/n-triples，text 是完整文档。get/export 默认 Turtle。Graph Store 提供 getGraph、putGraph、mergeGraph、removeGraph、hasGraph；ontology 提供 importOntology/exportOntology。import mode 默认 merge，replace 替换真实单图；返回解析条数，含重复，不是新增数。
n3 处理 RDF1.1 文档语法。同一文档的 blank node 共享身份，不同导入重新命名。拒绝 RDF-star 和文档变量，不执行推理。端点须实际提供 graphStore；Feature 方法在 store.api；组织视图仍按自身图映射执行，事务内没有图文档 API。
`host.org(id).backend('sparql')` 将 default/named 逻辑图映射到 `urn:migaia:org:<orgId>:` 下的真实命名图。不同组织隔离；dropOrg 删除目标组织全部物理图，包括空命名图与含 blank node 的文档。raw SPARQL 只允许配置的默认组织。
标准 RDF、图文档和 ontology 禁止操作 `urn:migaia:commit` 保留图。进程崩溃可能留下 marker；管理员确认没有活动提交后才可在数据库执行 `CLEAR SILENT GRAPH <urn:migaia:commit>`。绕过标准 API 修改该图会破坏提交确认。

错误 source 为 storage.backend.sparql。SPARQL_REQUEST_FAILED 是原生明确拒绝，保留 status/body/cause；SPARQL_UNAVAILABLE 是读取 transport/5xx 失败；SPARQL_RESPONSE_INVALID 是非法结果/文档；SPARQL_COMMIT_UNKNOWN 是写结果无法确认，须先核实 dataset，再创建新的后端。callback、草稿任务和 finalizer 的业务失败使用 TRANSACTION_FAILED，原生类型、primary 和原因链保留；已有 contract/协议错误不改身份。

host 默认检测；autoDetect:false 时先 await host.detect()。关闭拒绝新调用，取消活动读取，等待已发提交。dispose() 的主 Promise 保留清理失败；Symbol.asyncDispose 共享清理并只 report。endpoint、Oxigraph Store 与自备客户端由调用方管理，不由插件关闭。Oxigraph 0.4.11 无公开 close/dispose 方法。
hooks 只观察，失败交给 report；干预使用 host pipeline。HTTP 观察不含认证或正文。查询成本包含真实结果字节和客户端剩余操作；图文档整体解析和传输，事务条件文本随 quad/前提数量增长，不承诺数据库计划或推理性能。

Write RDF to a remote SPARQL endpoint or local Oxigraph store and use query chains to read, filter and change quads: data made of a subject, predicate, object and graph. Install the plugin with an HTTP or Oxigraph adapter, construct queries from RDF values, and use `expect` to require specific quads to remain present at commit. A network write with an unknown outcome is not retried automatically.

items: A quote breaks a query because a value was inserted as SPARQL syntax.
Two requests rename the same subject after reading an old value, assuming a predicate can have only one value.
A timed-out HTTP write is retried even though it already committed.
Blank nodes from separate RDF documents become confused because their identities were treated as global.
Terms and template bindings separate RDF data from query syntax. See HTTP reads and writes.
`expect` states which quads must still exist for a conditional commit. See Detect competing updates.
Graph documents use a real RDF parser/writer, with separate blank-node identities for separate imports. See Graph documents and ontology.
Unknown writes are not replayed automatically. Explicit rejection, read failure and unknown commit have distinct errors. See Failures and disposal.

String concatenation and a direct HTTP request leave escaping and commit confirmation to the application. This is shown without execution.

Native SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and UPDATE with term binding.
Accumulate changes and check preconditions in a conditional commit.
Import, export or replace one graph's RDF document.

blocks.text: Raw SPARQL templates express native query statements. A quad has a subject, predicate, object and graph. A ground quad has no blank node or variable. Organization views map logical graphs to separate physical named graphs.

blocks.text: Use Node.js 24 or later. The root does not load Oxigraph's native runtime. `/oxigraph` explicitly selects a real Store; `/http` uses runtime fetch. RDF parsing uses n3 and real RDF/JS declarations.

rows: Install an endpoint; id defaults to sparql.

blocks.text: The backend supplies RDF, SPARQL and native optimistic transactions, with no KV, records, vector, SQL or key locks. Standard RDF accepts named subjects/predicates, named or literal objects, and default/named graphs. Raw SELECT/CONSTRUCT and documents also support blank nodes. RDF-star, document variables and blank standard quads reject. Reasoning belongs to the database.

The endpoint and Store remain with the caller; the host never closes them. Oxigraph 0.4.11's public Store type has no close/dispose method. Release any external connection pool through that client's real API. Host shutdown rejects new calls, cancels active reads and waits for dispatched commits.

Without expect, changes have canonical quad-set semantics: different objects may coexist for one predicate. HTTP deployment must guarantee atomic execution of a conditional Modify and read-after-write visibility on the same dataset; the protocol alone cannot establish those properties. See the usage guide for failures, unknown commits and document limits.

blocks.text: Write two names and delete only Alice.

blocks.code:
import { Store } from 'oxigraph'
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { rdf } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { term } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/rdf'
import { sparqlBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql'
import { oxigraphEndpoint } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql/oxigraph'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [sparqlBackendPlugin({ endpoint: oxigraphEndpoint(new Store()) })]
})
const store = host.backend('sparql')
const quad = {
  subject: term.iri('urn:example:alice'),
  predicate: term.iri('urn:example:name'),
  object: term.literal('Alice'),
  graph: term.defaultGraph
}
await store
  .use(rdf)
  .add([quad, { ...quad, subject: term.iri('urn:example:bob'), object: term.literal('Bob') }])
const selected = store
  .use(rdf)
  .match({ predicate: quad.predicate })
  .where((value) => value.object.value === 'Alice')
console.log(await selected.count())
console.log(await selected.delete())
console.log(await store.use(rdf).match({}).count())

blocks.text: Expected output:

A quad uses named subject/predicate nodes, a named or literal object, and a default/named graph. term.literal accepts language or datatype. Term binding handles escaping. Standard RDF rejects blank nodes and variables.

match(pattern) accepts a subset of quad fields. Its query chain supports where, follow/inverse traversal, orderBy, distinct, skip, limit, pages, aggregates and stream. explain() distinguishes native from client steps; requirePushdown() rejects unsupported client steps before I/O.

delete counts deduplicated canonical quads actually selected and accepted for change. replace(old, new) changes only a selected old quad, returning 0 otherwise. Root calls wait for commit confirmation; counts inside a transaction describe its draft.
Require Alice to remain present before replacing it with Ada. If another transaction removed Alice, this commit conflicts.

blocks.code:
import { Store } from 'oxigraph'
import { createStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-host'
import { rdf } from '@migaia/storage-contract'
import { ConcurrencyPolicy } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/concurrency'
import { term } from '@migaia/storage-host/authoring/rdf'
import { sparqlBackendPlugin } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql'
import { oxigraphEndpoint } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-sparql/oxigraph'

await using host = await createStorageHost({
  plugins: [sparqlBackendPlugin({ endpoint: oxigraphEndpoint(new Store()) })]
})
const store = host.backend('sparql')
const quad = {
  subject: term.iri('urn:example:alice'),
  predicate: term.iri('urn:example:name'),
  object: term.literal('Alice'),
  graph: term.defaultGraph
}
await store.use(rdf).add([quad])
await store
  .tx()
  .concurrency(ConcurrencyPolicy.optimistic({ retries: 1 }))
  .run(async (scope) => {
    scope.use(rdf).expect([quad])
    await scope.use(rdf).delete([quad])
    await scope.use(rdf).add([{ ...quad, object: term.literal('Ada') }])
  })
console.log((await store.use(rdf).match({}).all()).map((value) => value.object.value).join(','))

blocks.text: expect conditions are conjunctions; expectAbsent requires each supplied quad to be absent. Draft changes deduplicate canonical quad identities with last-operation-wins for the same quad. Reads do not automatically form a read set. Concurrent insertions of different objects can both survive; predicates have no single-value guarantee.

ConcurrencyPolicy.optimistic({retries: 1}) retries one real conflict at most. The callback may run again, so perform external side effects after the transaction succeeds. backoffMs defaults to 20. Omitting the policy does not enable automatic optimistic retry. Only optimistic concurrency is supported, without key locks, wait/fail policies or interactive remote transactions.

One conditional DELETE/INSERT WHERE writes user quads and a commit marker, followed by ASK confirmation and marker cleanup. Only a successful Update followed by a successful ASK explicitly finding no marker is a retryable conflict. Unknown Update outcomes, failed ASK and cancellation during confirmation produce SPARQL_COMMIT_UNKNOWN. Later writes on that backend stop and are not replayed. Marker cleanup failures are reported after user data has committed.

A transaction may execute one raw update body only when its endpoint supplies atomicUpdate. It cannot mix RDF operations/preconditions or a second raw body. Oxigraph provides one native Store.update; httpEndpoint does not provide this capability and rejects before sending a write. Transaction raw templates expose update only, without select/ask/construct.

Start a real service that supports SPARQL Query and Update. The defaults use the `storage` dataset on local port 3030. For other addresses, set `SPARQL_QUERY_URL`, `SPARQL_UPDATE_URL` and `SPARQL_GRAPH_STORE_URL` to the same dataset; the Graph Store URL is used for graph document operations. This inserts data and reads it with ASK; the data remains in the service.

blocks.code: true

blocks.text: queryUrl/updateUrl are required; graphStoreUrl is needed only for graph-document features. URLs must be absolute HTTP(S) without embedded credentials. Optional auth is exactly `{basic: {user, password}}` or `{bearer}`. Mutations are sent once without redirect following. Reads retain fetch behavior. Graph Store HEAD404 returns false; GET404 rejects. Authentication headers are not diagnostic data.

The root raw tag supports select, ask, construct and update. A normal string is data, not syntax; bind RDF terms as template values. Raw SELECT/CONSTRUCT also support blank nodes scoped to one response.

Deployment must guarantee atomic execution of one conditional Modify and read-after-write visibility on the same dataset. Native paths cover Fuseki 6.2.0 and Oxigraph 0.4.11; other deployments must supply equivalent guarantees. An HTTP protocol is not itself a database transaction.
Write a graph, export it and import with replace. Every Feature used here is installed in this example.
